group_evidence.why_grouped: explicit agent-stated uncertainty: 'artifact38-layered-model-second-irreducible-transformation-phi' POSSIBLY relates to 'lossy-semantic-projection-blocked-by-qualify' (batch B0056). Note: A formal registry-style meta-review (artifact 38, dated 2026-09-01) of the same mathematical_ideas_that_can_be_implemented corpus this batch reads directly (Kallenberg/Shum/Dretske/Cover-Thomas/Audi/Plato-White/Davidson/DEL/Bayesian-Epistemology-Vol-2), cross-referencing it against the separate phase_measure_theory/knowledgeos_kernel research-step numbering (steps 17,19,25,26,29,34,37). Registers: N-Q2, a 'strongest evidence class' finding that KnowledgeOS/Dretske/Kallenberg form a three-way NEGATIVE convergence that probability is not knowledge and no scalar probability defines knowledge, matching and externally confirming the corpus's own 2026-08-25 self-refutation ('the biggest overclaim: knowledge is conditional expectation'; 'projection=measure is probably not the right primitive'), sharpened by noting conditional expectation is optimal only under an undeclared loss function. Finds the layered model X->Y_t->E_t->F_t->Pi_t->K_t structurally INSTANTIATES two of the reviewer's own prior corrections: step-17's F_t!=Knowledge_t (join-semilattice-overclaim traced to a filtration/state conflation) and step-37's withdrawal of a five-way-typing requirement in favor of a structured object where only some components have measure-theoretic representation (Pi_t is exactly that component). Registers G-109: a SECOND undefined transformation Phi: Pi_t -> K_t (probabilistic representation to epistemic state), explicitly distinct from and must-not-be-merged-with the pre-existing G1 gap (Qualify: observation to evidence, named/typed/no body) -- different carriers, different pipeline positions; argues Phi must exist and cannot be trivial precisely because 'probability is not knowledge' is a three-way negative convergence, so SOMETHING non-trivial must carry Pi_t to K_t. Registers D-Q4: the layered model's Gap B (undefined atomicity/independence criterion for dimensions d_i) refines a prior open question M-Q8, showing a previously-invoked relevance predicate ('258.21's Relevant(p)') supplies relevance but NOT atomicity/independence -- a property can be relevant while still decomposable, so the earlier routing of dimension-membership through Relevant(p) was necessary but not sufficient. Registers G-110: Pi (capital Pi) now carries THREE distinct corpus readings -- provenance (id=H(P,e,c,t,Pi); Lineage=Pi o R_der*; a pending Decision 3 on Pi's equivalence-class membership), Policy (the 8-primitive table's G-102), and (newly, from this layered model) probabilistic representation of uncertainty -- flagged as the corpus's 'fourteenth collision' and documentary-urgent since the layered model's Pi_t is load-bearing (it is what Phi maps from). Registers constraint C21: F_t != Pi_t != K_t as three distinct layers (information structure / probabilistic representation / epistemic state), explicitly noting still ZERO new primitives and ZERO new canonical relations added by this whole reviewed batch of files. Explicitly credits the reviewed source material's own discipline (repeated refusal to declare victory: 'I would not say we have filled it completely'; 'K_t is still not formally solved') as matching a discipline previously found in the corpus's separate Gita-lane synthesis, now recurring in a mathematical lane. Explicit non-licensing statement: the layered model is NOT adopted, G-109 is not G1 and must not be folded into it, Determination is re-raised not re-instated, and 21 of the 25 renamed source files in the directory were at review time read only by heading (Shum, Cover & Thomas, Audi, Plato, Davidson, DEL still 'unexamined' by this reviewer at artifact-38 time).

a_rows_sample.anchor: K_t is the smallest possible unit of knowledge about an observation at time t.
a_rows_sample.statement: Proposes, and repeatedly re-affirms as a 'candidate definition, not yet formally proven', K_t(o) = the smallest epistemically meaningful unit of knowledge about observation o at time t, explicitly warning against prematurely identifying K_t with a data point, a claim, or the existing six-tuple (entity/property/context/relation/time/authority) -- those may become representations of K_t, not K_t itself, restated as the invariant 'Representation != Knowledge Identity'.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Can K_t be decomposed into smaller knowledge units without losing the knowledge about the observation? If yes, it wasn't minimal. If no, we have a candidate minimal knowledge unit.
a_rows_sample.statement: Proposes an operational minimality criterion for K_t via a decomposition test (K_t -> {K_t,1, K_t,2, ...}): if the decomposition preserves all knowledge about the observation, the original unit was not minimal; if no such decomposition exists, it is a candidate minimal unit -- offered as a way to formalize 'smallest' without prematurely fixing K_t's internal structure.

a_rows_sample.anchor: A sentence is a linguistic representation that may contain one or more K_t units. ... the number of sentences gives us a possible dimensional view, but not necessarily the true number of dimensions.
a_rows_sample.statement: Using a repeated Nexus-server worked example (RHEL 9.8, 8 vCPU, port 8081, etc. as ten atomic statements), argues a sentence is not necessarily one K_t unit -- e.g. 'has 8 vCPUs and 31 GB RAM' contains two atomic units -- and that an observation's true dimensionality is not bounded by however many sentences currently describe it (K_t(O) subset-of all potentially observable aspects of O; 'Knowledge at t != the complete observation'); new sentences discovered later add new dimensions (K_t^11), and a corrected statement changes an existing dimension's value rather than necessarily creating a new one.

a_rows_sample.anchor: WorldState_t -> Observation_t^A -> InformationState_t^A -> EpistemicState_t^A -> KnowledgeAttribution, with history H_{<=t} preserved. It then proposes K_t^{A,R} as a time-indexed knowledge attribution, dependent on participant A, extraction regime R.
a_rows_sample.statement: Reading an unread-in-this-batch corpus document, reports its chain WorldState_t -> Observation_t^A -> InformationState_t^A -> EpistemicState_t^A -> KnowledgeAttribution (with preserved history H_{<=t}) and its participant/regime-relative K_t^{A,R}; explicitly distinguishes this from the dialogue's own new atomic-K_t hypothesis, treating the latter as a possible FURTHER refinement (one measurable statement per observation dimension) rather than something the attached document already established, and notes the document's own probability treatment P(K_t^A|F_t^A) as extraction-uncertainty, explicitly distinct from Knowledge itself.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Q = domain of possible items; K subset-of Q = a particular knowledge state; script-K = space/family of possible states; probability (Q, script-K, p). The crucial distinction is: script-K != K_t != P(K_t | O_{<=t}).
a_rows_sample.statement: Reports a Knowledge Space Theory (KST) formalism (Q as domain of possible items, K as a particular state, script-K as the family of possible states, with probability attached as (Q,script-K,p)) as external confirmation that a knowledge-space, a particular state, and a probability distribution over states are three genuinely different objects; notes KST's own K_t is a learner-capability state (a different, narrower sense than the dialogue's broader KnowledgeOS K_t), and that the dialogue's atomic-unit idea asks a question KST does not answer: what is the state/value of each individual knowledge unit within a state.

a_rows_sample.anchor: P(k_i | E) is the epistemic confidence/degree of support for proposition k_i, given the available evidence. ... k_i != P(k_i)
a_rows_sample.statement: Repeatedly insists that probability attached to a knowledge unit must be given a precise referent -- distinguishing P(claim is true), P(claim is supported by available evidence), P(the measurement/extraction is correct), and P(claim belongs to K_t) as not necessarily the same quantity, and stating k_i != P(k_i): the knowledge unit itself is not identical to its probability. Also proposes that not every claim's epistemic measure need be a probability -- it could be categorical status, an interval, a confidence level, measurement uncertainty, or logical entailment strength -- warning against forcing every kind of knowledge into probability merely because probability is mathematically convenient.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Observation -> Atomic propositions -> Evidence -> Measured epistemic state -> Ideal/reference state -> distance -> knowledge gap. This potentially connects several previously separate strands: Phase 1 ... Phase 2 ... KST ... Pritchard ... Zero ... Knower ... Evidence ... Kernel
a_rows_sample.statement: Proposes a 'candidate unifying structure, not yet a completed theory': Observation -> Atomic propositions -> Evidence -> Measured epistemic state -> Ideal/reference state -> distance -> knowledge gap, claimed to potentially connect the corpus's Phase-1 (knowledge as relationship/justification/state evolution), Phase-2 (Knowledge Space/participant/time/projection), KST (Q, script-K, K_t, p), Pritchard's belief-counts-as-knowledge conditions, Zero, Knower-ownership, Evidence/determination, and Kernel-as-substrate strands, while explicitly warning against collapsing these prematurely.

a_rows_sample.anchor: EpistemicState = Acquisition x Support x Resolution x Validity
a_rows_sample.statement: Reports a multidimensional EpistemicState formulation (Acquisition x Support x Resolution x Validity) as already-derived corpus material supporting the general direction of a non-monolithic, multi-axis knowledge state, alongside a stated distinction chain Knowledge!=Reality, Observation!=Knowledge, Dimension!=Statement, Dimension!=Value, Guidance!=Decision, Zero!=Knowledge, Parsing!=Knowledge, Parsing!=Dimension-Discovery.

a_rows_sample.anchor: What is the minimum structure of k_t such that the entire KnowledgeOS theory — evidence, probability, context, identity, Zero, evolution, proposal, decision and action — can be derived without adding arbitrary architectural assumptions?
a_rows_sample.statement: Closes the file's line of inquiry with an explicit unresolved research question: what is the minimal structure of the atomic knowledge unit k_t from which the rest of the theory (evidence, probability, context, identity, Zero, evolution, proposal, decision, action) could be derived without arbitrary additional architectural assumptions -- stated as the next major research question rather than answered.

a_rows_sample.anchor: A sentence is not automatically a knowledge dimension merely because it is syntactically a sentence. ... independent knowledge-bearing statement -> candidate dimension
a_rows_sample.statement: Restates the minimal-knowledge-unit hypothesis k_t(O) (smallest independently meaningful unit of knowledge about an observation at t) with the qualification that sentence != dimension automatically -- semantic independence of a statement must be established before it counts as a candidate dimension; and states K_t(O) is necessarily partial, since K_t(O) subset-of D(O), the full (possibly unbounded) dimension set of the observation.

a_rows_sample.anchor: k_i = (O, d_i, v_i, t, E_i, p_i, q_i)
a_rows_sample.statement: Extends the atomic knowledge claim to a seven-field tuple k_i=(O,d_i,v_i,t,E_i,p_i,q_i) -- observation, semantic dimension, claimed value, time, evidence/information source, epistemic probability, and an explicit information-sufficiency/support status q_i -- with K_t(O)={k_1,...,k_n} as the resulting knowledge state, and reiterates that dimensionality is representation-relative rather than an intrinsic finite property of the object (a sentence maps to one or more atomic claims, not one-to-one).

a_rows_sample.anchor: K_t should not be identified with a Kripke model or possible-world set. Status: research conclusion / compatibility constraint, not yet kernel theorem.
a_rows_sample.statement: Confirms the DEL document's rejection of K_t as a Kripke pointed model (M,w) strengthens (without proving) the corpus's independently-developed atomic-tuple direction k_i=(O,d_i,v_i,t,E_i,C_i,p_i,q_i); explicitly records the possible-worlds rejection as a research conclusion/compatibility constraint, not a kernel theorem.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The missing step is: $$(O,E_{\le t},A,G,EC)\;\longrightarrow\;K_t(O)$$ ... The file itself almost explicitly states this as the unanswered operation \(\mathcal M\): $$\mathcal M:(O,E_{\le t},A,G,EC)\rightarrow K_t(O)$$
a_rows_sample.statement: Identifies the central missing derivation in the reviewed K_t/observation research as the unanswered operation M:(O, E_{<=t}, A, G, EC) -> K_t(O) -- the document being reviewed 'repeatedly approaches it but never actually derives it' -- where O is observation, E_{<=t} is evidence up to time t, A is the Knower/agent, G is goal, and EC is the epistemic contract.

a_rows_sample.anchor:
The document currently jumps: $$Oightarrow k_1,\ldots,k_nightarrow K_t$$ But **where do \(k_1,\ldots,k_n\) come from?** ... dimension \(
eq\) statement \(
eq\) knowledge atom \(
eq\) value ... but does not provide the transformation between them.
a_rows_sample.statement: Corrects/sharpens the atomic-knowledge-unit hypothesis by pointing out that reviewed prior work jumps directly from an observation O to a set of atoms k_1..k_n without deriving them, despite itself distinguishing dimension != statement != knowledge atom != value; the transformation producing the atoms from an observation is never actually supplied.

a_rows_sample.anchor: $$O\overset{\mathcal D}{\longrightarrow}\{d_i\}\overset{\mathcal P}{\longrightarrow}\{q_i\}\overset{\mathcal E}{\longrightarrow}\{s_{i,t}\}\overset{\mathcal A}{\longrightarrow}K_t$$ where \(O\) = observation; \(d_i\) = observable/aspect dimension; \(q_i\) = atomic proposition ...; \(s_{i,t}\) = epistemic state/value ...; \(K_t\) = resulting knowledge state.
a_rows_sample.statement: Proposes decomposing the missing K_t-construction derivation into a four-operator pipeline: D (observation to dimensions {d_i}), P (dimensions to atomic propositions {q_i}), E (propositions to epistemic-state values {s_i,t}), and A (values aggregated to K_t) -- named as the candidate missing derivation, with a worked Nexus-server example (RHEL 9.8, 8 vCPU, 31GB RAM, port 8081, etc. -> candidate atoms k_i) illustrating that no mathematical operation currently justifies which atoms are 'correct'.

a_rows_sample.anchor: $$K_t=\operatorname{Aggregate}(k_{1,t},\ldots,k_{n,t})$$ and we must determine whether that aggregation is: a set, vector, graph, distribution, state space, or something else. That is explicitly still open in the document.
a_rows_sample.statement: Names a second missing derivation: the aggregation of individual knowledge atoms {k_i,t} into the knowledge state K_t, with the mathematical type of the aggregate (set/vector/graph/distribution/state-space/other) left explicitly open.

a_rows_sample.anchor: I think the previous research was looking for the missing piece **one level too late**. We kept asking: What is \(D(K_t,I_t)\)? But before that, we need: How is \(K_t\) generated? And before that: How is an observation transformed into atomic knowledge propositions?
a_rows_sample.statement: Argues the research programme has been searching for the missing piece at the wrong level: the priority order of open questions should be (1) how is an observation transformed into atomic knowledge propositions, before (2) how is K_t generated from those atoms, before (3) what is the comparison function D(K_t,I_t) -- reordering research priority away from the distance function toward the earlier construction steps.

a_rows_sample.anchor: $$R_t\overset{\operatorname{Obs}_A}{\longrightarrow}O_t^A$$ where \(R_t\) is the world/reality state and \(O_t^A\) is what participant \(A\) can observe. ... consistent with the document's existing ... projection $$\Pi_A:\mathcal W\rightarrow\mathcal E_A$$ but the document explicitly treats that projection as a hypothesis rather than an established theory.
a_rows_sample.statement: Identifies an even deeper missing derivation than K_t-construction: the theory currently starts with observation O as given, but a genuinely epistemological theory must also derive Reality -> Observation, i.e. R_t --Obs_A--> O_t^A (world/reality state to what a specific participant A can observe), consistent with but more explicit than the document's existing (hypothesis-only) projection Pi_A: W -> E_A.

a_rows_sample.anchor: **The Knowledge-State Construction Derivation** $$R_t\rightarrow O_t^A\rightarrow Q_t^A\rightarrow E_t^A\rightarrow K_t^A$$ followed by: $$(A,G,EC)\rightarrow I_t^A\rightarrow Z_t^A\rightarrow\text{investigation/action}\rightarrow K_{t+1}^A$$ ... it has not derived the **transformations between the nodes**.
a_rows_sample.statement: Names and consolidates the overall missing derivation as 'The Knowledge-State Construction Derivation': R_t -> O_t^A -> Q_t^A -> E_t^A -> K_t^A, followed by (A,G,EC) -> I_t^A -> Z_t^A -> investigation/action -> K_{t+1}^A; concludes the prior work has developed almost all the nodes of this pipeline but never derived the transformations connecting them, and that the most important missing function is the decomposition of M:(O,E_{<=t},A,G,EC) -> K_t into formally justified sub-operations.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Knowledge is a stateful relationship between an observation, a knower, evidence, context, purpose, and what is currently warranted to be asserted about that observation. ... K_t = KnowledgeState(O,S,E,C,G,t)
b_rows_sample.statement: Foundational proposition of the synthesis: Knowledge is a stateful relationship (not a bare proposition), formalized as K_t = KnowledgeState(O,S,E,C,G,t) over observation O, epistemic subject/knower S, evidence E, context C, goal/purpose G and time t; the same observation can have different knowledge states depending on these parameters.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Knowledge can be: expanded, refined, revised, weakened, contradicted, retracted, superseded. Thus knowledge evolution is not equivalent to information accumulation.
b_rows_sample.statement: States knowledge is temporal (K_t1 != K_t2) but explicitly non-monotonic: K_{t+1} is not necessarily a superset of K_t (a probability can drop from 0.95 to 0.20 after new evidence), so knowledge evolution admits expansion, refinement, revision, weakening, contradiction, retraction and supersession, and must not be equated with mere information accumulation.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Knowledge units may carry an epistemically appropriate measure; probability is one important class of such measures. This avoids turning the entire theory into an unjustified probabilistic ontology.
b_rows_sample.statement: States knowledge units may be represented by categorical states, logical entailment, intervals, measurements, confidence, evidence strength, or qualitative epistemic status, with probability as only one class of appropriate measure -- an explicit guard against defaulting the whole theory to a probabilistic ontology.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Extraction retrieves material. Determination establishes what that material warrants asserting. ... The extraction mechanism must not silently become the authority that determines truth.
b_rows_sample.statement: Restates Extraction != Determination as one of the strongest candidate invariants, with a pipeline Observation -> Evidence -> Extraction -> Determination -> Knowledge Claim, and the explicit constraint that extraction must never silently become the authority determining truth.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Knower owns the frame ... KnowledgeOS can: observe, extract, calculate, compare, propose, but cannot silently redefine the epistemic purpose of the knower.
b_rows_sample.statement: Restates 'Knower owns the frame' as one of the strongest cross-regime findings, with the practical constraint that KnowledgeOS may observe/extract/calculate/compare/propose but must never silently redefine the Knower's epistemic purpose.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Residual -> Candidate Knowledge. This is a discovery mechanism rather than a primitive definition of knowledge.
b_rows_sample.statement: States that a model residual (Observed-Expected) should not automatically be classified as error -- it may contain previously unexplained structure and should be treated as candidate knowledge, a discovery mechanism rather than a primitive definition; and separately states aggregation ({k_1,...,k_n} -> k') is itself a knowledge transformation that can expose structure, not assumed to be universally lossless or beneficial.

b_rows_sample.anchor: R(A,B) != R(B,A) unless symmetry is independently established.
b_rows_sample.statement: States relations (evidence, inference, conditioning, causation, determination, proposal, decision) are directional by default: R(A,B) != R(B,A) unless symmetry is independently established for that relation.

b_rows_sample.anchor: If we reduce everything to the minimum, I think the theory currently has five fundamental layers: O -> K_t -> K_t^* -> Delta_t -> K_{t+1}
b_rows_sample.statement: Proposes a minimal five-layer core (O: what is observed; K_t: what is currently warranted to be known; K_t*: what would be sufficient for the purpose; Delta_t: the discrepancy between actual and required knowledge; K_{t+1}: the state after epistemic evolution) around which everything else -- evidence, probability, context, identity, Zero, Lord, Sarathi, governance -- is said to operate.

b_rows_sample.anchor: we do not yet have sufficient evidence to claim: 1. that k_t has a universally fixed mathematical tuple; ... 10. that one of the competing models is the final model.
b_rows_sample.statement: Explicit ten-item list of claims NOT yet supported by evidence: a universally fixed mathematical tuple for k_t; every sentence being a knowledge dimension; every knowledge value being a probability; Knowledge Space being infinite; Knowledge Space having a particular topology; the Kernel necessarily containing eight primitives; Identity necessarily being one particular 6-tuple; Zero being mathematically equivalent to any philosophical concept; Atman being computationally represented by KnowledgeOS; and any one competing model being the final model.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Knowledge is a temporally situated, context-dependent, evidence-grounded state of warranted understanding about an observation, constituted by minimal knowledge units and evaluated relative to a purpose-defined ideal state. ... KnowledgeOS should not primarily be a repository of propositions. It sho
b_rows_sample.statement: Closing central philosophical statement and its architectural consequence, compressing the 29-section synthesis: Knowledge as a temporally situated, context-dependent, evidence-grounded state of warranted understanding, constituted by minimal knowledge units and evaluated against a purpose-defined ideal state, with the corollary that KnowledgeOS's role is representing/measuring/comparing/validating/evolving knowledge states rather than storing propositions; explicitly caveats that a separate attached 'seven-work synthesis' contributes subordinate pieces (generation, relational identity, context, uncertainty, aggregation, residuals, directional relations) that remain secondary until more rigorously established.

a_notations: k_t = smallest independently evaluable knowledge claim about an observation
a_aliases: Kt smallest unit of knowledge about an observation

group_evidence.why_grouped: explicit agent-stated uncertainty: 'knowledge-theory-integrated-research-model-29-sections' POSSIBLY relates to 'atomic-knowledge-unit-kt-observation-hypothesis' (batch B0056). Note: A 29-section consolidated 'research-level theory' document (S2310) synthesizing the K_t/Ideal-State/Zero/Lord/Sarathi hypotheses developed across the preceding dialogue (S2309) into one organized statement: K_t=KnowledgeState(O,S,E,C,G,t); a minimal knowledge unit k_t(O); knowledge as partial/temporal/non-monotonically-evolving; K_t* as a Knower-defined sufficiency (not absolute truth) Ideal State; Delta_t=D(K_t,K_t*) as knowledge discrepancy; Zero refined to mean K_t|=EC(G,C) rather than completeness; a five-layer core reduction O->K_t->K_t*->Delta_t->K_{t+1}; six provisional invariants of differing evidentiary strength; and an explicit ten-item list of claims NOT yet supported. Explicitly labelled research-level, not final architecture. Possibly the same evolving hypothesis thread as S2309's atomic-knowledge-unit-kt-observation-hypothesis (a direct continuation), possibly a distinct consolidation artifact -- not resolved by this batch.

a_rows_sample.anchor: docs/knowledge/schema/authorities.yaml types authority as a five-rank trust grade of a document ... That is a property of an ARTIFACT, not of an ACTOR. ... Verdict: PARTIALLY VERIFIED. Three of four senses separated. Recorded as TG-07.
a_rows_sample.statement: Authority carries four senses (competence Auth(a,r,c,p); 7-ary f(Actor,Role,...); actor-standing rank; and the EKP's five-rank artifact trust-grade authoritative/derived/generated/historical/provisional); a prior audit mapped the artifact-trust-grade sense onto 'Standing' (an actor attribute), which is a category error since artifact-trust-grade and actor-standing have different subjects of predication; recorded as remaining gap TG-07.

group_evidence.why_grouped: explicit agent-stated uncertainty: 'authority-vs-authorization-conflation' POSSIBLY relates to 'authority-overload' (batch B0041). Note: Authority (a standing, time-indexed relation) and Authorization (a dated act) are explicitly distinguished by Step 187 §187.1 but then used interchangeably from Step 190 onward, despite Authority being time-indexed while an authorization act is a point event that must be separately recorded.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Evolution <-> KM update; Correction/Refutation <-> AGM revision. This is a genuine result and the corpus does not know it.
a_rows_sample.statement: Finds RevisionType::Evolution (the corpus's 'the system really changed from 3.69 to 3.70', boxed 'Evolution is not an error') is exactly Katsuno-Mendelzon's motivating case for UPDATE (the world changed, the old belief was correct then), while Correction/Refutation match AGM REVISION (new information about a static world); notes AGM is mentioned only 5 times across 564 corpus files and the KM revision/update distinction appears nowhere, so the corpus independently re-derived, from a version-number example, a distinction belief-revision literature has held since 1991 -- and split it six ways where KM splits two.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The credibility set C is exactly Policy x Authority. ... C gates input acceptance; Policy+Authority gate admission; both leave the prior state unchanged on rejection.
a_rows_sample.statement: Finds the corpus's governed admission (Closure-03: LLM proposes, Lord evaluates, Governance authorizes; a proposal may be rejected) is exactly credibility-limited (non-prioritized) revision K⊛phi = K*phi if phi in C, else K, with the credibility set C identified structure-preservingly as Policy x Authority.

a_rows_sample.anchor: H monotone AND K'=Derive(H') non-monotone === JTMS
a_rows_sample.statement: Finds the corpus's boxed Revision = EventAddition + StateReDerivation (H'=H union {E_revision}, K'=Derive(H',Omega,EC,M)) is exactly a Doyle-style JTMS: the corpus's own Fagin extraction already states 'knowledge history is monotonic in preservation; knowledge state is not necessarily monotonic in projection', which is the JTMS invariant verbatim (justification store grows monotonically, derived belief set is non-monotone).

a_rows_sample.anchor: AGM does not apply to A as stated. Hansson's base revision does. ... importing AGM results would import theorems that are false of A.
a_rows_sample.statement: Structural incompatibility: AGM's carrier K=Cn(K) is deductively closed, but the corpus's assertion set A (measured: zero occurrences of a consequence operator Cn) is a finite set of asserted items with identity/provenance/evidence links, i.e. a Hansson belief BASE, not a belief SET; since base contraction and AGM contraction on Cn(B) are provably inequivalent, naively importing AGM theorems would import claims false of A.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Two of the corpus's six revision types are changes to the interpretation function, which AGM cannot express. ... This is the largest single gap found in this document, and it runs against the external theory rather than against KnowledgeOS.
a_rows_sample.statement: Decisive finding: AGM holds the language L and its interpretation fixed -- every operator maps L-sentences to L-sentences, with no operator for changing what sentences MEAN -- but the corpus's Reinterpretation ('the original observation was valid, but we interpreted it incorrectly', a change in Evidence(O,P,C,R)'s rule R) and ModelRevision ('reasonable under the old model, but the model itself was subsequently changed', a change in M within Derive(H,Omega,EC,M)) are both first-class corpus revision types with no AGM counterpart at all; framed as the corpus formalizing something AGM chose to hold constant, i.e. the gap runs against the external theory, not against KnowledgeOS.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Sigma cong {0,1}^2 is a product, not an order. Supported (1,0) and Refuted (0,1) are incomparable ... Sigma cannot be an entrenchment ordering.
a_rows_sample.statement: Refutes mapping Sigma onto an AGM entrenchment ordering: AGM entrenchment <= is a total, transitive preorder satisfying dominance and minimality, but the corpus's Sigma (isomorphic to {0,1}^2, the Supported/Refuted product) is a product structure, not an order -- Supported(1,0) and Refuted(0,1) are incomparable, neither more entrenched than the other. Offers, only as a stated-not-adopted hypothesis (BR-H4), a lattice ordering (0,0)<={(1,0),(0,1)}<=(1,1) under set inclusion on the support set, explicitly noting this would order informativeness, not resistance-to-retraction, and the corpus asserts no such order.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Retraction — "the source withdraws its support" — is not expressible in AGM, because AGM beliefs have no sources.
a_rows_sample.statement: Notes AGM models a single agent's single belief set at one time with no source identifiers, while KnowledgeOS carries provenance, multiple sources, authority and an inquiry register; consequently RevisionType::Retraction (a source withdrawing its support) cannot be expressed in AGM at all and requires base revision augmented with justifications (i.e. JTMS).

a_rows_sample.anchor: interpretation change | sources/provenance on beliefs | an authority predicate | a requirement set | a goal state | paraconsistent tolerance ... a consequence operator Cn | an entrenchment/plausibility order | a contraction operator
a_rows_sample.statement: Lists missing primitives on the belief-revision side needed to host KnowledgeOS (interpretation change for Reinterpretation/ModelRevision; sources/provenance on beliefs for Retraction; an authority predicate for governed admission; a requirement set for Zero; a goal state for Ideal State; paraconsistent tolerance for Conflict, since AGM's K*5 Consistency postulate forbids it) and on the KnowledgeOS side needed to host belief revision (a consequence operator Cn, currently 0 occurrences, without which 'belief set' is undefined; an entrenchment/plausibility order, since nothing currently orders assertions by retractability; a contraction operator, since Retraction is named as a RevisionType but not defined as an operator, and its membership in the operator-registry O_core is unratified).

a_rows_sample.anchor: BR-H1 ... BR-H2 ... BR-H3 ... BR-H4 ... BR-H5 ... BR-H6
a_rows_sample.statement: States six falsifiable hypotheses with named falsifiers: BR-H1 (Evolution<->KM-update and Correction/Refutation<->AGM-revision is exact in role); BR-H2 (governed admission satisfies credibility-limited-revision postulates with C=Policy x Authority, falsified by a rejected proposal that still changes A); BR-H3 (Revision=EventAddition+StateReDerivation satisfies the JTMS invariant, falsified by a RevisionType that removes an event from H); BR-H4 (Sigma admits no total entrenchment order consistent with corpus operations); BR-H5 (Reinterpretation/ModelRevision are not definable as any AGM/KM operator composition over a fixed L); BR-H6 (because Cn is absent, no AGM theorem transfers to A unmodified, falsified by exhibiting one that holds of A for a non-trivial reason).

a_rows_sample.anchor: THE CLOSEST OF THE FIVE — and the corpus is ahead of the framework on one axis ... the substrate the corpus describes is a justification store, and that is a JTMS.
a_rows_sample.statement: Final verdict: belief revision is 'the closest of the five' external theories compared in this series, with four exact correspondences (more than any other), a resolvable carrier mismatch (move from AGM to base revision), and one axis (Reinterpretation/ModelRevision) where KnowledgeOS is ahead of the external framework rather than under-formalized; endorses and sharpens the corpus's own Gardenfors-derived self-description ('epistemic states and their dynamics as the primary modelling problem', Kernel=preservation substrate) into 'the substrate the corpus describes is a justification store, and that is a JTMS.'

a_rows_sample.anchor: Implement Epistemic Change as multiple mechanisms ... reject a single undifferentiated K_{t+1}=delta(K_t,x). Instead ... Revision != Contraction != Update ... revision concerns correcting an epistemic state regarding a static world, whereas update concerns becoming current after the world itself changes.
a_rows_sample.statement: FR-5 (section 6): rejects a single undifferentiated transition K_{t+1}=delta(K_t,x); requires distinguishing Revision(K_t,e)->K_{t+1} (correction/reorganization of a static-world epistemic state), Contraction(K_t,p)->K_{t+1} (withdrawal of a commitment), and Update(K_t,Delta W)->K_{t+1} (the represented world changed) as semantic categories (not necessarily three implementation services), following the Handbook's revision-vs-update distinction.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Implement 'revision is constrained, not uniquely determined' ... Constraints(delta) not=> Unique(delta) ... Semantic invariants constrain admissible operations but do not, by themselves, select a unique operation unless an additional selection criterion is established. This principle applies beyond revision: equality, evaluation, contradiction, aggregation, transition, policy semantics.
a_rows_sample.statement: Section 11 (general methodological principle): AGM-style material shows desirable rationality constraints do not determine a unique revision operator (Constraints(delta) does not imply Unique(delta)); generalized as 'semantic invariants constrain admissible operations but do not, by themselves, select a unique operation unless an additional selection criterion is established', explicitly extended beyond revision to equality, evaluation, contradiction, aggregation, transition, and policy semantics. Judged compatible with existing kernel discipline.

a_rows_sample.anchor: What I would NOT implement ... AGM as KnowledgeOS revision ... Event Calculus as delta ... Description Logic as KnowledgeOS ontology ... FDE as KnowledgeOS evaluation. Already experimentally rejected as sufficient ... Four-valued knowledge. Still insufficient ... Closed-world assumption. Explicitly rejected ... Query = Sat. Rejected ... TELL = requirement insertion. Rejected ... Model uniqueness = Determination. Not yet ... Distributed knowledge logic = KnowledgeOS social ontology. Not yet ... N_eff. Still off the critical path.
a_rows_sample.statement: Section 18, an eleven-item explicit non-adoption list, each rejecting an over-strong external-theory identification even where the same Handbook material motivates the underlying distinction: AGM as the revision theory, Event Calculus as delta, Description Logic as ontology (subsumption/model-existence/instance-checking/open-world used only as research inputs), FDE as evaluation (already experimentally rejected), four-valued knowledge, closed-world assumption, Query=Sat, TELL=requirement-insertion, ModelUniqueness=Determination, distributed-knowledge-logic=social-ontology, and N_eff -- all explicitly rejected or deferred as established KnowledgeOS semantics.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Part 2: Knowledge Evolution and Change -- FR-5 Epistemic Change Typing [STRONG], FR-6 Non-Monotonic Evolution [STRONG], FR-8 Derivation Lineage [STRONG CANDIDATE]
a_rows_sample.statement: Part 2 groups FR-5, FR-6 and (unusually, ahead of the Representation part) FR-8 under Knowledge Evolution and Change: FR-5 Revision != Contraction != Update, each with a distinct signature (Revision(K_t,e), Contract(K_t,p), Update(K_t,DeltaW)); FR-6 K_t not-subseteq K_{t+1} permitted, not itself indicating failure; FR-8 Support(q)={p, p->q,...} as DerivationLineage(q), status STRONG CANDIDATE pending one validation pass.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Part 5: What Is NOT Implemented -- AGM as KnowledgeOS revision: Use distinctions only ... FDE as KnowledgeOS evaluation: Experimentally rejected ... N_eff: Off critical path
a_rows_sample.statement: Part 5 formalizes the non-adoption list as an 11-row table (item, reason): AGM as revision (use distinctions only), Event Calculus as delta (research input only), Description Logic as ontology (research input only), FDE as evaluation (experimentally rejected), four-valued knowledge (insufficient), closed-world assumption (explicitly rejected), Query=Sat (rejected), TELL=requirement-insertion (rejected), Model-uniqueness=Determination (not yet), Distributed knowledge logic (not yet), N_eff (off critical path).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Two places where KnowledgeOS exceeds the external theory: Reinterpretation and ModelRevision -- AGM/KM hold the language fixed; two of the corpus's six revision types change the interpretation function. No operator exists in the framework. Determination/Decision/Action -- a three-way split where Wald has two, and the extra cut is the one governance needs.
a_rows_sample.statement: Names two places where KnowledgeOS's own formalization exceeds the compared external theory rather than merely matching or falling short of it: two of the corpus's six revision types (Reinterpretation, ModelRevision) change the interpretation function itself, something AGM/KM hold fixed and have no operator to express; and the corpus's three-way Determination/Decision/Action split adds a cut beyond Wald's two-way decision-theoretic split, specifically the cut that governance needs.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Zero <-> an antichain of unsatisfied requirements in a finite lattice — an ORDER, not a NUMBER
b_rows_sample.statement: Finds Zero(K,G,EC) (evaluated over a finite requirement set with sufficiency rules Gamma, returning one of ten statuses per requirement, boxed 'Zero != simple subtraction') fits Shannon's measure-free structural layer: requirements generate a finite meet-semilattice under partition refinement, and Zero is the set of requirements not yet in the satisfied down-set -- an antichain in a lattice, an ORDER rather than a NUMBER; the corpus's own boxed rejection of simple subtraction is exactly the statement that this lattice is not a measure, stated without the vocabulary.

b_rows_sample.anchor: |gaps(A)| = |gaps(B)| = 2, yet A != B as work plans — any count/scalar conflates them. That is a demonstration that Zero is not a cardinality, i.e. not a measure.
b_rows_sample.statement: Reports an executed corroboration from zero_reference.py: two work plans A and B have equal gap-counts (|gaps(A)|=|gaps(B)|=2) yet are different work plans, so any scalar/cardinality summary of Zero conflates them -- an independent demonstration (found by running code, not by information-theoretic argument) that Zero cannot be a cardinality/measure, agreeing with the information-theory finding.

b_rows_sample.anchor: H, I, D_KL are all functionals of a probability distribution. (Omega,F,P) as a triple: 0 occurrences in both lanes; T-3 rules probability not required. Shannon's quantitative layer is unavailable to KnowledgeOS by the same ruling that declined probability.
b_rows_sample.statement: Decisive incompatibility: Shannon entropy, mutual information and KL-divergence are all functionals of a declared probability distribution (Omega,F,P), which has zero occurrences in the corpus and was explicitly ruled unnecessary by Step 282's T-3; therefore the entire Shannon quantitative layer is unavailable to KnowledgeOS by the same ruling that declined probability, leaving only the measure-free lattice layer (which supports refinement/coverage/gap structure but no number).

b_rows_sample.anchor: entropy appears 87 times in the corpus, 0 ratified. ... every one of those 87 uses is either (a) metaphorical, (b) about an external regime not adopted, or (c) an error.
b_rows_sample.statement: Measures 87 corpus occurrences of the word 'entropy'/'entropy H(' with zero ratified formal uses, and infers (recorded as unaudited hypothesis IT-H1, not an asserted fact) that every occurrence must be metaphorical, about an unadopted external regime, or an error, since no probability distribution exists anywhere in the corpus to license a genuine Shannon entropy computation; classifies this as the same defect class as prior findings about quantitative vocabulary used without the structure that licenses it, noting the corpus's own Shannon extraction already warns 'information is not meaning is not knowledge.'

b_rows_sample.anchor: An assertion with Sigma=(0,1) Refuted is a first-class member of A and, on the veridicality thesis, carries no semantic information at all. Adopting Floridi would make Refuted inexpressible.
b_rows_sample.statement: Decisive incompatibility: Floridi's veridicality thesis holds semantic information is necessarily truthful (false 'information' is not information), but the corpus's Closure-03 result 'Admission is not a truth function' deliberately retains Refuted assertions as first-class members of A; adopting Floridi's thesis would make Refuted assertions inexpressible -- classified as the same shape of error as adopting S5 veridicality for Sigma in the DEL comparison document.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Dretske's definition is strictly stronger — it requires (i) a conditional probability, (ii) its value to be exactly 1, and (iii) a background-knowledge index k. KnowledgeOS supplies none.
b_rows_sample.statement: Finds Dretske's information-carrying definition (signal r carries the information that s is F iff the conditional probability of s-is-F given r and receiver prior knowledge k equals exactly 1) strictly stronger than what KnowledgeOS's Evidence(O,P,C,R) (a relevance relation under a rule) can supply, especially since the verification-lane Qualify function has no implemented body (TG-14); concludes Evidence is not Dretskean information-carrying and cannot become so without reversing the T-3 no-probability ruling.

b_rows_sample.anchor: a way to distinguish not-asked from asked-and-empty | tolerance of contradictory signals as a state | provenance/authority | a goal state | non-veridical carriers ... a source distribution | a channel | an empirical relational structure | a code/compression notion
b_rows_sample.statement: Lists missing primitives on the information-theory side needed to host KnowledgeOS (a way to distinguish not-asked from asked-and-empty, since a sample-space partition has no 'unasked' cell -- the same defect class found against DEL; tolerance of contradictory signals as a state, for Conflict; provenance/authority, for governed admission; a goal state, for Ideal State; non-veridical carriers, for Refuted assertions) and on the KnowledgeOS side needed to host information theory (a source distribution -- 0 occurrences, declined by T-3; a channel -- no P(O|phi) anywhere; an empirical relational structure -- corpus finding G-12 blocks any numeric information measure independently of T-3; a code/compression notion -- absent and not obviously needed).

b_rows_sample.anchor: IT-H1 ... IT-H2 ... IT-H3 ... IT-H4 ... IT-H5
b_rows_sample.statement: States five falsifiable hypotheses: IT-H1 (all 87 corpus 'entropy' uses are metaphorical/regime-external/erroneous, falsified by exhibiting one that declares (Omega,F,P) and computes H over it); IT-H2 (Zero is a lattice antichain, not a measure -- no scalar summary preserves the ten-status distinction, already partly corroborated by zero_reference.py); IT-H3 (no distance-to-Ideal-State satisfying Q12 is definable without a metric or distribution, neither of which exists); IT-H4 (adopting Floridi veridicality would make Refuted inexpressible); IT-H5 (Evidence(O,P,C,R) is strictly weaker than Dretskean information-carrying, falsified by deriving Dretske's conditional-probability-1 condition from Qualify, currently impossible since Qualify has no body).

b_rows_sample.anchor: THE WEAKEST FIT OF THE FIVE — the quantitative layer is unavailable and the semantic layer contradicts a boxed corpus result ... What this analysis adds is that the residue is a lattice, and that Zero is already sitting in it.
b_rows_sample.statement: Final verdict: information theory is the weakest fit of the five external theories compared in this series -- no entropy/mutual-information/KL is available (all require the declined distribution), Floridi's veridicality thesis directly contradicts the corpus's Admission-is-not-a-truth-function result, and Dretske needs a channel and independence/prior structure the corpus lacks -- but the measure-free partition/coverage lattice does exactly fit Zero, and the corpus's own 2026-08-25 conclusion ('information is not meaning is not knowledge') is endorsed as correct; the analysis's own addition is identifying that the surviving residue is specifically a LATTICE, and that Zero already sits in it.

a_rows_sample.anchor: A C-10 receipt claims that governed knowledge delivery occurred and acknowledgement was recorded.
a_rows_sample.statement: D1's decided receipt claim boundary, consumed verbatim by E2: delivery occurred (a world-fact) and acknowledgement was recorded (a record-fact), asymmetrically.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Twelve fields. Five parts each: (1) semantic meaning · (2) classification · (3) claim limitation · (4) evidence relationship · (5) ownership + C-10 responsibility.
a_rows_sample.statement: A twelve-field completeness model for C-10 receipts (receipt_id, issuer, session_reference, actor_reference, knowledge_reference, knowledge_version, delivery_timestamp, acknowledgement_timestamp, acknowledgement_method, external_correlation_reference, lifecycle_state, invalidation_reference), each classified REQUIRED/SUPPORTING/CORRELATION ONLY/FORBIDDEN with an ownership four-part model (semantic/data/invariant/authority).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Anti-corruption rules — seven, all binding on §5–§8
a_rows_sample.statement: Seven anti-corruption rules bind the receipt model: Recording ≠ Asserting; Reference ≠ Ownership; Correlation ≠ Authority; Evidence ≠ Proof; Receipt Identity ≠ Receipt Authority; Acknowledgement Recorded ≠ Knowledge Understood ≠ Applied ≠ Compliance Achieved; Receipt Evidence ≠ Independent Proof of Underlying Event.

a_rows_sample.anchor: receipt_id makes a receipt referable. It does NOT make it authoritative. A receipt is an evidence record, not a certificate.
a_rows_sample.statement: Receipt identity (a receipt is distinguishable from every other receipt) is distinguished from receipt authority (the receipt's assertions are binding); C-10 holds none of the latter beyond D1's claim.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Test: orthogonal ∧ necessary ∧ sufficient.
a_rows_sample.statement: The four-part ownership model (semantic/data/invariant/authority owner) is justified by testing it against orthogonality (fields diverge and converge across the same dimension set), necessity (without the split 'C-10 stores it' collapses into 'C-10 owns it'), and sufficiency (no field required a fifth dimension; NONE is a legal, informative authority-owner value).

a_rows_sample.anchor: actor_reference ... FORBIDDEN as a C-10-owned field.
a_rows_sample.statement: An actor_reference field is forbidden as C-10-owned because it would invite the identity-binding inference D1 disallows, would import C-5 (identity attestation, an open capability) into C-10, and because self-declared identity is only evidential (INV-ATTR-1/INV-ATTR-2); if the estate ever needs 'who acknowledged', it must arrive through C-5 attestation or as external_correlation_reference content, never as a C-10-owned field.

a_rows_sample.anchor: session_reference is simultaneously REQUIRED and NON-ATTESTING.
a_rows_sample.statement: session_reference is defined as a recorded association between the acknowledgement and an execution context — status RECORDED, NOT ATTESTED — and explicitly does not mean identity attestation, actor verification, or execution authority.

a_rows_sample.anchor: For each at-risk field: intended meaning · permitted inference · forbidden inference · the five-way misreading test (AUTHORITY · IDENTITY · APPLICABILITY · COMPLIANCE · VERIFICATION)
a_rows_sample.statement: A semantic-inflation discovery over five at-risk fields (receipt_id, issuer, actor_reference, session_reference, external_correlation_reference) each tested against a five-way misreading test (AUTHORITY/IDENTITY/APPLICABILITY/COMPLIANCE/VERIFICATION) with a recorded prohibition per field, e.g. 'a receipt exists, therefore the act was warranted' is explicitly forbidden.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Divergence 1 is the one with lasting cost: AMD6 called the rename bounded-context protection, not style.
a_rows_sample.statement: Four verified divergences between the delivered, AMD6-corrected E2 and a re-sent assignment: (1) field renamed to drop 'applicability' vs reverting to 'applicability_reference'; (2) field classification vocabulary present vs absent; (3) D1 asymmetry preserved vs restated symmetrically (a weaker delivery claim); (4) seven vs six anti-corruption rules. Restoring 'applicability' to a field name is flagged as reintroducing exactly the ownership implication the anti-corruption rule forbids.

a_rows_sample.anchor: This review does not evaluate architectural correctness... It checks completeness · provenance · decision-boundary preservation only.
a_rows_sample.statement: A Governance completeness/provenance review is explicitly bounded: it does not redesign the artifact, change field decisions, approve adoption, verify implementation correctness, or replace Architecture reasoning, and per AMD1 Flag H must never be cited as independent verification of the artifact.

a_rows_sample.anchor: §5.1 states 'four of them are classified SUPPORTING.' Mechanical count of the §5.1 table: 7 REQUIRED · 3 SUPPORTING · 1 CORRELATION ONLY · 1 FORBIDDEN = 12.
a_rows_sample.statement: INFO-1: the E2 artifact's own summary sentence miscounts its own field-classification table (claims four SUPPORTING fields; the table mechanically counts three); no field classification is wrong, only the summary sentence.

a_rows_sample.anchor: the same process shaped both sides of the E2 ↔ D5 interface.
a_rows_sample.statement: INFO-2: the producing process of E2 also authored the D5 establishment-criteria proposal and the canonical C-10 analysis, meaning the same process shaped both sides of the E2↔D5 interface; recorded as non-blocking but as a residual for future acts to weigh.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Fourth occurrence of substantive input reaching a governed decision from outside the governed channel
a_rows_sample.statement: INFO-3: the Flag-O resolution and the seventh anti-corruption rule are consumed by E2 from a PO/ARB act absent from any registered instrument, marking the fourth recorded instance of substantive input reaching a governed decision from outside the governed channel within this work item; recorded as OBSERVED evidence under ES-006.1, not promoted to a standard.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The Seventh Rule: Receipt Evidence ≠ Independent Proof of Underlying Event.
a_rows_sample.statement: The seventh anti-corruption rule, registered by this act rather than left unregistered: a receipt's delivery element is evidence toward a world-fact, and its acknowledgement element is evidence of a record-fact — without this rule the delivery element could be read as self-sufficient proof that delivery occurred, which D1 does not claim.

a_rows_sample.anchor: This is the fourth recorded instance of substantive input reaching a governed decision from outside the governed channel...Four occurrences within one work item is EVIDENCE, NOT A STANDARD.
a_rows_sample.statement: Explicit governance note that a repeated pattern (four occurrences) is recorded as OBSERVED evidence under ES-006.1 and that no methodology is promoted by the registration nor is the pattern converted into a rule.

a_rows_sample.anchor: ACCEPT WITH RECORDED FOLLOW-UP ITEMS (Option B) ... E2 STATUS: ADOPTED
a_rows_sample.statement: PO/ARB adopts the E2 receipt completeness model with recorded follow-up items (Option B chosen over plain accept, return-for-clarification, or reject) because none of the review's findings has architectural impact or requires reopening the artifact.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Adopting a completeness model is not evidence of capability existence — under D5's own scheme a definition is Class C (future/architectural) evidence, which cannot establish existence by itself.
a_rows_sample.statement: Adopting a completeness/design model for a capability is explicitly distinguished from establishing that the capability exists; such adoption is Class C (future/architectural) evidence under the D5 scheme and cannot by itself establish existence.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 13 of 20 ordered pairs are separable by an explicit witness. The 7 that are not form a refinement order ... But the order is lambda-relative.
b_rows_sample.statement: Details result 3 (E2): the five equality relations form a refinement implication order in 7 of 20 pairs (the rest genuinely non-substitutable), and the order itself moves with the observation window lambda.

group_evidence.why_grouped: labels share the notation 'E2'

a_rows_sample.anchor: O_core occurs 5 times, all inside that one file. No declaring artifact exists. ... A decision reported inside a Stratum-1 research file, with no authority record, is not an authority act.
a_rows_sample.statement: Flags that Step 273's foundational premise 'the verified semantic operation universe O_core' (citing an unlocated 'attached HPA response') has O_core occurring only 5 times, all inside that single research file, with governance-notes.md (through GN-73) containing zero entries for O_core or Steps 271-273 -- treated as an unauthorized-decision discrepancy (new item D-0) rather than accepted premise.

a_rows_sample.anchor: a normative choice is required | true | ... the operation universe cannot be derived | PARTIALLY | derivable to a 14-element lower bound; membership not derivable | ... innovation appears necessary | false | every construct below is PROMOTION or DERIVATION
a_rows_sample.statement: Evaluates the mandate's STOP conditions against evidence (not assumption): four trigger (normative choice required; two corpus-supported definitions unreconciled; a ratified decision would need changing; identity/equivalence changes materially), one partially triggers (operation universe: derivable to a 14-element lower bound, membership not derivable), and two do not trigger (innovation not necessary anywhere but one place; authority can be placed) -- determining which artifacts (00-03, 19, 21, BLOCKED-MANIFEST) are decision-independent and producible now versus which (04-18, 20) are blocked.

F(Hr) = F(Hs) = True ... i = relate(A1,A4,supersedes) -> congruent: True ... i = assert A2 -> congruent: True ... i = relate(A4,A1,refines) -> congruent: True ... a_rows_sample.statement: Structural (by-construction) explanation for why congruence held in every test: T's derived signature K x Op x Policy x Authority -harpoon-> K x Outcome does not include History in its domain, so T cannot depend on it — a function cannot depend on an argument it does not receive. This holds under exactly two assumptions: A1 (T reads only K, Policy, Authority — PROVEN by elimination of actor/time/evidence/context during signature derivation) and A2 (no operation consults order-of-arrival — HOLDS for the twelve derived operations because A and R are sets, making order structurally unobservable).

a_rows_sample.anchor: A2 is the one that could fail. Any future operation reading insertion order — "the first assertion wins", "the most recently added is authoritative" — breaks congruence immediately. That is a design constraint the theory now states explicitly rather than assumes silently.
a_rows_sample.statement: Explicit forward-looking design constraint: assumption A2 (no operation consults insertion order) is violable by future design — any future operation implementing 'first assertion wins' or 'most recently added is authoritative' semantics would break congruence immediately; the theory now states this as an explicit constraint rather than a silent assumption.

a_rows_sample.anchor: SUFFICIENT UNDER ASSUMPTIONS. Not sufficient unqualified: the assumptions are real and A2 is violable by future design. Not insufficient: no counterexample exists and none can, given A1. Not unknown: the test was constructed correctly and executed.
a_rows_sample.statement: Final classification: the Knowledge-State/History sufficiency question is SUFFICIENT UNDER ASSUMPTIONS — deliberately neither 'sufficient unqualified' (the assumptions A1/A2 are real and A2 is violable), nor 'insufficient' (no counterexample exists, and none can given A1), nor 'unknown' (the test was validly constructed and executed).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Knowledge State is sufficient for FUTURE COMPUTATION. It is NOT sufficient for GOVERNANCE AUDIT. ... Who asserted this, and when? NO ... Was every admission properly authorised? NO — GovernanceValid(K,Γ) needs History ... What did we believe last March? NO — needs History
a_rows_sample.statement: The state/history sufficiency boundary is drawn precisely: K alone answers what is currently held, what follows from an operation (congruence), whether structural/semantic invariants hold, and current epistemic status (recomputable from e); K alone CANNOT answer who asserted something and when, whether every admission was properly authorised (GovernanceValid(K,Gamma) needs History), or what was believed at a past point in time (needs History or a bitemporal interpretation of t).

a_rows_sample.anchor: K answers what is known. History answers how it came to be known and by whom. Neither reduces to the other, and T needs only the first.
a_rows_sample.statement: Governing principle stated as the resolution of the state/history boundary the programme has circled since the executed History(K)!=K counterexample: K answers what is known; History answers how it came to be known and by whom; neither reduces to the other, and the transformation function T needs only K.

b_rows_sample.anchor: At least the following relations must be separated: = representation/structural equality; ≡ semantic equality; ≈ observational equivalence; ≅_I identity equivalence; ≅_P provenance-sensitive equivalence; ≅_H historical equivalence.
b_rows_sample.statement: The overloaded notation K1=K2 is decomposed into (at least) six distinct relations that must not be conflated: structural equality (=), semantic equality (equiv), observational equivalence (approx), identity equivalence (cong_I), provenance-sensitive equivalence (cong_P), and historical equivalence (cong_H); the corpus is said to explicitly record the first four distinctions and warn they are not interchangeable.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Same proposition ⇏ Same evidence identity. ... two observations can concern the same proposition while remaining distinct evidence objects.
b_rows_sample.statement: Preserved historical result: identity is not equality — two evidence objects e1,e2 can both support the same proposition p (Supports(e1,p) and Supports(e2,p)) without e1=e2; this affects provenance, deduplication, replay, validation, audit and merge, and is attributed to an earlier corpus reconstruction rather than newly derived here.

b_rows_sample.anchor: x =_str y iff their representations are structurally identical. ... =_str ≠ semantic equality unless the representation has already been proven canonical.
b_rows_sample.statement: Structural equality x=_str y (representations structurally identical) is computationally convenient but is warned to not equal semantic equality unless the representation is already proven canonical — two structurally different representations can denote the same semantic state.

b_rows_sample.anchor: x ≡_sem y iff Semantics(x)=Semantics(y). ... Semantic equality is conceptually appropriate, but currently underdefined.
b_rows_sample.statement: Semantic equality x equiv_sem y is defined via a semantic interpretation function Sem:Representation->Meaning being equal on x and y, but is flagged as not computationally decidable while Sem itself remains formally undefined — conceptually appropriate but currently underdefined.

b_rows_sample.anchor: H1 ≈ H2 iff every permitted observation produces the same result: ∀O∈𝒪: O(H1)=O(H2). ... This is the relation already underlying Step 260's behavioral quotient.
b_rows_sample.statement: Observational equivalence for histories (H1 approx H2 iff every permitted observation O produces the same result) and for states (K1 approx K2 iff every permitted state observation agrees) is identified as the same relation already underlying Step 260's behavioral quotient; notably it does not require internal representations to be identical.

b_rows_sample.anchor: SameId(x,y) ... Identity tracks denotation; equality compares values. This formulation is a reconstruction, not yet a corpus-proven final definition.
b_rows_sample.statement: Identity (SameId(x,y)) answers whether two references denote the same domain object, independent of value equality: x=_str y can hold with SameId false (two separately created records with identical content but distinct observations), and SameId can hold while representations differ (the same domain object having evolved) — 'identity tracks denotation; equality compares values', explicitly flagged as a reconstruction, not a corpus-proven final definition.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Historical equality asks: Are these states the same point or condition in an evolution history? ... Semantic equality ⇏ Historical equality.
b_rows_sample.statement: Historical equality asks whether two states are the same point in an evolution history, distinct from current semantic equality: K0 -Revise-> K1 can have K0 equiv_sem K1 (representation changed, semantics didn't) while K0 !=_H K1 (distinct historical states) — semantic equality does not imply historical equality; matters especially for Replay and audit.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Provenance is semantically relevant: K1 ≢ K2. Provenance is metadata only: K1 ≡ K2. ... equality cannot be resolved until the theory determines which information is semantically essential. This is a key dependency for Step 265.
b_rows_sample.statement: Provenance equality is genuinely ambiguous: given K1={p,e1}, K2={p,e2} with e1!=e2 both supporting p, either provenance is semantically relevant (K1 not-equiv K2) or metadata only (K1 equiv K2); the earlier corpus is said to identify this ambiguity explicitly and conclude it cannot be resolved until the theory determines which information is semantically essential — flagged as a key dependency for Step 265 (provenance placement).

b_rows_sample.anchor: No universal equality hierarchy has yet been proven. ... Identity and Provenance equality are independent dimensions.
b_rows_sample.statement: A candidate implication chain (structural => semantic => observational equivalence) is proposed but explicitly not declared universally valid without further assumptions; identity and provenance equality are treated as independent dimensions from this chain; current position: no universal equality hierarchy has yet been proven.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Explicit assertion membership ≠ semantic entailment. ... a∈_exp K ... K⊨a ... Stored fact ≠ logically derived fact.
b_rows_sample.statement: Membership in an assertion-based state K is typed into explicit assertion membership (a in_exp K, a is literally one of K's stored assertions) versus semantic consequence (K models a, semantically entailed but not necessarily stored) — a proposed formal distinction (not yet a theorem) preventing the category error of treating a stored fact as identical to a logically derived one; flagged as essential for Step 262's assertion type.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Merge equality: semantic + identity + provenance dependent. Exact final semantics remain unresolved.
b_rows_sample.statement: Operation test — Merge: Merge(K1,K2) cannot be specified using structural equality alone, since a1=(p,e1) and a2=(p,e2) sharing proposition p could legitimately merge to {a1,a2} (kept separate) or to a single combined-evidence assertion depending on ontology; Merge equality is semantic+identity+provenance dependent, with exact final semantics unresolved.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Supersession requires identity/version distinction. ... collapsing them under semantic equality would destroy the very relation x2 ≻ x1.
b_rows_sample.statement: Operation test — Supersede: if Meaning(x1)=Meaning(x2) but Identity(x1)!=Identity(x2) and x2 supersedes x1, collapsing x1,x2 under semantic equality would destroy the supersession relation x2 succ x1 itself; supersession therefore requires an identity/version distinction, strongly suggesting semantic equality alone cannot serve as the sole equality relation.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Replay requires historical identity/equality independent of current state equality. ... Replay(H1)=K and Replay(H2)=K yet H1 ≠_H H2.
b_rows_sample.statement: Operation test — Replay: two distinct histories H1,H2 (H1 !=_H H2) can replay to the same current state K (Replay(H1)=Replay(H2)=K); Replay is treated by the corpus as a history/audit operation rather than another state transformation, and requires historical identity/equality independent of current-state equality.

b_rows_sample.anchor: | Operation | Structural equality | Semantic equality | Identity | Historical equality | Provenance | Current assessment | Merge...Supersede...Replay...Remove...Revise...Deduplicate...Validate
b_rows_sample.statement: The full operation/equality matrix across Merge, Supersede, Replay, Remove, Revise, Deduplicate, Validate rates each of structural/semantic/identity/historical/provenance equality as insufficient, required, relevant, potentially-required, or context-dependent per operation, with every row's overall status UNRESOLVED, NORMATIVE/DOMAIN-DEPENDENT (Deduplicate), or 'Assessment relation' (Validate); Remove requires identity for correct object targeting (must not remove a2 when removing a1 despite structural identity), Revise cannot use semantic equality as its sole target selector (must not implicitly revise x2 when revising x1 despite x1 equiv_sem x2), Deduplicate cannot be specified until its preservation policy is known (structural/semantic/identity/provenance criteria can each give different results), and Validate shows semantic state equality does not imply identical validation results because validation is a relation over (K,E) pairs, not K alone — reinforcing that not every operation is a state transformation T:K->K.

b_rows_sample.anchor: No single equality relation is adequate for all KnowledgeOS operations. ... KnowledgeOS requires a typed family of relations.
b_rows_sample.statement: Major correction to the kernel concept: rejects the implicit assumption 'KnowledgeOS needs one equality operator', replacing it with 'KnowledgeOS requires a typed family of relations' (=_str, equiv_sem, approx_obs, SameId, equiv_H, equiv_P) that may be connected by formally established implications but must not be conflated.

b_rows_sample.anchor: K1 ≡_K K2 ⟺ ∀O∈𝒪_K: O(K1)=O(K2) ... 𝒪_K is not yet completely closed. Therefore this is a candidate formal definition, not a completed theorem.
b_rows_sample.statement: Candidate formal definition of Knowledge-State equality as purely observational/behavioral: K1 equiv_K K2 iff every permitted state observation O in the (not-yet-closed) set O_K agrees on K1 and K2; explicitly a candidate, not a completed theorem, because O_K is not yet closed.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Equality → Congruence → Quotient → Minimality. This is the correct dependency direction.
b_rows_sample.statement: If K1 equiv_K K2 (no permitted observation distinguishes them) and all mandatory operations preserve that equivalence, equiv_K becomes the congruence relation needed for the minimal quotient K*=H/equiv (Step 260) — establishing the dependency direction Equality -> Congruence -> Quotient -> Minimality as correct.

b_rows_sample.anchor: the observation set is not fully closed; the operation registry is not fully closed; provenance placement remains unresolved; assertion semantics remain unresolved; temporal semantics remain unresolved; identity semantics remain unresolved. The governing prompt explicitly says that final kernel sele
b_rows_sample.statement: Explicit refusal to overclaim equiv_K as final: six named open dependencies remain (observation-set closure, operation-registry closure, provenance placement, assertion semantics, temporal semantics, identity semantics); the governing prompt is cited as requiring final kernel selection to halt while equality remains ambiguous, and this gate is obeyed.

b_rows_sample.anchor: bounded contexts may legitimately require different relations: same assertion / same evidence / same domain identity / same version / same semantic meaning / same observable state ... PRIMARY KEY must therefore not automatically be interpreted as SemanticIdentity. ... content hash must not automatic
b_rows_sample.statement: DDD interpretation: rather than one generic 'Equality' concept used everywhere, different bounded contexts legitimately require different named relations (same assertion, same evidence, same domain identity, same version, same semantic meaning, same observable state); a database PRIMARY KEY must not automatically be interpreted as SemanticIdentity, and a content hash must not automatically become DomainIdentity.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 𝔎=(K,=_str,≡_sem,≈_obs,SameId,≡_H,≡_P). The next question is not 'Which one is the equality?' It is 'Which relation is the appropriate congruence relation for each operation and which relation defines semantic equality of Knowledge States?'
b_rows_sample.statement: Mathematical reframing: KnowledgeOS's state carries a relational structure 𝔎=(K,=_str,equiv_sem,approx_obs,SameId,equiv_H,equiv_P) rather than a single equality; the research question shifts from 'which relation is THE equality' to 'which relation is the appropriate congruence for each operation, and which defines semantic equality of Knowledge States'.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Q1 — what problem was the model created to solve? ... "this model says what decisions an Engineer resolves with them"
b_rows_sample.statement: The Engineering Decision Model was created because standards say what the rules are, while the model says what decisions an engineer resolves with them: rules existed but the decisions they answer were unindexed. Its anti-problem: it is a decision INDEX, never a second rulebook (ARB, 2026-07-11) — created to prevent duplicated authority, not to add a layer. Its birth act included a vocabulary correction (2026-07-11): a DDD Domain Service is executable, a decision is a specification. Its adoption bar: one real engineering cycle must show consistent resolution through the model; it is DRAFT until earned.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Q2 — which decisions does it explicitly model? ... Eight — all of one family
b_rows_sample.statement: Eight decisions are explicitly modeled, all of one family (the flow of knowledge and artifacts through governed work), grouped by question: 'Where does it belong?' (DetermineConcern, DeterminePlacement - mechanized by doc-placement.php); 'What is it/does it live?' (DetermineArtifactLifecycle - deletion litmus, DetermineArtifactType); 'Is it worth keeping/raising?' (DetermineReusePotential - Harvest, DeterminePromotionPath - ladder entry); 'What governs/verifies it?' (DetermineApplicableStandards, DetermineQualificationMethod). Deliberately excluded: ADR-making, capability approval, authority acts, promotion rulings — 'promotion is a human governance act and is never automated'; 'the AI evaluates and recommends — authority remains with governance.' The absence of governance decisions from the catalog is design, not gap.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Q3 — which discovered decisions are not represented? ... FREEZE and RETIRE extend nothing in the catalog
b_rows_sample.statement: Answered in a prior Discovery pass and carried forward unchanged: FREEZE (n>=3, undeclared authority) and RETIRE (PM-6) extend nothing in the catalog, submitted as insufficiency evidence per the model's own stopping rule. Implicit but exercised: the challenge-commissioning trigger and terminology adoption. Nothing further found in this pass, which per the stopping rule is the correct amount.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Q4 — does it govern the full ladder, or only architecture decisions? ... NEITHER — and the answer is the INVERSE of the commission's suspicion
b_rows_sample.statement: The model governs zero architecture decisions (no DetermineArchitectureDecision exists; ADRs are governance acts, outside the catalog by design). What it governs on the ladder Observation->Hypothesis->Evidence->Principle->Architecture is the entry points, not the rungs: DetermineReusePotential opens the ladder (observation->candidate); DeterminePromotionPath routes onto it (candidate->pilot->qualification->ARB decides). The rungs belong to ES-006.1, and the model correctly refuses to own them since it is an index, never a second rulebook.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Q5 — Knowledge Governance or only Engineering Governance? ... Engineering Governance NOW; Knowledge Governance ANTICIPATED
b_rows_sample.statement: The model's own Decision Catalogs table states Engineering Standards answer the catalog's Engineering Decisions, while Project-Knowledge-class Knowledge Decisions (DetermineKnowledgeNeed, Source, Representation, Qualification, Promotion) are 'pilot-gated candidates — arrive only with pilot evidence; same pattern, different domain.' Engineering Governance is present now; Knowledge Governance is anticipated with the arrival condition already stated, and the entire ontology/meta-model corpus of this programme is exactly the kind of pilot evidence the anticipated catalog says it is waiting for.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Q6 — extend the model, or map onto it? ... MAP. Tested element by element
b_rows_sample.statement: Ontology/meta-model elements map onto the existing decision model rather than extending it: archetype classification extends DetermineArtifactType (same question, richer vocabulary); KNOWLEDGE != ARTIFACT (I-1) is presupposed by DetermineArtifactLifecycle's deletion litmus; AUTHORITY-SCOPE/CONTAINER boundary maps to DetermineConcern/DeterminePlacement; GOVERNANCE-STATUS/EVIDENCE-STATUS maps to DeterminePromotionPath; NATURE (normative force) maps to DetermineApplicableStandards. Nothing in the ontology requires a new decision; the only extension pressure (FREEZE/RETIRE) is not ontology-driven, but comes from the enacted governance record. Verdict: the ontology supplies the vocabulary the catalog's procedures presuppose; the catalog supplies the purpose the ontology elements must serve — they interlock, neither extends the other.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Q7 — would a second decision model violate ubiquitous language? ... YES — three times over
b_rows_sample.statement: A second decision model would violate ubiquitous language three times over: (1) the model's charter states it is 'a decision INDEX, never a second rulebook' — a v2 is exactly what it exists to prevent; (2) I-5, lint-enforced, requires one authoritative artifact per topic+context, so a second model is a literal violation; (3) ES-005.4 requires one rule -> one home. A competing 'KnowledgeOS Decision Model' would have been the UL violation and was not created; the Discovery and Validation passes are readings of the one model, not rivals to it.

b_rows_sample.anchor: RESULT: THE MODEL DOES NOT SURVIVE INTACT. One claim FALSIFIED · two WEAKENED · two SURVIVED · two unchanged
b_rows_sample.statement: Overall falsification result: of the domain model's claims, one is falsified, two weakened, two survived, two unchanged; the strongest claim in the model (D-2) was among those weakened, by evidence the model itself had cited. Method: every test executed against artifacts, not reasoned from the model, using the repository's own instruments (Round47-OP's nine admissible justifications, the R16 Workbook Strong/Medium/Weak scale); four falsifiers were sought, three landed.

b_rows_sample.anchor: W-1 · D-2's "own decision series" is a shared authority — two of four grounds fall
b_rows_sample.statement: D-2's claim of 'its own decision series, ADR-M distinct from ADR-AIP' is weakened: Round39-D6's header states decision authority for all ADRs is 'sponsor + ARB' and amendment requires sponsor+ARB approval, so ADR-M is a scoping device under a shared authority, not a separate authority. Its claim of 'independent evolution' is falsified: Round39-D6 states the ADRs 'were authored together on 2026-06-25' — a series written in one sitting evidences independent subject, never independent evolution over time. This matches the ARB Chair's named falsifier 'ADR separation is historical rather than semantic' — half true: separation is real in subject, absent in time.

b_rows_sample.anchor: S-1 · D-2 survives on a ground I had not weighted — an explicit mutual scope exclusion
b_rows_sample.statement: D-2 survives on a new ground: Round39-D6's verbatim rule 'Governance discoveries (constitutional/capability) MUST NOT appear here. No DDD concepts here' is a deliberately maintained boundary (not an accident of filing), bidirectional in effect (ADR-M excludes governance, ADR-AIP carries no methodology rules), and survives the shared-authority finding since a shared authority that forbids itself from mixing two subjects is evidence FOR two models, not against. D-2 remains a boundary, but on subject exclusion, not on decision-series separation or independent evolution.

b_rows_sample.anchor: S-3 · D-1 survives every falsifier
b_rows_sample.statement: D-1 survives every falsifier sought: no multiple owners of the same concept found (DA/ARB throughout), no changes that fail to co-occur (ES set moves under STANDARDS_INDEX), no forced co-evolution with a product (ratification and freeze are product-independent), no absent invariants (append-only rulings, R-46).
