b_rows_sample.statement: Per-domain confidence after falsification (R16 Strong/Medium/Weak scale): D-1 Strong->STRONG; D-2 Strong->MEDIUM; D-3 Strong->WEAK; D-6a (Evidence Protocol) new->MEDIUM; D-6b (Product Evidence) new->STRONG; D-5 (Engineering Capability, not a context) Medium->MEDIUM (unchanged, H-CAT-1 stands); D-4 (Workflow, rejected) ->STRONG as a rejection; D-7 (PKS, a context type) new->WEAK. Distinction drawn: falsified is worse than unevidenced — D-3 and D-7 carry contradicting evidence (falsified); D-6a carries no evidence (unevidenced).

b_rows_sample.statement: Per-domain recommendations: D-1 ACCEPT; D-2 REVISE (restate the boundary on the one surviving ground, Round39-D6's scope exclusion; delete 'own decision series' and 'independent evolution' as grounds); D-3 DEFER (untestable at n=1, revisit when a second runtime adapter exists); D-6a DEFER, D-6b ACCEPT; D-5 ACCEPT the demotion (do not promote until ARB overturns H-CAT-1 on evidence); D-4 ACCEPT the rejection; D-7 REVISE (restate as an observation of one instance, record PKS-as-projection as falsified). b_rows_sample.statement: Fifteen candidate concerns, each citing its supporting commission and what it waits on: K-1 dimensional-with-archetypes meta-model; K-2 the archetype set (strong: DOMAIN/PROCESS/CAPABILITY/KNOWLEDGE/ARTIFACT/RUNTIME ASSET/PROJECTION; weaker: CONTAINER; weakest: PURPOSE); K-3 the four partial orders (authority, production, realization, containment); K-4 11 invariant relationships vs 8 implementation choices; K-5 DP-n as capability anchor; K-6 Knowledge Space = declared boundary+owner+constitution; K-7 authority = provenance x standing, four progression kinds; K-8 the strategic domain set PD-1/2/3/5; K-9 viewpoints as presentation; K-10 decision-readiness as the platform's product; K-11 FREEZE/RETIRE as insufficiency evidence; K-12 PKS extends context-engineering with governance; K-13 the canon-track reference artifacts themselves; K-14 the mission is enacted via 8 artifacts; K-15 ownership splits (candidate-unowned=ladder working, operating-unowned=defect, sole instance Runtime Adapter).

b_rows_sample.anchor: 3. HYPOTHESIS — plausible, insufficient evidence (H-1..H-9)
b_rows_sample.statement: Nine hypotheses with evidence state: H-1 the space map is the platform's real ownership/context map (n=1, downgraded); H-2 GOVERNANCE as a fifth viewpoint (asset found, framing undecided); H-3 PURPOSE more fundamental than CONTAINER (n=0); H-4 KnowledgeOS as a 'Knowledge Architecture Platform' (n=1); H-5 'generates -> PKS', the loop's head edge and the platform's distinctive bet (n=0 inside and outside); H-6 capability may read across a space boundary, never own (n=1 capability); H-7 space nesting (unevidenced); H-8 DOMAIN's decision-silence is dormant not permanent (untestable at n=1); H-9 EVIDENCE-STATUS/OPERATIONAL-STATE as meta-model dimensions (proposed, undocketed).

b_rows_sample.anchor: ANNOTATED 2026-08-02 — THREE CORRECTIONS ... LEVEL MIXING — my third instance of that error class
b_rows_sample.statement: Three annotated corrections (recorded in KnowledgeOS_Relationship_Ontology.md): (1) section 2's six concepts are not siblings but four ontological layers (Purpose/Mission, Platform/Capability+Knowledge, Representation/Artifact, Application/PKS+Product) listed as one set — a third instance of level mixing; (2) PKS is a CONTAINER, not a layer below ARTIFACT — a PKS contains artifacts, and KNOWLEDGE SPACE is admitted as the container concept, defined by a declared boundary (scope.include), not a folder; (3) the document itself conflates two levels — section 1 (dimensions) is a meta-model, section 2 (concepts) is an ontology, both named rather than the whole renamed. The chain in section 2 is completed by naming DP-n (DESIGN POLICY) as the anchor stopping capabilities from floating, observable in the Capability Catalog's 1:1 CAP->DP binding.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Concepts × kind × owner (C-1..C-13)
b_rows_sample.statement: Thirteen concepts classified by kind and owner: C-1 VISION (purpose, sponsor); C-2 MISSION (purpose, sponsor, enacted-unratified); C-3 ENGINEERING STRATEGY (purpose->governance bridge, ARB/sponsor); C-4 ENGINEERING PRINCIPLE (governance, DA/sponsor+ARB/platform depending on series); C-5 DESIGN POLICY DP-n (governance, DA via Catalog); C-6 ENGINEERING CAPABILITY (capability, its DP-n not a domain); C-7 ENGINEERING KNOWLEDGE (knowledge, DA/sponsor+ARB); C-8 ENGINEERING ARTIFACT (representation, its owner field); C-9 KNOWLEDGE SPACE (container, the space's own owner); C-10 PKS (container, product team); C-11 PRODUCT (application, product team); C-12 RUNTIME ADAPTER (runtime element, no owner found); C-13 PROJECTION (projection, the generating space).

b_rows_sample.anchor: C-9 KNOWLEDGE SPACE — admitted, and the evidence is a boundary, not a folder ... A Knowledge Space is not a folder. It is a DECLARED SCOPE with an owner and a governing constitution
b_rows_sample.statement: KNOWLEDGE SPACE is admitted, evidenced by: knowledge-schema.yaml's declared scope.include; three registered documentation roots (knowledgeos, pks, publicdigit); ES-005.1's three concerns (Product, Platform, Runtime mount); the EKP having its own constitution and owner. A Knowledge Space is a declared scope with an owner and a governing constitution, not a folder — which is why the '13% coverage' question was a scope decision, not a bug.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The relationship model — the commission's seven questions ... contains = a container relation · references = a pointer · generates = produces a new instance · depends on = cannot be understood without
b_rows_sample.statement: A full relationship table across all thirteen concepts, using four typed relations (contains = container relation, references = a pointer, generates = produces a new instance, depends on = cannot be understood without). Notable entries: KNOWLEDGE SPACE may contain artifacts and other knowledge spaces, generates PROJECTIONS; PKS may contain product artifacts but never reusable Method, references Engineering Knowledge, generates Product Projections; ARTIFACT is a leaf (contains nothing) but depends on the Knowledge it represents; KNOWLEDGE generates nothing, being represented rather than generative.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Missing concepts — recorded as hypotheses, not admitted (H-1..H-4)
b_rows_sample.statement: Four candidate concepts recorded as hypotheses, none admitted: H-1 'I-12', a Capability may read across a space boundary but never own what it reads (n=1 capability, needs a second cross-boundary reader); H-2 Engineering Domain as owner of Capabilities (no artifact binds a CAP to a PD; DP-n already fills the slot); H-3 Knowledge Space nesting, does the EKP contain the PKS or sit beside it (containment vs adjacency unevidenced); H-4 whether OPERATIONAL-STATE attaches to the Artifact or the Knowledge it carries (would change I-1's granularity).

b_rows_sample.anchor: RO-2 | Are Knowledge Spaces nested or adjacent?
b_rows_sample.statement: RO-2: are Knowledge Spaces nested or adjacent (H-3) — authority: ARB.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The three challenges — accepted, and one is settled by my own evidence rules ... CONTAINER demoted CONFIRMED → CANDIDATE ... my own admission rule decides it, not deference
b_rows_sample.statement: Three reviewer challenges: (1) 'Archetype' replaces 'nine kinds' until MM-1, since 'archetype' already exists in the corpus (RQ-002) so the rename mints nothing — a ubiquitous-language decision, decided with governance (MM-1), not unilaterally; (2) CONTAINER is demoted from CONFIRMED to CANDIDATE by the author's own admission rule: 'Containers generate Projections' is observed in exactly one space (the EKP's knowledge-graph.php), n=1, and nesting is unevidenced (H-3) — the settling test is a second generating space (confirms) or a capability-plus-scope reduction (refutes); (3) PURPOSE, possibly more fundamental than Container, is flagged not resolved, since the mission is enacted and unratified (D-5 pending), and deepening PURPOSE before ratification would model ahead of the domain expert — recorded as hypothesis U-ONT-2, n=0.

b_rows_sample.anchor: What exists instead ... FOUR DISTINCT PARTIAL ORDERS, one per relationship type: AUTHORITY · PRODUCTION · REALIZATION · CONTAINMENT
b_rows_sample.statement: Four evidenced partial orders replace the refuted single stack: AUTHORITY (who justifies whom) PURPOSE->STRATEGY->PRINCIPLE->DP-n->CAPABILITY; PRODUCTION (who produces whom) PROCESS->Knowledge/Artifacts/Evidence, CAPABILITY->Evidence, CONTAINER->Projection (n=1); REALIZATION (concept -> executable/persistent form) KNOWLEDGE->ARTIFACT (I-1), CAPABILITY->RUNTIME ASSET (R-7, SC-6 gap); CONTAINMENT (what moves together) CONTAINER contains Artifacts (contains other spaces? H-3 open). The intuition underneath the stack survives: relations are directional, with DOMAIN/KNOWLEDGE conceptual and RUNTIME/ARTIFACT realized; but 'which is above' is only answerable per relation, not for the stack as a whole.

a_rows_sample.statement: Falsifier V-2: the discovery's claim that C-14 policy enforcement is 'absent / NO OWNER' is falsified by AST-007 (db-safety-check.sh), an adopted Tier-1 blocking gate at PRE_ACTION; the correct characterisation is a coverage/ownership gap, not an absent capability.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Four capabilities have NO OWNER: C-5 separation attestation, C-10 knowledge distribution, C-14 policy enforcement, C-19 communication composition. INFERRED: these four, not the six roles, are the substance of ADR-AIP-04.
a_rows_sample.statement: Headline finding: of a 20-capability inventory (C-1..C-20) derived from evidence of what the platform actually does, four capabilities (C-5 separation attestation, C-10 knowledge distribution, C-14 policy enforcement, C-19 communication composition) have no declared owner -- proposed as the real substance of ADR-AIP-04, in contrast to the six proposed roles.

a_rows_sample.anchor: EKS-02: three capabilities are routinely conflated -- policy authorship, policy derivation (C-13, live), policy enforcement (C-14, absent). Only the third is missing, and no role fixes it; a gate does.
a_rows_sample.statement: Finding F-7: policy authorship, policy derivation (C-13, live via doc-placement.php), and policy enforcement (C-14, initially claimed absent) are three distinct capabilities routinely conflated; the fix for a missing enforcement capability is a mechanical gate, not a named role.

a_rows_sample.anchor: AST-007's own trace assigns it to capability: CAP-09, context: verification-evidence -- i.e. the one live blocking enforcement instance sits in BC-3 Verification & Evidence, NOT in BC-2 Implementation Guidance.
a_rows_sample.statement: Amendment 1 withdraws the C-14/BC-2 placement as unsupported by evidence, since AST-007's own registry trace assigns it to CAP-09 in BC-3 (Verification & Evidence), not BC-2; opens new question OQ-H (does C-14's home lie in BC-2 or BC-3?).

a_rows_sample.anchor: the C-14 correction moved onto the C-5 row while C-14 still displayed the falsified "absent / NO OWNER" ... shared the look-alike cell ... and the first match was C-5.
a_rows_sample.statement: Correction #2 (finding W-2) discovers the Amendment 1 pointer correcting C-14's status was applied by a scripted first-match string replace and accidentally landed on the C-5 row instead, because both capabilities shared an identical look-alike table cell -- and it proposes extending the existing 'no automated search-and-replace on source code' rule's scope to any artifact with look-alike sites.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Therefore Amendment 1's status LIVE, NARROW, UNMODELLED was still too strong, and is corrected to CONTESTED.
a_rows_sample.statement: Correction #2 (finding W-6) further downgrades C-14's status from Amendment 1's 'live, narrow, unmodelled' to CONTESTED, because AST-007's own registry trace assigns it to CAP-09 (Constitutional Observation & Escalation, halt-on-trip), whose defined behaviour may be a different capability than C-14 entirely; SB-3's premise is correspondingly restored to OPEN/UNQUANTIFIED.

a_rows_sample.anchor: C-5: YES existence, control-plane function category. C-10: NOT YET ESTABLISHED, deferred category. C-14: CONTESTED, deferred. C-19: YES, stewardship/cross-cutting category. The forbidden collapse is absent.
a_rows_sample.statement: Independent verification confirms the existence/category split was applied without the forbidden collapse for all four capabilities: C-5 exists (control-plane function), C-10's existence is NOT YET ESTABLISHED (category deferred), C-14's existence is CONTESTED (category deferred), C-19 exists (stewardship/cross-cutting), each argued from positive properties rather than derived from the other axis.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The four are not four candidate contexts. They are one CONTROL LOOP with four distinct capabilities in it. policy/knowledge DEFINED (BC-1) -> C-10 DELIVERS it to the gated session -> C-14 GATES the act -> C-19 EXPRESSES the outcome <- C-5 ATTESTS who acted
a_rows_sample.statement: Structural finding: C-5, C-10, C-14, C-19 are not four independent candidate bounded contexts but four capabilities within one control loop -- BC-1's policy/knowledge is delivered by C-10 to a gated session, C-14 gates the act, C-19 expresses the outcome, and C-5 attests who acted and how separately -- while still having four distinct reasons to change, so the relationship, not a merged boundary, is what explains them.

a_rows_sample.anchor: a unifying invariant candidate falls out of it: both control-plane capabilities are defeated by the SAME failure -- self-assertion by the gated party. C-5 is defeated by self-declared separation; C-14 by self-declared compliance.
a_rows_sample.statement: A unifying control-plane invariant candidate (proposed, not adopted): a gate's verdict may not be issued by the party the gate constrains; observed support: G-1 already enforces this for closure, and CAP-09's write-paths are deliberately closed, so the invariant is already implemented twice but never stated as a general rule.

a_rows_sample.anchor: the answer is NO: on current evidence there is no distinct C-14 capability. Every stage of the policy-to-effect path is already performed by an owned capability ... What EKS-02 actually records is not a missing capability but a missing COVERAGE
a_rows_sample.statement: Original (later superseded) analysis: mapping the nine-stage policy-to-effect path (definition, derivation, evaluation, observation, admission control, blocking/halt, escalation, audit, advisory tripwires) against evidence shows every stage already performed by an owned capability (chiefly CAP-09/BC-3), so EKS-02's gap is a coverage gap within existing machinery, not a missing capability -- this categorical denial is itself withdrawn later by Amendment 1 as a category argument doing an existence test's job.

a_rows_sample.anchor: On current evidence, no platform-wide C-14 capability is established. A Tier-1 enforcement pattern exists within CAP-09, but whether that instance constitutes the same capability as C-14 remains OPEN.
a_rows_sample.statement: C-14's categorical denial is replaced by provisional wording: no platform-wide C-14 capability is established, but a Tier-1 enforcement pattern exists within CAP-09, and whether that instance is the same capability as C-14 is OQ-H, unresolved -- with four separated sub-concerns (policy tier assignment, coverage mapping, enforcement execution, enforcement assurance), each with a different owner status.

a_rows_sample.anchor: registry.yaml carries AST-007 at governance_tier ... adoption: adopted, PRE_ACTION. That is policy enforcement — mechanical, blocking, in production today.
a_rows_sample.statement: Falsifies a prior claim that C-14 policy-enforcement is 'absent': one asset (AST-007) is mechanically blocking and in production, so the correct classification is a coverage gap for the narrower C-15 claim, not an absent capability.

a_rows_sample.anchor: an enforcement capability must have a real effect path. A script that prints a warning is monitoring or advisory control, not enforcement.
a_rows_sample.statement: Distinguishes policy definition/evaluation/observation/monitoring/enforcement/admission-control/runtime-blocking/escalation/audit as separate capabilities, and defines enforcement strictly as requiring a decision point, protected operation, effect, failure mode, override model, and auditability.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The four unowned capabilities (corrected state)
a_rows_sample.statement: Records four capabilities with no bounded-context owner as one control loop (policy/knowledge DEFINED in BC-1 -> C-10 DELIVERS -> C-14 GATES -> C-19 EXPRESSES <- C-5 ATTESTS): C-5 Separation attestation (existence YES, cross-context control-plane assurance capability, NOT a bounded context); C-10 Knowledge distribution (existence NOT YET ESTABLISHED, deferred); C-14 Policy enforcement (existence CONTESTED, deferred); C-19 Communication composition (existence YES, stewardship/cross-cutting expression concern, NOT a bounded context). Flagged as a proposal finding, not adopted architecture; C-10/C-14 existence remain UNDECIDED.

b_rows_sample.anchor: INV-ATTR-2/G-2: separation is Declared, NOT attestable. No mechanism can establish who performed an act; assurance rests entirely on where the human starts the session.
b_rows_sample.statement: Finding F-4: role separation between producer, verifier, and approver is Declared, not attestable (INV-ATTR-2/G-2); no mechanism in the estate can establish who actually performed an act, so assurance rests entirely on where the human starts a session -- a capability described as C-5, separation attestation, with no owner today.

b_rows_sample.anchor: One process occupied verification -> architecture-review -> architecture-drafting -> domain roles in sequence, and in each lane recorded its own START -- a governance act -- because no separate governance process was present
b_rows_sample.statement: Finding F-9/F-9a: the drafting process itself, first-hand, occupied verification, architecture-review, architecture-drafting and domain roles in sequence within one process, self-recording its own STARTs each time -- evidence that 'Governance' as practised is a cross-cutting capability set with only ONE strictly-separated duty (acceptance/closure via COMPLETE, mechanically refused to non-governance/human writers), not a distinct actor.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Absence of a C-5-owned aggregate may disqualify a separate bounded context but must NOT be used as proof that the capability itself does not exist.
b_rows_sample.statement: Refinement applied to C-5: absence of a C-5-owned authoritative aggregate/state disqualifies it from being its own bounded context but must not be read as evidence against the capability's existence -- an existence/category conflation the original analysis had committed for C-14 most clearly.

Single-operator constraint -- six separations, distinguished explicitly: process separation, access separation, artifact isolation, independent execution, organizational independence, external attestation.
b_rows_sample.statement: C-5's separation dimensions must distinguish six kinds: process separation, access separation, artifact isolation, independent execution, organizational independence, and external attestation; organizational independence must never be treated as established in a single-operator environment.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Material participation in producing the evidence being verified? YES, and this is decisive ... my Verification #2 findings W-1...W-6 fed the correction chain that runs into this artifact's lineage
b_rows_sample.statement: An independence gate is extended beyond mere non-authorship to material participation: a verifier whose own prior findings materially shaped a later correction chain is disqualified from verifying that chain's output, even without direct authorship of the artifact under review.

b_rows_sample.statement: A unifying control-plane invariant candidate (proposed, not adopted): a gate's verdict may not be issued by the party the gate constrains; observed support: G-1 already enforces this for closure, and CAP-09's write-paths are deliberately closed, so the invariant is already implemented twice but never stated as a general rule.

b_rows_sample.anchor: two independent grounds: an ADOPTED invariant (INV-ATTR-2) that presupposes the capability, and the capability has been PERFORMED. C-10 satisfies neither limb.
b_rows_sample.statement: A two-limb existence test emerges from Amendment 1's C-5 analysis: a capability's existence is supported by (1) an ADOPTED invariant presupposing it, and/or (2) the capability having been PERFORMED at least once; C-5 satisfies both limbs (INV-ATTR-2 adopted; SB-1 clearance is a performed instance), while C-10 satisfies neither.

b_rows_sample.anchor: organizational independence NOT_ESTABLISHED (not NOT_APPLICABLE) ... in a single-operator environment organizational independence is not among the achievable separations, and it MUST NOT be represented as established.
b_rows_sample.statement: A four-state model for separation dimensions is adopted (NOT_APPLICABLE, NOT_ESTABLISHED, ESTABLISHED, EXTERNALLY_ATTESTED); organizational independence is corrected from the original 'not applicable / undefined' to NOT_ESTABLISHED, because NOT_APPLICABLE risks collapsing into PASS while NOT_ESTABLISHED correctly states a real, currently unsuppliable assurance gap.

b_rows_sample.anchor: intra-platform third-party != external attestation ... A different process under the same operator, on the same filesystem -- that is evidence of process separation, not of externality.
b_rows_sample.statement: Correction #3 adds external attestation as a sixth separation dimension at NOT_ESTABLISHED, and sharpens the distinction that a different process under the same operator establishing a fact (as Verification #3 did for SB-1) is process separation, never external attestation -- no party outside the platform has attested any separation claim in this estate.

b_rows_sample.anchor: This is C-5 -- separation attestation -- failing in production, on the very work item that is analysing it.
b_rows_sample.statement: Finding I-2, an explicit analogy: the estate's identity-attribution mechanism has produced both a false negative and a false positive on the same question within one day, on the exact work item studying separation attestation (C-5) -- framed as C-5 failing in production, recorded as evidence, with no ownership or OQ-A conclusion drawn.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Producing a fresh analysis would create a second, competing C-5 model -- while the first is mid-verification (S5 ACTIVE, outstanding). That forks the subject under assurance.
b_rows_sample.statement: Search-before-modelling (ES-005.4) applied concretely: a commission to define C-5 fresh is refused because a 922-line canonical analysis already treats C-5 across four sections, and producing a competing model while the canonical one is mid-verification would fork the subject under active assurance.

b_rows_sample.anchor: If I author this analysis I become a producer on the item I govern ... C-5 operating correctly forbids its own analysis being written by the party that governs the record it rests on. This refusal is itself C-5 evidence
b_rows_sample.statement: A self-referential separation argument: Governance for the work item refuses to author a C-5 analysis because doing so would make it a producer on the item it governs -- the exact shape of defect §4 of the provenance reconciliation had just recorded -- and the refusal is offered as a third, live instance of C-5 evidence on the very work item studying C-5.

b_rows_sample.anchor: CLASSIFICATION: HISTORICAL VERIFICATION EVIDENCE / NOT INDEPENDENT / PROVENANCE-CONFLICTED ... ca6039a8 is neither deleted nor rewritten. Its substantive findings F-1...F-7 were separately adopted as verified findings by PO/ARB act and are not disturbed by this classification
b_rows_sample.statement: A defective-provenance classification vocabulary is introduced: an artifact can be classified HISTORICAL EVIDENCE / NOT INDEPENDENT while its substantive content (findings) remains adopted and undisturbed -- only the assurance/independence claim is refused, not the content.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The platform cannot attest a specified session execution. identity binding must NOT be placed inside C-10's authoritative state, because C-10 cannot establish it. It is C-5-shaped
b_rows_sample.statement: The sharpest finding in the D3 prep: a C-10 receipt's binding to a specific session execution can never be stronger than what INV-ATTR-1/INV-ATTR-2 permit (self-declared, not attested), so identity binding cannot be placed inside C-10's authoritative state -- it is C-5-shaped, and C-5 owns no attestation record either.

b_rows_sample.anchor: ca6039a8 was reclassified as HISTORICAL EVIDENCE + NOT INDEPENDENT/PROVENANCE-CONFLICTED -- not deleted, findings intact, only its ASSURANCE STATUS refused. That is exactly the shape of receipt invalidation ... invalidation is PURPOSE-SCOPED, not global.
b_rows_sample.statement: The earlier reclassification of the AMD2 verification artifact (ca6039a8) as historical-but-not-independent is offered as a real, worked instance of what 'receipt invalidation' should look like: invalidation is purpose-scoped (it removes assurance standing while leaving the content usable as evidence), not a global deletion.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Do not import C-5's existence test automatically. Do not assume 'adopted invariant + performed capability' is a universal rule.
b_rows_sample.statement: The two-limb existence test derived from C-5's evidence (adopted invariant + performed capability) is explicitly declared not a universal rule to be imported automatically for other capabilities; C-10 must construct its own establishment test rather than inherit C-5's.

a_rows_sample.anchor: This document does NOT design the Kernel. It produces QUESTIONS, OBSERVATIONS, DISTINCTIONS, and FALSIFICATION TARGETS -- not architecture.
a_rows_sample.statement: Explicit methodological self-limitation: integrating Chinese philosophical traditions (Daoism/Confucianism/Mohism/Xunzi/Zhuangzi), Tarka-Nyaya (Annambhatta's Tarka-sangraha), and Audi's Western epistemology to interrogate assumptions underlying a minimal Knowledge Kernel produces questions/observations/distinctions/falsification targets only, explicitly not architecture or a kernel design.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Names are normative, not descriptive.
a_rows_sample.statement: Ten Chinese-tradition observations against the Kernel's Western assumptions: (1) names are normative not descriptive (Kongzi's zhengming), (2) identity is relational not intrinsic (Xunzi/Confucianism role-based identity), (3) change is continuous not discrete (Daoist hua vs discrete state transitions), (4) contradiction is not necessarily error (Zhuangzi perspectivalism: some contradictions are legitimate differing perspectives), (5) justification is practical (Mohist non-correspondence truth: a claim is true if it works), (6) context is constitutive not external (Zhuangzi/Xunzi), (7) knowing and acting are inseparable (Xunzi: knowledge as capacity not possession), (8) authority is relational/role-based (Confucianism), (9) continuity can be transformation (Zhuangzi: sameness via continuous process, not essence), (10) absence and withdrawal are different (Daoism) -- each posed as a challenge the Kernel's naming/identity/change/contradiction/justification/context/knowledge/authority/continuity/retraction treatment must answer.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Definition defects must be tested.
a_rows_sample.statement: Ten Tarka-Nyaya observations for testing the Kernel boundary: (11) a defining characteristic must avoid avyapti (under-covers), ativyapti (over-covers), asambhava (cannot apply); (12) reason must establish the conclusion via the paksa-sadhya-hetu discipline (proposition/reason/example/application/conclusion); (13) vyapti (invariable concomitance) must be tested in both directions (anvaya/vyatireka); (14) five defective reasons (savyabhicara/viruddha/satpratipaksa/asiddha/badhita) give precise argument-defect vocabulary; (15) absence claims need a counter-correlate (pratiyogi) and a specified kind of absence; (16) viparyaya (erroneous apprehension) shows representation is not truth -- the Kernel must not silently convert representation into semantic truth; (17) samsaya (doubt: mutually contradictory attributes in the same substratum) must be kept distinct from contradiction and error; (18) nigrahasthana (argument failure points) catalogs precise failure modes (abandoning/changing the proposition or reason, etc.); (19) the conclusion (nigamana) must not exceed what the premises establish; (20) abhava (negation/non-existence) has multiple types (absolute/prior/subsequent/locus-specific absence).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Justification is distinct from knowledge.
a_rows_sample.statement: Ten Audi (Western epistemology) observations: (21) justified true belief need not be knowledge (Gettier cases) -- Kernel must handle justified false beliefs differently from knowledge; (22) multiple basic sources of knowledge (perception/memory/introspection/reason/testimony) must not be collapsed; (23) direct (non-inferential) vs indirect (inferential) knowledge must both be handled; (24) justification is prima facie/defeasible (undermining and overriding defeaters); (25) knowledge does not require certainty; (26) internalism vs externalism is a real distinction the Kernel must take a position on; (27) memory preserves but does not create knowledge -- preservation vs generation must be distinguished; (28) testimony transmits knowledge via the attester's knowledge, but testimony-based justification can arise independently; (29) coherence alone is not sufficient for justification; (30) skepticism (hallucination/illusion/dreaming) challenges knowledge claims -- the Kernel must handle uncertainty/fallibility without collapsing into skepticism.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The 10 Strongest Falsification Questions
a_rows_sample.statement: Ten falsification questions posed against any Kernel boundary claim, five from Chinese traditions (how does the Kernel determine a unit of knowledge is no longer 'the same'; how is continuity maintained across change; does naming prescribe or merely label; is context internal or external to a claim's truth; does justification depend on practical consequences) and five from Tarka-Nyaya (does the boundary definition suffer avyapti/ativyapti/asambhava; is every claimed invariant tested in both anvaya and vyatireka directions; what is the counter-correlative if 'retraction does not exist as a Kernel state'; does any claimed capability exceed its premises; has an argument's reason changed shape mid-debate without being recorded).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Names prescribe what things should be, not just name what they are.
a_rows_sample.statement: Five most-surprising observations: normative naming (names prescribe, not just classify); contradictions are not necessarily errors (perspectival difference vs logical inconsistency); absence != withdrawal (a claim no longer existing vs no longer assertable); knowing is becoming, not possessing; the smallest boundary may be defined by what it must NOT include (per Tarka's ativyapti/asambhava tests).

a_rows_sample.anchor: The 5 Observations Most Likely to Be Relevant to a Minimal Knowledge Kernel
a_rows_sample.statement: Five observations ranked most relevant to a minimal Knowledge Kernel: identity is relational not intrinsic; justification is practical (consequence-based, not merely internal-consistency-based); change is continuous (versioning/state management must handle continuous transformation, not just discrete states); context is constitutive (must be internal to knowledge representation, not external metadata); naming is normative (must be handled as part of the knowledge itself).

a_rows_sample.anchor: The Observations That Should NOT Influence Architecture Without Further Evidence
a_rows_sample.statement: Five observations explicitly flagged as not (yet) architecturally actionable: Daoism's claim that 'the Dao that can be named is not the enduring Dao' (not directly relevant -- the kernel must name things regardless); Confucian ritual (li) emphasis (unclear translation to a kernel); Mohism's claim that impartiality requires active effort (ethical claim, unclear architectural implication); 'knowledge changes as it is used' (unclear how to model without further investigation); Tarka's full nigrahasthana catalog (more detailed than a minimal kernel needs -- core attacks on definition/reason/vyapti/fallacious-reason are more immediately applicable).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Questions That Conventional DDD Analysis May Not Expose
a_rows_sample.statement: Ten questions conventional DDD analysis may not expose: whether bounded contexts/boundaries are actually stable or shift with context; whether identity is a relation rather than an aggregate property; whether names are normative rather than stable identifiers; whether contradiction can be a legitimate perspective difference rather than an error; whether justification is fundamentally practical/consequence-based rather than internal; whether context is constitutive of knowledge rather than external; whether knowledge is a capacity ('becoming') rather than a possession; whether absence has multiple types rather than being uniform non-existence; whether 'retraction' is a continuous process rather than a deletion event; whether certainty is required for knowledge at all.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Questions That Chinese Philosophy Does NOT Help Answer
a_rows_sample.statement: Explicit scope limitation: Chinese philosophy provides no help on formal modeling, implementation (APIs/data structures/algorithms), performance/scalability/reliability, UX, integration with existing systems, security, data persistence/storage/versioning, distributed-systems/network-topology questions, temporal modeling, or computational complexity -- it offers distinctions and observations, not a modeling language.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Separation of Grounds
a_rows_sample.statement: A four-tier separation-of-grounds discipline is applied throughout: Historically Grounded Observation (direct textual claims from Daodejing/Zhuangzi/Kongzi/Mohist fa/Xunzi/Tarka-sangraha/Audi), Philosophical Interpretation (what those claims imply), Architectural Inference (what a Kernel would need to account for under that interpretation), and Speculation (extensions beyond the source material, e.g. how a Kernel might implement Confucian role-based justification or Daoist continuous transformation) -- kept explicitly distinct.

a_rows_sample.anchor: These are not questions about missing capabilities. They are questions about the assumptions the Kernel makes about the nature of knowledge itself.
a_rows_sample.statement: Final consolidated set of 15 architect-facing questions (naming as neutral vs normative; identity as property vs relation; contradiction as error vs perspective; context as external vs constitutive; justification as claim-property vs practical relationship; retraction as event vs process; transformation as discrete vs continuous; absence as single state vs typed (abhava); knowledge as possession vs capacity; authority as source-property vs relationship; whether boundary reasoning is established via paksa-sadhya-hetu or assumed; whether invariants are tested in both anvaya/vyatireka directions; whether representation is silently converted into truth; whether the knowledge/non-knowledge boundary is stable or provisional; whether impartial evaluation is a default or an active achievement) -- framed explicitly as questions about the Kernel's assumptions about the nature of knowledge itself, not about missing capabilities.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The S1-F018 mapping is no longer merely a candidate... the dilemma therefore demands an external-but-atomic member -- and that is precisely asambhava: a definition describing something that cannot exist under the Constitution. So Session 1's inference is corroborated from a source it did not have... POSSIBLE INDEPENDENT ARRIVAL -- third in the register.
a_rows_sample.statement: S1-F023's self-labelled inference that S1-F018's Entity/Value-Object dilemma is an asambhava case (a definition describing something that cannot exist) is independently corroborated: S2-R-F018.1 established from law (not from the Tarka taxonomy) that the dilemma's option set omits the route the law actually takes -- EvidenceLinks as a bounded Collection of external-content references under C-3 -- which is exactly an external-but-atomic member the dilemma's options cannot represent; recorded as a possible independent arrival (third in the review series's register).

Note: S1-F023's nine-family falsification instrument derived from the Tarka-sangraha, designed to run post-adjudication against any candidate Kernel definition; the corpus built it but Session 1 records it was never actually run. Related to but a later, more developed artifact than chinese-tarka-audi-kernel-falsification-lens (S0405, B0011) and nyaya-sutra-kernel-falsification-lens (S0407, B0011).

a_rows_sample.anchor: CR-4 FALSIFIED -- TYPE 2, editorial ... 'I would not call it general semantic equivalence ... closer to K1 approx_{Q,Gamma,O} K2 = contextual observational equivalence.' ... [NEG] A naming correction is not a substantive theory blocker. REMOVED.
a_rows_sample.statement: Section 11: falsifies the CR-4 semantic-equivalence multiplicity claim as merely editorial -- the corpus already contains its own correction that the executable CLOSURE-4 tester actually defines a different, narrower relation (approx_obs, contextual observational equivalence K1 approx_{Q,Gamma,O} K2) rather than general semantic equivalence (equiv_sem), already classified in a prior register as 'not conflicting -- mis-slotted'; removed as a blocker.

a_rows_sample.anchor: ⭐⭐ Consequence for my own plan. CR-4 is filed there as ... 'cheapest — the corpus already contains its own repair' and 'nearly self-resolving'. On this evidence it is a three-way conflict in which one option collapses a distinction another was created to protect, and a second carries a standing 'too strong' review. a_rows_sample.statement: Corrects the investigation's own prior CR-4 disposition (from a previous batch's cr4-equiv-sem-falsified-editorial finding, filed as 'cheapest -- the corpus already contains its own repair', 'nearly self-resolving'): given the newly-found three-way conflict, CR-4 is actually a genuine decision problem where one candidate solution (A) would collapse a distinction another structure (C) was specifically built to protect, and a second candidate (B, CLOSURE-4) carries a standing peer-review verdict of 'too strong' -- so CR-4 is NOT the cheapest of the corpus's five conflict records. Notes CLOSURE-4 is proposed by CR-4 to fill the 'approx_obs' slot while definition A uses an observational criterion to define 'equiv_sem' itself -- two different proposals independently filling different slots of the same 7-tuple with the same kind of content, which is the collapse arriving by two separate routes. Explicitly names this the SECOND misclassification found in the investigator's own forward plan in one day (after D1), noting both errors run the same way: a genuine decision problem filed as cheap/mechanical because its true multiplicity had not yet been enumerated.

b_rows_sample.anchor: At least the following relations must be separated: = representation/structural equality; ≡ semantic equality; ≈ observational equivalence; ≅_I identity equivalence; ≅_P provenance-sensitive equivalence; ≅_H historical equivalence.
b_rows_sample.statement: The overloaded notation K1=K2 is decomposed into (at least) six distinct relations that must not be conflated: structural equality (=), semantic equality (equiv), observational equivalence (approx), identity equivalence (cong_I), provenance-sensitive equivalence (cong_P), and historical equivalence (cong_H); the corpus is said to explicitly record the first four distinctions and warn they are not interchangeable.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Same proposition ⇏ Same evidence identity. ... two observations can concern the same proposition while remaining distinct evidence objects.
b_rows_sample.statement: Preserved historical result: identity is not equality — two evidence objects e1,e2 can both support the same proposition p (Supports(e1,p) and Supports(e2,p)) without e1=e2; this affects provenance, deduplication, replay, validation, audit and merge, and is attributed to an earlier corpus reconstruction rather than newly derived here.

b_rows_sample.anchor: x =_str y iff their representations are structurally identical. ... =_str ≠ semantic equality unless the representation has already been proven canonical.
b_rows_sample.statement: Structural equality x=_str y (representations structurally identical) is computationally convenient but is warned to not equal semantic equality unless the representation is already proven canonical — two structurally different representations can denote the same semantic state.

b_rows_sample.anchor: x ≡_sem y iff Semantics(x)=Semantics(y). ... Semantic equality is conceptually appropriate, but currently underdefined.
b_rows_sample.statement: Semantic equality x equiv_sem y is defined via a semantic interpretation function Sem:Representation->Meaning being equal on x and y, but is flagged as not computationally decidable while Sem itself remains formally undefined — conceptually appropriate but currently underdefined.

b_rows_sample.anchor: H1 ≈ H2 iff every permitted observation produces the same result: ∀O∈𝒪: O(H1)=O(H2). ... This is the relation already underlying Step 260's behavioral quotient.
b_rows_sample.statement: Observational equivalence for histories (H1 approx H2 iff every permitted observation O produces the same result) and for states (K1 approx K2 iff every permitted state observation agrees) is identified as the same relation already underlying Step 260's behavioral quotient; notably it does not require internal representations to be identical.

b_rows_sample.anchor: SameId(x,y) ... Identity tracks denotation; equality compares values. This formulation is a reconstruction, not yet a corpus-proven final definition.
b_rows_sample.statement: Identity (SameId(x,y)) answers whether two references denote the same domain object, independent of value equality: x=_str y can hold with SameId false (two separately created records with identical content but distinct observations), and SameId can hold while representations differ (the same domain object having evolved) — 'identity tracks denotation; equality compares values', explicitly flagged as a reconstruction, not a corpus-proven final definition.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Historical equality asks: Are these states the same point or condition in an evolution history? ... Semantic equality ⇏ Historical equality.
b_rows_sample.statement: Historical equality asks whether two states are the same point in an evolution history, distinct from current semantic equality: K0 -Revise-> K1 can have K0 equiv_sem K1 (representation changed, semantics didn't) while K0 !=_H K1 (distinct historical states) — semantic equality does not imply historical equality; matters especially for Replay and audit.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Provenance is semantically relevant: K1 ≢ K2. Provenance is metadata only: K1 ≡ K2. ... equality cannot be resolved until the theory determines which information is semantically essential. This is a key dependency for Step 265.
b_rows_sample.statement: Provenance equality is genuinely ambiguous: given K1={p,e1}, K2={p,e2} with e1!=e2 both supporting p, either provenance is semantically relevant (K1 not-equiv K2) or metadata only (K1 equiv K2); the earlier corpus is said to identify this ambiguity explicitly and conclude it cannot be resolved until the theory determines which information is semantically essential — flagged as a key dependency for Step 265 (provenance placement).

b_rows_sample.anchor: No universal equality hierarchy has yet been proven. ... Identity and Provenance equality are independent dimensions.
b_rows_sample.statement: A candidate implication chain (structural => semantic => observational equivalence) is proposed but explicitly not declared universally valid without further assumptions; identity and provenance equality are treated as independent dimensions from this chain; current position: no universal equality hierarchy has yet been proven.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Explicit assertion membership ≠ semantic entailment. ... a∈_exp K ... K⊨a ... Stored fact ≠ logically derived fact.
b_rows_sample.statement: Membership in an assertion-based state K is typed into explicit assertion membership (a in_exp K, a is literally one of K's stored assertions) versus semantic consequence (K models a, semantically entailed but not necessarily stored) — a proposed formal distinction (not yet a theorem) preventing the category error of treating a stored fact as identical to a logically derived one; flagged as essential for Step 262's assertion type.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Merge equality: semantic + identity + provenance dependent. Exact final semantics remain unresolved.
b_rows_sample.statement: Operation test — Merge: Merge(K1,K2) cannot be specified using structural equality alone, since a1=(p,e1) and a2=(p,e2) sharing proposition p could legitimately merge to {a1,a2} (kept separate) or to a single combined-evidence assertion depending on ontology; Merge equality is semantic+identity+provenance dependent, with exact final semantics unresolved.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Supersession requires identity/version distinction. ... collapsing them under semantic equality would destroy the very relation x2 ≻ x1.
b_rows_sample.statement: Operation test — Supersede: if Meaning(x1)=Meaning(x2) but Identity(x1)!=Identity(x2) and x2 supersedes x1, collapsing x1,x2 under semantic equality would destroy the supersession relation x2 succ x1 itself; supersession therefore requires an identity/version distinction, strongly suggesting semantic equality alone cannot serve as the sole equality relation.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Replay requires historical identity/equality independent of current state equality. ... Replay(H1)=K and Replay(H2)=K yet H1 ≠_H H2.
b_rows_sample.statement: Operation test — Replay: two distinct histories H1,H2 (H1 !=_H H2) can replay to the same current state K (Replay(H1)=Replay(H2)=K); Replay is treated by the corpus as a history/audit operation rather than another state transformation, and requires historical identity/equality independent of current-state equality.

b_rows_sample.anchor: | Operation | Structural equality | Semantic equality | Identity | Historical equality | Provenance | Current assessment | Merge...Supersede...Replay...Remove...Revise...Deduplicate...Validate
b_rows_sample.statement: The full operation/equality matrix across Merge, Supersede, Replay, Remove, Revise, Deduplicate, Validate rates each of structural/semantic/identity/historical/provenance equality as insufficient, required, relevant, potentially-required, or context-dependent per operation, with every row's overall status UNRESOLVED, NORMATIVE/DOMAIN-DEPENDENT (Deduplicate), or 'Assessment relation' (Validate); Remove requires identity for correct object targeting (must not remove a2 when removing a1 despite structural identity), Revise cannot use semantic equality as its sole target selector (must not implicitly revise x2 when revising x1 despite x1 equiv_sem x2), Deduplicate cannot be specified until its preservation policy is known (structural/semantic/identity/provenance criteria can each give different results), and Validate shows semantic state equality does not imply identical validation results because validation is a relation over (K,E) pairs, not K alone — reinforcing that not every operation is a state transformation T:K->K.

b_rows_sample.anchor: No single equality relation is adequate for all KnowledgeOS operations. ... KnowledgeOS requires a typed family of relations.
b_rows_sample.statement: Major correction to the kernel concept: rejects the implicit assumption 'KnowledgeOS needs one equality operator', replacing it with 'KnowledgeOS requires a typed family of relations' (=_str, equiv_sem, approx_obs, SameId, equiv_H, equiv_P) that may be connected by formally established implications but must not be conflated.

b_rows_sample.anchor: K1 ≡_K K2 ⟺ ∀O∈𝒪_K: O(K1)=O(K2) ... 𝒪_K is not yet completely closed. Therefore this is a candidate formal definition, not a completed theorem.
b_rows_sample.statement: Candidate formal definition of Knowledge-State equality as purely observational/behavioral: K1 equiv_K K2 iff every permitted state observation O in the (not-yet-closed) set O_K agrees on K1 and K2; explicitly a candidate, not a completed theorem, because O_K is not yet closed.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Equality → Congruence → Quotient → Minimality. This is the correct dependency direction.
b_rows_sample.statement: If K1 equiv_K K2 (no permitted observation distinguishes them) and all mandatory operations preserve that equivalence, equiv_K becomes the congruence relation needed for the minimal quotient K*=H/equiv (Step 260) — establishing the dependency direction Equality -> Congruence -> Quotient -> Minimality as correct.

b_rows_sample.anchor: the observation set is not fully closed; the operation registry is not fully closed; provenance placement remains unresolved; assertion semantics remain unresolved; temporal semantics remain unresolved; identity semantics remain unresolved. The governing prompt explicitly says that final kernel sele
b_rows_sample.statement: Explicit refusal to overclaim equiv_K as final: six named open dependencies remain (observation-set closure, operation-registry closure, provenance placement, assertion semantics, temporal semantics, identity semantics); the governing prompt is cited as requiring final kernel selection to halt while equality remains ambiguous, and this gate is obeyed.

b_rows_sample.anchor: bounded contexts may legitimately require different relations: same assertion / same evidence / same domain identity / same version / same semantic meaning / same observable state ... PRIMARY KEY must therefore not automatically be interpreted as SemanticIdentity. ... content hash must not automatic
b_rows_sample.statement: DDD interpretation: rather than one generic 'Equality' concept used everywhere, different bounded contexts legitimately require different named relations (same assertion, same evidence, same domain identity, same version, same semantic meaning, same observable state); a database PRIMARY KEY must not automatically be interpreted as SemanticIdentity, and a content hash must not automatically become DomainIdentity.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 𝔎=(K,=_str,≡_sem,≈_obs,SameId,≡_H,≡_P). The next question is not 'Which one is the equality?' It is 'Which relation is the appropriate congruence relation for each operation and which relation defines semantic equality of Knowledge States?'
b_rows_sample.statement: Mathematical reframing: KnowledgeOS's state carries a relational structure 𝔎=(K,=_str,equiv_sem,approx_obs,SameId,equiv_H,equiv_P) rather than a single equality; the research question shifts from 'which relation is THE equality' to 'which relation is the appropriate congruence for each operation, and which defines semantic equality of Knowledge States'.

b_notations: K1 equiv_K K2 iff forall O in O_K: O(K1)=O(K2)

group_evidence.why_grouped: labels share the notation 'equiv_sem'

a_rows_sample.anchor: Repaired in 6 of 6 contradiction-bearing cases -- and under all three contradiction models, because the boundary records the conflict regardless of which value the model assigns to it. ... This CORRECTS my own Experiment G conclusion.
a_rows_sample.statement: Confirms that defining closure over the boundary B rather than the value repairs D-0 (contradiction-invisible-to-Zero) in 6 of 6 tested cases under all three contradiction models, explicitly correcting Experiment G's earlier claim that the contradiction-codomain choice and the closure question could not be separated.

a_rows_sample.anchor: the four Zero readings are not total over the value domain ... Any value outside {top,bot,U} is invisible to every reading, and every reading CLOSES on it. ... a contradictory state is declared epistemically closed.
a_rows_sample.statement: D-0: re-running Phase D under three-valued/four-valued/delegated contradiction models produces identical Zero readings across all seven suite cases, but the identical result is itself a defect -- none of strict/weak/reasoned/Kleene can see any value outside {top,bot,U}, so a contradictory state closes under every reading.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Boundary closure is identical across all three contradiction models -- CONFIRMED. Choosing among three-valued / four-valued / delegated is unnecessary for closure, which removes a blocker Experiment G had declared load-bearing.
a_rows_sample.statement: Re-confirms with the typed vocabulary (who-can-act derived from type, not free text) that boundary-based Zero closure is invariant across all three contradiction models, reconfirming Artifact I's earlier finding at higher rigor.

a_rows_sample.anchor: D-0's agreement was attributed to the readings testing only F and U. True but incomplete. The models are separable in isolation — one unrelated U anywhere in the state masks the difference completely, in any bucket.
a_rows_sample.statement: Corrects and sharpens D-0's earlier finding: the models ARE separable in isolation, but one unrelated U anywhere in the epistemic state masks the difference completely in any bucket, because Zero_weak/Zero_kleene are existential quantifiers that absorb at U; with 5 of 8 Sat_c classes non-executable, this masking saturation is the normal regime, not an edge case -- the sixth instance of the recurring projection-vs-structure diagnosis, and the first found in the readings rather than a value or metric.

Validates the Zero Lens claim UNKNOWN≠ABSENT with a concrete formal witness: if Contr(p) and NoAssessment(p) both map to U, the representation has collapsed two semantically distinct situations, and this Representation_Collapse(Contr,Unknown) is now measurable.

Gives the precise masking-mechanism table: models are separable (2 distinct reading profiles) when zero other requirements are at U, but become inseparable (1 profile) as soon as even one other requirement is at U, regardless of its bucket -- caused by Zero_weak/Zero_kleene being existential quantifiers over the state (absorbing at the first U encountered), which Zero_reasoned inherits through Zero_weak; since 5 of 8 Sat classes are non-executable, saturation is the normal regime, not the edge case, meaning the contradiction-model choice is unobservable in exactly the regime KnowledgeOS actually occupies.

a_rows_sample.anchor:
| `Contradiction ⇒ ¬Zero` | **FALSE** |
| `Zero_weak` on a contradictory state, under **A** and **B** | **closes** (`true`) |...> `[NEG]` **NEG-7. Contradiction does not merely fail to imply Zero — under both A and B a contradictory state CLOSES.**
a_rows_sample.statement: Tests Zero interaction directly rather than assuming it: Contradiction does NOT imply not-Zero (false), and under both A and B, Zero_weak on a contradictory state actually closes (true) -- NEG-7, stronger than originally anticipated: contradiction doesn't merely fail to imply Zero, it actively produces closure. This reproduces D-0 in a new setting, confirming it is not an artifact of one model, and connects to KR-CONTR-MODELS' finding that the readings saturate.

a_rows_sample.anchor: > `[EXP]` **`Zero` cannot be defined before evaluation semantics are expressive enough to answer "`U` because *what*?"** The dependency is **`Sat → Zero`**, never the reverse.
a_rows_sample.statement: Retrospectively explains why Zero resisted definition: the old Zero(K,I,EC)⟺Δ=∅ was underspecified because Sat itself was -- when Sat(r)=U one must ask 'U because what?' since U_unobservable is epistemically different from U_not-assessed; the dependency is Sat->Zero, never the reverse, confirmed from two independent directions (this experiment's §8, and KR-CONTR-MODELS §6's saturation finding).

b_rows_sample.anchor: > **What evaluation structure is minimally required to preserve the distinctions the KnowledgeOS programme has already declared important?**
b_rows_sample.statement: W-KR-CONTR-2026-09 reframes the Contr question from 'three vs four values' to the deeper question of what evaluation structure is minimally required to preserve the programme's already-declared-important distinctions.

b_rows_sample.anchor: * Candidate A — fourth value: **7/12** * Candidate B — delegation: **7/12** * Candidate C — exclusive construction: **7/12** * Candidate D — structured evaluation: **12/12**
b_rows_sample.statement: Reports the core scoring result: A/B/C each pass only 7/12 required distinctions, failing on the identical seven; D (structured evaluation) passes all 12. The seven common failures collapse the unknown family (Unobservable≡InsufficientEvidence≡Underdetermined≡TheoryIncomplete≡...→U), meaning adding a contradiction value does not address distinctions lying outside the contradiction dimension.

b_rows_sample.anchor:
$$
\chi(G)=3.
$$... **Given this particular required-distinction set and this adequacy criterion, at least three distinguishable flat classes are required.**
b_rows_sample.statement: The experiment turns adequacy into a graph-coloring/injectivity problem over the required-distinction graph, finding chromatic number chi(G)=3; carefully qualified: this does not establish the correct evaluation domain has three values, only that at least three distinguishable flat classes are required given this distinction set and adequacy criterion -- and separately, nine 'no determinate value' conditions cannot be adequately represented by any flat value domain regardless of cardinality, making the obstruction structural rather than cardinal.

States a methodological principle from the chromatic-number finding: colourability only proves pairwise coding capacity under the chosen abstraction, it does not establish that resulting values carry the required semantic or operational meaning -- cardinality sufficiency is not semantic adequacy.

b_rows_sample.anchor:
$$
\min |\text{representation}|=2
$$

with the two minimum representations: $$
\{\text{value},\text{reason}\}
$$

and $$
\{\text{polarity},\text{reason}\}.
$$

And: **reason is indispensable.**
b_rows_sample.statement: The exhaustive minimum-representation search finds min|representation|=2, with two minimum representations {value,reason} and {polarity,reason}, establishing that reason is indispensable -- evaluation outcome is not value alone, EVal=(v,r) is the minimum representation found in the tested search space, kept explicitly [EXP]/[PROP] not a new KnowledgeOS primitive.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Candidate C maps contradiction to `T`. Yet it passes invariants I1–I5. Why? Because those invariants test contradiction against the **unknown family**, rather than against satisfaction itself.
b_rows_sample.statement: Candidate C (exclusive construction) maps Contradiction to T (Satisfied) yet passes invariants I1-I5, because those invariants only test Contr≠Unknown-family, not Contr≠Satisfied -- exposing a genuine coverage gap in the invariant suite itself, not merely a bad candidate; proposes I11: Contr≠Satisfied as a legitimate but not-yet-ratified [PROP] test-protocol addition, explicitly preserving the historical conflict (I1-I5 pass, capability guard fails) rather than retroactively declaring the suite complete.

b_rows_sample.anchor:
### R_A

The first implementation unfairly returned `T` for theory-incomplete/uninterpreted cases... ### E7

The literal `"C"` detector accidentally matched context identifiers such as `C1/C2`.
b_rows_sample.statement: Records two implementation self-corrections during the experiment: R_A, an initial implementation unfairly returned T for theory-incomplete/uninterpreted cases, corrected so all nine no-determinate-value conditions return U; E7, a literal 'C' contradiction detector accidentally matched context identifiers like C1/C2, corrected -- both classified as test-implementation defects, not candidate properties, caught by investigating rather than forcing expected results (E9).

b_rows_sample.anchor: > **The experiment does not support representing contradiction as a distinguished scalar evaluation value. The tested adequacy requirement is satisfied by a structured representation in which at least one reason-like dimension is indispensable. The precise evaluation semantics, including the role of contradiction, remains OPEN.**
b_rows_sample.statement: States the accepted formulation of the current Contr finding: the experiment does not support representing contradiction as a distinguished scalar value; a structured representation with an indispensable reason-like dimension satisfies the tested adequacy requirement; the precise evaluation semantics including contradiction's role remains OPEN -- explicitly weaker and safer than 'structured evaluation is the answer', since D is the surviving candidate, not yet the final theory.
