a_rows_sample.statement: Identity-family validation decisions: INV-KOS-002 STRONG (reproduced 3x, two-X LLM comparison) -> KERNEL, SURVIVES (Adopted Core law 1); H-KOS-Context-001 STRONG saturation -> KERNEL, SURVIVES/CONSOLIDATE with Context-002 into law 1; H-KOS-Context-002 STRONG saturation (Avacchedaka) -> KERNEL(principle)+REPRESENTATION(the tuple), SURVIVES (see Special Area A); H-KOS-Relationship-001 STRONG (SS30 fundamental discovery, Tripuji trinity) -> KERNEL, SURVIVES (laws 1+10); H-KOS-Relation-001 STRONG (hypergraph corroboration, C-6) -> KERNEL(principle)+REPRESENTATION(graph), SURVIVES -- the principle constitutional, the graph an expression layer.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Avacchedaka -- Ruling: both -- the principle is universal; the device is a modelling technique.
a_rows_sample.statement: Special Area A ruling: a claim without its delimiting conditions over-applies (the bounded-context violation, DDD 'same data shape != same concept') -- this corruption is not domain-specific, it is the definition of meaning-loss, so the principle is Universal; the formal delimiting-conditions tuple (Entity.Property.Context.Relation.Time.Authority) is a REPRESENTATION technique, one way among several to express the boundary, not itself a kernel law. Consequence: the principle enters the Adopted Core (law 1); the tuple is deferred to REPRESENTATION.

a_rows_sample.anchor: the HPA's five strongest validation decisions are carried into the core unchanged: Similarity != Identity ... Avacchedaka ... Abhava ... LLM boundary ... deferred mechanisms
a_rows_sample.statement: The decision explicitly re-affirms P5's five strongest validation rulings unchanged: Similarity != Identity is the decisive failure test (an epistemic identity law, not a database decision); Avacchedaka -- principle constitutional, tuple = representation; Abhava -- requirement constitutional, taxonomy = mechanism; the LLM boundary -- only two fundamental absences (persistent epistemic identity + historical belief evolution); deferred mechanisms (validation engines, debate pipeline, lifecycle stages, evidence schemas, context tuples, epistemic graphs, TMS/AGM/type/topology) remain outside the kernel.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Context-001 -> Context-002 (law 1's context clause): Context is part of identity: a knowledge object carries its delimiting conditions (its semantic frame) and is never valid beyond them.
a_rows_sample.statement: Decision 2b: H-KOS-Context-001 (semantic frame preservation) and H-KOS-Context-002 (Avacchedaka, delimiting conditions) are ruled to be the same constitutional content -- 'meaning requires its boundary' -- and render as one clause of the Identity Law with final frozen wording. Rows rendered: H-KOS-Context-001, H-KOS-Context-002; the delimiting-conditions tuple (Entity.Property.Context.Relation.Time.Authority) remains a deferred REPRESENTATION technique -- the principle is the law, the tuple is one way to express it.

group_evidence.why_grouped: labels co-occur in the same contribution's labels[] 3 separate times across the corpus

a_rows_sample.anchor: Jñāna : (K_t,\;Doubt_t) \rightarrow (K_{t+1},\;Doubt_{t+1})
a_rows_sample.statement: From the closing verses (knowledge as a weapon that cuts doubt arising from ignorance): models Jnana not as a primitive/object but as a transformation operator J:(K_t,Doubt_t)->(K_{t+1},Doubt_{t+1}), with intended effect Doubt_{t+1}<Doubt_t under appropriate conditions -- reinforcing the earlier Jnana~delta interpretation over Jnana=Knowledge. Also formalizes Ajnana->Samsaya->Jnana->Buddhi->Karma as a candidate kernel cycle: ignorance->doubt->investigation->knowledge->discrimination->decision->action->new observation->updated K_t.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Zero \neq Doubt ... "I don't know X." -> Zero ... "I have two conflicting claims about X." -> Samsaya
a_rows_sample.statement: Explicitly separates five concepts previously at risk of conflation: Zero (detection of missing/absent knowledge, 'I don't know X'); Samsaya/doubt (unresolved epistemic uncertainty, 'I have two conflicting claims about X'); Ajnana (lack/absence of understanding); Jnana (knowledge/transformation that resolves or transforms uncertainty, 'evidence establishes claim A'); Buddhi (discrimination/decision capability, 'therefore accept A'). Zero != Doubt is proposed as an excellent candidate for formalization.

a_rows_sample.anchor: K_t=(X_t,\Sigma_t,\Pi_t,\Gamma_t,\Delta_t)
a_rows_sample.statement: Proposes KnowledgeOS is not fundamentally a set (beyond K_t subset K): a five-component knowledge state K_t=(X_t,Sigma_t,Pi_t,Gamma_t,Delta_t) where X_t=represented knowledge content, Sigma_t=epistemic quality/state dimensions, Pi_t=provenance, Gamma_t=context/constraints, Delta_t=detected gaps/uncertainties, with kernel transitions K_{t+1}=F(K_t,O_t,B_t,A_t) -- assessed as a much richer mathematical object than K_t subset K alone.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Content equality? ... Epistemic equality? ... Provenance-sensitive equality? ... Behavioural equality?
a_rows_sample.statement: Explicitly connects Chapter 4's doubt/knowledge/lineage material to the Step 287 open equality problem K_1 equiv K_2, posing four distinct candidate readings: content equality (X_1=X_2); epistemic equality (Sigma_1=Sigma_2); provenance-sensitive equality ((X_1,Pi_1) cong_lambda (X_2,Pi_2)); behavioural equality (delta(K_1,o)=delta(K_2,o) for all o). States plainly that Chapter 4 gives philosophical motivation for asking this question but does not provide the mathematical answer -- Step 287's OPEN status remains correct.

Constructs a five-operator formal algebra: Omega:W->O (observe), Q:O->E (qualify), J:ExK->K' (know/transform), B:K'xC->D (discriminate), A:D->W' (act), with explicit composition K_{t+1}=J(Q(Omega(W_t)),K_t), D_t=B(K_{t+1},C_t), W_{t+1}=A(D_t,W_t). Proposes working kernel definition Kernel=(K_t,Omega,Q,J,B,A,Delta,Sigma,Pi) with central transition K_t --Omega,Q--> E_t --J--> K'_t --B--> D_t --A--> W_{t+1} --Omega--> K_{t+1}, explicitly non-canonical pending formal validation. Frames Chapter 4's strongest contribution as a theory of what the kernel DOES with knowledge (Knowledge->discrimination->decision->action->new state), not another primitive.

a_rows_sample.anchor: freeze a KERNEL-CANDIDATE-v1 consisting of only \{K_t,\;Zero,\;Sa\d{m}śaya,\;Jñāna,\;Buddhi,\;Decision,\;Action\}
a_rows_sample.statement: Recommends, before simulating the whole Gita-KnowledgeOS system, freezing a minimal KERNEL-CANDIDATE-v1 = {K_t, Zero, Samsaya, Jnana, Buddhi, Decision, Action} and mathematically testing operators J, B, A, Omega, Q for closure, typing, identity, composition, reversibility, monotonicity, and information loss -- explicit caution that the source's religious claims must not be converted into technical claims by analogy alone; the strongest candidates are those independently derivable from KnowledgeOS per Step 286. Chapter 4 generates and corroborates hypotheses; it does not ratify the kernel.

b_rows_sample.anchor: KnowledgeOS Kernel = the smallest unit capable of epistemic state transition
b_rows_sample.statement: Central hypothesis: KnowledgeOS Kernel = the smallest unit capable of epistemic state transition, not merely the smallest unit that stores knowledge. Kernel = (State, Transition Capability): the state is what the kernel currently holds, the transition capability determines what can legitimately happen to that state. Gita lens (analytical, not DDD names): Mind -> evolving epistemic state, Buddhi -> discriminative capability, Karma -> action/transition, Phala -> resulting state/outcome.

b_rows_sample.anchor: K = (K_t,\Omega_K)
b_rows_sample.statement: Candidate kernel K=(K_t,Omega_K) with 11 candidate operations, each carrying a load-bearing distinction: (1) Observe(O_t) with O_t != K_t (observation is not automatically knowledge, preserving W->O->E and Qualify); (2) Discriminate(K_t,O_t)->{d_1..d_n} = the Buddhi operation, meaning 'distinguish', not yet 'decide truth'; (3) Qualify(x,E,C,t,Pi), the G1 unresolved operation, whose result may be {admit,reject,defer,qualify} rather than binary {true,false}; (4) Incorporate: K_{t+1}=Incorporate(K_t,p), a state transformation not simple insertion; (5) Reject(K_t,p) with Reject != Prove False (a proposition can be rejected as insufficiently qualified without being established false); (6) Contradict: recognizing p _|_ q via the corpus's Relation primitive; (7) Revise(K_t,p,E) for evidence-conflicting knowledge, with explicit warning not to import AGM revision theory merely because it exists, per Step 287; (8) Supersede: p_1 supersedes p_2 while preserving lineage; (9) Recall(K_t,h)/Remember distinguishing currently-known from historically-known, with K_t != H_K (history of states/transitions); (10) Withdraw(p): K_t -> K_{t+1} with withdraw != delete history (the historical fact of having held it may remain, important for auditability); (11) Act/Transform(a), external to the epistemic state per Command != Transformation != Result and Step 285's finding that Action, Event, Policy were external to the verification projection.

b_rows_sample.anchor: \delta:(K_t,O_t,C_t)\rightarrow K_{t+1} ... only when the transition satisfies the kernel's invariants
b_rows_sample.statement: The kernel should not be an unrestricted machine: reject delta:KxO->K as an unrestricted transition function; instead delta:(K_t,O_t,C_t)->K_{t+1} only when the transition satisfies the kernel's invariants. Kernel operation = candidate transition + discrimination + qualification + state transition, subject to constraints. Motivated by the 'mind can become its own enemy' observation made mathematically useful.

b_rows_sample.anchor: \Omega_K = \{\operatorname{Discriminate},\operatorname{Qualify},\operatorname{Transition}\}
b_rows_sample.statement: Speculative minimal-algebra hypothesis: Omega_K = {Discriminate, Qualify, Transition} might suffice, with Accept/Reject/Revise/Supersede as specialized transition types -- explicitly flagged 'we should not assume this minimality', proposed as a mathematical question to attack rather than an established result.

b_rows_sample.anchor: KnowledgeOS Kernel: the smallest bounded epistemic mechanism that maintains a time-indexed knowledge state and can discriminate and perform legitimate transitions of that state under the applicable constraints.
b_rows_sample.statement: Provisional formal kernel definition: K = (K_t, Omega_K, I) where K_t = current knowledge state, Omega_K = permitted kernel operations, I = kernel invariants; K_t --omega in Omega_K--> K_{t+1} only if I(K_t,omega,K_{t+1})=true. Gita gives only the philosophical lens Mind~Kernel, Buddhi~discriminative capability; the mathematical/DDD investigation determines the actual kernel. Key research hypothesis: Kernel != Knowledge Store, but potentially Kernel = Epistemic State + Discrimination + Legitimate State Transition.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Step 291 — KnowledgeOS Kernel and Operation Algebra
b_rows_sample.statement: Proposes next research step 'Step 291 -- KnowledgeOS Kernel and Operation Algebra' with 12 questions: minimal kernel definition; whether K_t is the kernel state or the kernel holds additional state; minimal Omega_K; which operations are genuinely epistemic vs belong outside (Governance, Authority, Action, Replay); whether Discriminate is primitive or composite; what Qualify consumes/produces; whether every legitimate K_t->K_{t+1} transition can be classified; determinism of the transition; which invariants must never be violated; whether the operation algebra can be proven minimal; which parts are independently derivable vs merely Gita-correspondences.

b_rows_sample.anchor: B(K_t,x)\rightarrow d ... d \in \{\text{supported},\text{refuted},\text{contradictory},\text{unknown},\text{unqualified},\text{inadmissible}\}
b_rows_sample.statement: Mathematical correction to 'the kernel should always be busy determining right and wrong': right/wrong should not initially be binary. Buddhi should implement a discrimination function B(K_t,x) -> d with d in {supported, refuted, contradictory, unknown, unqualified, inadmissible}, not a Boolean truth oracle. Hence Buddhi = epistemic discrimination, not Buddhi = truth; the kernel does not create truth, it evaluates what can legitimately be concluded from its current state and evidence.

b_rows_sample.anchor: \mathcal B: (K_t,O_t,E_t,C_t) \rightarrow D_t
b_rows_sample.statement: Proposes B:(K_t,O_t,E_t,C_t)->D_t (discrimination/decision result), enumerating what B must do: distinguish, compare, validate, detect contradiction, assess evidence, qualify, reject, accept, defer, update the knowledge state, preserve provenance, determine what remains unknown. Central hypothesis: KnowledgeOS Kernel ~philosophically~ Mind; Buddhi ~philosophically~ Kernel's discrimination capability; K_t = changing Knowledge State; K (calligraphic) = Knowledge Space. Four-level picture: Knowledge Space K -> Knowledge State K_t -> KnowledgeOS Kernel -> Buddhi -> epistemic operations -> K_{t+1}. Explicitly marked as hypothesis pending testing against actual Gita passages and the existing KnowledgeOS corpus, not yet canonical.

b_rows_sample.anchor: \mathcal K \overset{\Omega}{\longrightarrow} O_t \overset{\mathcal B}{\longrightarrow} D_t \overset{\delta}{\longrightarrow} K_{t+1}
b_rows_sample.statement: The central kernel question evolves from 'what operations does the Kernel perform?' to 'what can a bounded KnowledgeOS Kernel legitimately know, observe, discriminate, and conclude about a knowledge space larger than its current state?'. Final research-model pipeline: K (Knowledge Space) --Omega (observation/projection)--> O_t (observation) --B (Buddhi/discrimination)--> D_t (discrimination result) --delta (state transition)--> K_{t+1} (new Knowledge State). Explicitly not yet canonical architecture; identifies convergence of existing open questions about Observation, Proposition, State, Event, Buddhi, Qualify, delta, and the five-axis Sigma.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Can the existing KnowledgeOS eight primitives and the five-axis \Sigma=(A,S,R,V,C) express the proposed Mind–Buddhi–Kernel behavior without introducing a new primitive?
b_rows_sample.statement: Proposes pausing philosophical interpretation after Chapter 12 to test mathematically: can the existing eight primitives and five-axis Sigma=(A,S,R,V,C) express the proposed Mind-Buddhi-Kernel behavior without a new primitive? Specifically test whether Buddhi = an operation over existing primitives, Mind = a state/orientation over existing primitives, and Kernel = (K_t, operations, invariants, transition rules) -- framed as the first real mathematical/DDD test of the 'KnowledgeOS Kernel = Mind' interpretation.

b_rows_sample.anchor: E_d(K_t)=K_{t+1} ... R_d(K_t)=K_{t+1} ... C(K_t,o)=K_{t+1} ... X(K_t)\rightarrow \text{conflict-qualified state} ... Z(K_t)\rightarrow G_t
b_rows_sample.statement: Six candidate (not canonical) operators: E (Expansion) discovers a new relevant dimension d not-in D_t, now in D_{t+1}; R_d (Refinement) improves an existing dimension, v_t(d) prec_d v_{t+1}(d); C (Correction) changes an existing value because new evidence shows the previous state was wrong -- explicitly Purification != monotonic accumulation, since a purified state may contain less due to removed erroneous knowledge; X (Contradiction resolution) given p and not-p, the kernel must not arbitrarily select one, producing a conflict-qualified state until Buddhi/evidence/qualification can discriminate; Q (Qualification), the unresolved G1 operator, determining sufficient justification for the intended epistemic purpose, reframed via the recent Cavell-derived reconsideration so purification can mean correctly recognizing a gap cannot currently be resolved rather than resolving it; Z (Zero detection) detects epistemic absence, Z(K_t)->G_t (recognized gaps), with G_t transformable via E,R,C,Q into G_{t+1} -- the system becomes more purified partly by knowing more accurately what it does not know.

b_rows_sample.anchor: \{\operatorname{Discriminate},\ \operatorname{Qualify},\ \operatorname{Transition}\}\ \cong\ \{\equiv,\ G1,\ \delta\}
b_rows_sample.statement: The philosophically-proposed minimal kernel algebra Omega_K={Discriminate,Qualify,Transition} (from S2219, the kernel-definition-from-evidence-maths-DDD file) maps exactly onto the formal lane's independently-established blockers: Discriminate = the equality/distinguishability relation equiv (the unique minimal cycle cut per Steps 289/291, unique over both graph universes); Qualify = the corpus's own Qualify:Observation x Policy -> Evidence, i.e. G1, named/typed/no body, irreducible; Transition = K_t --delta--> K_{t+1}, i.e. delta, commit case unspecifiable, executed as K1 is K0. This is a genuine independent arrival (derived from 'what must a kernel be able to do', not from the dependency graph, 261.23, or the G1 register) but a NEGATIVE convergence: it solves none of the three, and is a restatement of the blocker set, not a kernel. Registered as new gap G-90 (derived, raises confidence, closes nothing). Sharp consequence stated: any minimal kernel algebra containing Qualify inherits G1 -- since Qualify is the one irreducible gap, a genuinely minimal kernel cannot be closed without closing G1.

b_rows_sample.anchor: A correctly shaped triple whose three components are EXACTLY the three open items. It states the problem well. It populates nothing.
b_rows_sample.statement: Tests the proposed kernel shape K=(K_t,Omega_K,I) slot by slot against the formal lane: K_t (the state) is OPEN (per Step 285; 258.35 says it may not be a tuple at all); Omega_K (permitted operations) is OPEN (N-4 mandatory membership open, 0 of 22 operations has a body/identity/ratification per 291); I (invariants) has 0 of 7 established (per REFINED-STEP-287-INVARIANTS), and I is downstream of equiv in 261.30's chain. Conclusion: a correctly-shaped triple whose three components are exactly the three open items -- a well-posed problem statement, not progress toward closure; must not be mistaken for populating the kernel (per 291's 'shape -> content requires a derivation, and none exists').

b_rows_sample.anchor: 1. Perceive / receive ... 5. Orient
b_rows_sample.statement: Proposes the KnowledgeOS kernel may need five fundamentally different classes of work: (1) Perceive/receive O_t; (2) Represent O_t->K_t; (3) Discriminate B_t(K_t,O_t)->d_t; (4) Transform delta(K_t,d_t)->K_{t+1}; (5) Orient rho_t(K_t,Omega). The fifth (Orient) is said to become much more visible once Chapter 11 (the horizon Omega) is added to the model.

b_rows_sample.anchor: \Omega = \{ Observe,\; Discriminate,\; Relate,\; Validate,\; Qualify,\; Transform,\; Reject,\; Accept,\; Revise \}
b_rows_sample.statement: Candidate (non-canonical) operator family from Chapters 10-15 combined: Omega={Observe, Discriminate, Relate, Validate, Qualify, Transform, Reject, Accept, Revise}, with Buddhi approx delta as the mechanism selecting/executing several of these, e.g. delta(Observation,Context)->Decision and delta(K_t,E_t)->K_{t+1}, connecting to the unresolved Qualify problem from Steps 285-287.

b_rows_sample.anchor: \mathcal K \neq K_t \neq \mathcal M
b_rows_sample.statement: Formal first principle: K (Knowledge Space, potentially unbounded) != K_t (Knowledge State at time t, what the system currently represents) != M (KnowledgeOS Kernel, the smallest persistent computational unit that evaluates and transforms knowledge states). The Gita's language helps interpret M as Mind, but the software kernel is not literally the philosophical mind. Defines M = the smallest unit capable of epistemic state transition, i.e. capable of K_t->K_{t+1} under some evidence/observation/proposition/event/operation.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Z:\boxed{K_t\rightarrow G_t} ... \delta: \boxed{(K_t,G_t,E_t,C_t)\rightarrow D_t} ... \tau: \boxed{(K_t,D_t)\rightarrow K_{t+1}}
b_rows_sample.statement: Full typed operator pipeline: Z:K_t->G_t (gap/boundary discovery, internal inspection); delta:(K_t,G_t,E_t,C_t)->D_t (discrimination/Buddhi, taking gaps, evidence, and context); tau:(K_t,D_t)->K_{t+1} (transition/transformation). Composition tau o delta o Z is type-correct given matching interfaces; for external input f_x(K_t)=tau(K_t,delta(x,E,C)); for internally discovered gaps f_Z(K_t)=tau(K_t,delta(Z(K_t))). The kernel therefore performs two fundamentally different activities: external epistemic input (x->delta) and internal epistemic inspection (K_t--Z-->G_t).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Level 0 — Primitive kernel mechanisms ... Level 1 — epistemic operations ... Level 2 — higher-order processes
b_rows_sample.statement: Proposes a three-level operator hierarchy to address the concern that not all candidate operators should be primitive: Level 0 primitives {delta,Z,tau} (smallest candidates); Level 1 epistemic operations built from primitives (Observe, Compare, Validate, Qualify, Revise, Accept, Reject), e.g. Accept(x)=tau(K_t,delta(x,E,C)=accepted), Reject(x)=tau(K_t,delta(x,E,C)=rejected); Level 2 higher-order processes as compositions (Purification, Learning, Investigation, Knowledge evolution), P = O_1 o O_2 o ... o O_n, assessed as important for DDD (avoiding conflating primitive operations with their compositions).

b_rows_sample.anchor: \mathcal M=(Q,\mathbb O,\delta,\tau,\mathbb I)
b_rows_sample.statement: Proposes formalizing the kernel as a state machine M=(Q,O,delta,tau,I) where Q=kernel control states (renamed from S to avoid collision with Sigma's S axis), O=kernel operations, delta=discrimination function, tau=transition function, I=invariants. Also proposes the kernel invariant M != K_t must hold (otherwise K_t->K_{t+1} would mean the kernel becomes a different object every time); formalized as Identity(M_t)=Identity(M_{t+1}) while K_t != K_{t+1} is permitted -- 'persistent kernel identity + mutable epistemic state' proposed as a fundamental candidate architectural invariant, worth testing against the corpus.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Qualify: X\rightarrow \{Qualified,\;Unqualified,\;Terminated\} ... Kernel determines the admissible epistemic status of a state transition.
b_rows_sample.statement: Refines Qualify (still classified G1) via the Cavell insight (justification may legitimately terminate rather than being infinitely extended) into Qualify:X->{Qualified, Unqualified, Terminated}, rather than assuming qualification is always a total true/false decision -- candidate only. Reframes the kernel's deeper job away from 'determine truth' toward 'Kernel determines the admissible epistemic status of a state transition', assessed as much closer to what the corpus actually supports; enumerates the kernel's operative questions (what do we have, what evidence supports it, what is missing, what conflicts, what relationship exists, what can legitimately be concluded, where must qualification stop, what state transition is admissible).

a_rows_sample.anchor: INV-ATTR-2/G-2: separation is Declared, NOT attestable. No mechanism can establish who performed an act; assurance rests entirely on where the human starts the session.
a_rows_sample.statement: Finding F-4: role separation between producer, verifier, and approver is Declared, not attestable (INV-ATTR-2/G-2); no mechanism in the estate can establish who actually performed an act, so assurance rests entirely on where the human starts a session -- a capability described as C-5, separation attestation, with no owner today.

a_rows_sample.anchor: this is the first recorded instance of it failing in the FALSE-BAR direction. INV-ATTR-2 anticipated that a process could wrongly claim independence; this event shows the same mechanism can make a process wrongly claim to be barred
a_rows_sample.statement: INV-ATTR-2 ('separation is declared, not attestable') is extended by observed evidence to a second failure direction: not only can a process wrongly claim independence (the failure the invariant was framed against), but the same unverified-self-declaration property can make a process wrongly claim to BE barred, harming an assignment rather than assurance.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The platform cannot attest a specified session execution. identity binding must NOT be placed inside C-10's authoritative state, because C-10 cannot establish it. It is C-5-shaped
a_rows_sample.statement: The sharpest finding in the D3 prep: a C-10 receipt's binding to a specific session execution can never be stronger than what INV-ATTR-1/INV-ATTR-2 permit (self-declared, not attested), so identity binding cannot be placed inside C-10's authoritative state -- it is C-5-shaped, and C-5 owns no attestation record either.

a_rows_sample.anchor: One prohibition, three surfaces: an unresolved status may never be laundered into a resolved one.
a_rows_sample.statement: A single cross-cutting prohibition is observed recurring in three independent places in the estate's governance (independence classification, C-5 separation dimensions, D4.1 compensating controls, later a fourth at D4.3 M4): an unresolved epistemic status must never be laundered into a resolved one -- recorded as an observation bearing on, but distinct from, the canonical unifying-invariant candidate.

a_rows_sample.anchor: This process is not a neutral party to this question... It has an interest in concluding that that record is worth preserving.
a_rows_sample.statement: Full process-disclosure practice: a producing process discloses its own prior participation and interest in the outcome (having authored the canonical analysis, D5, and prior governance registrations) and binds itself out of later verifying or accepting its own work (R-34/P-2).

a_rows_sample.anchor: This process is not a neutral party to this question, and the reason is specific... many of the 210 transitions and 99 grants whose durability is the subject of this ADR were recorded by this process.
a_rows_sample.statement: Full conflict-of-interest disclosure: the ADR's producer recorded many of the transitions whose durability is under analysis, has an interest in concluding the record is worth preserving, and binds itself out of approving, verifying, or accepting its own ADR.

a_rows_sample.anchor: the Governance actor was correct to refuse to decide. That refusal is actually evidence that the separation model is working.
a_rows_sample.statement: The PO/ARB's own observation, recorded as OBSERVED evidence: a producer bar held under direct pressure to breach it, twice, without an exception being requested, is evidence that the separation-of-authority model is functioning; the registering process explicitly draws no conclusion about C-5 (separation attestation) ownership from it.

a_rows_sample.anchor: the S4b lane's registered executionContext names the producer as claude-code-session:5e1dd9ee. The plan 3817eb2b was produced by claude-code-session:1c8b041b.
a_rows_sample.statement: INFO-2: a provenance discrepancy exists in the governance record itself (not the plan) — the plan discloses its own producer correctly, but the lane's registered executionContext names a different process as producer; reconciling this is left as a Governance act.

a_rows_sample.anchor: C-12's principle — author ≠ independent reviewer, not author ≠ every prior reviewer — would make it authoring-eligible again, and repeated authoring remains a QUALITY RISK rather than an independence failure.
a_rows_sample.statement: Clarifies an eligibility rule already precedented in the chain: the exclusion rule is 'author ≠ independent reviewer', not 'author ≠ every prior reviewer who ever touched this artifact' — a process that authored earlier amendments remains eligible to author a later, different correction, though the repetition itself is recorded as a quality risk rather than an independence failure.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Independence — the seven criteria, all required ... distinct process/session identity ... is not a continuation/compaction/fork/resume lineage of a barred producer
a_rows_sample.statement: States a seven-criterion independence test (process identity, non-authorship of the artifact/prior corrections/prior verifications, non-lineage from a barred producer, non-inherited working context) with the rule that a different session ID alone is insufficient; if lineage cannot be established the classification must be NOT ATTESTED, never PASS.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Independence is not one property ... Role independence ... Authority independence ... Access independence ... Organizational independence ... Financial independence ... Technical independence ... Temporal independence ... Cognitive independence
a_rows_sample.statement: Decomposes 'independence' into eight distinct dimensions and a six-level evidence-strength ladder (self-declaration through independent external assessment), concluding a platform can prove some dimensions (recorded identity difference, access-enforced separation) but not others (no collusion, no cognitive bias, organizational independence) from metadata alone.

a_rows_sample.anchor: A reviewer checking only the two names it was handed would have PASSED this gate and proceeded ... this is exactly why the same commission forbids hand-copied grant lists: the chat-supplied exclusion set was narrower than the governed one.
a_rows_sample.statement: Demonstrates the failure mode of trusting a prompt-supplied exclusion list rather than the governed record: the chat-supplied set of two barred names missed a fourth clause that fires on a registered grant covering the same performer under a different role in this same chain.

a_rows_sample.anchor: a REGISTERED act that is not live is a FALSE RECORD — and here it would falsely assert that an independent reviewer is at work on the gate that exists to guarantee independence.
a_rows_sample.statement: States the converse of the estate's 'a live but unregistered act still counts as missing' rule: a registered-but-not-live START is a false record, which is the worse failure direction on the one gate whose purpose is guaranteeing independence.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 'Fresh' is satisfied in the sense the record can test — no prior participation. It cannot mean 'no knowledge of the estate': this session read MEMORY.md and CONTEXT.md at startup via the repository's SessionStart hook, which is disclosed here rather than left to be discovered.
a_rows_sample.statement: Narrows what 'fresh' can mean under the record's own tests: no prior participation is provable; absence of any estate knowledge is not, and unavoidable bootstrap reading is disclosed rather than concealed.

a_rows_sample.anchor: independence is not transferable: an assignment whose recorded evidence names a8ce5a39 cannot be discharged by 8a525719 without the record asserting something false about who did the work.
a_rows_sample.statement: Names a second-order independence failure distinct from personal ineligibility: a genuinely independent process cannot discharge a review under a workflow lane whose registered execution context names a different process, since INV-ATTR-1 means the engine itself would never detect the substitution.

a_rows_sample.anchor: I will not adopt another process's identity in order to become operable.
a_rows_sample.statement: States a refusal principle: a process must not adopt a different, already-registered process's self-declared identity merely to satisfy a commission's addressee field and become operable.

a_rows_sample.anchor: a live but unregistered act still counts as missing ... a REGISTERED act that is not live is a FALSE RECORD.
a_rows_sample.statement: Restates the estate's two-directional recording rule as the reason a chat-delivered commission cannot substitute for a recorded START transition.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 'It is CODE provenance, never AI-process attestation: nothing here asserts who produced the artifact (EKS-07 stays unsolved; self-declared process identity is not independently attested authorship).' — scripts/lib/EngineeringKnowledge/Shared/Domain/HandoffContext.php:11–15
a_rows_sample.statement: AI processes are first-class actors (they invoke CLIs, author artifacts, and record transitions -- e.g. recordedBy:architecture on 2 HANDOFF transitions), but their identity cannot be established by any mechanism: tier-1 source states verbatim that this is code provenance, never AI-process attestation (EKS-07 unsolved); self-declared process identity, as practiced (e.g. a document declaring its producer as claude-code-session:5e1dd9ee), is explicitly marked 'self-declared and NOT attestable.'

a_rows_sample.anchor: What EKS does not do with AI processes ... No process identity ... No cross-process notification ... No agent registry ... No capability restriction. Every hook is advisory; nothing an AI process can do is prevented by EKS.
a_rows_sample.statement: EKS explicitly does not: issue/record/verify any AI-process identifier (self-declaration is the practice); notify concurrent processes of each other's actions (discovery is only by re-reading files, EKS-07); register any AI process in registry.yaml; or restrict any AI-process capability (every hook is advisory; nothing an AI process can do is prevented by EKS).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Exactly one mutation owner per work item is a mechanically enforced invariant (I-1)
a_rows_sample.statement: Grants: a grant without a humanActRef is refused by the engine ('the record never manufactures authority -- G-2/R5b'). Exactly one mutation owner per work item is mechanically enforced (I-1). Closure is a governance act (G-1): COMPLETE refuses any writer but governance/human. Producer != acceptor (R-34, INV-ATTR-2): a process cannot verify/accept its own work; separation is declared, not attestable.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Governance does not treat a later-arriving text as automatically governing... a later act is not automatically a supersession.
b_rows_sample.statement: A later-arriving instruction/act is not automatically treated as superseding a prior, already-executed one; which text governs is a disposition the PO/ARB must make explicitly.

b_rows_sample.anchor: What a self-review CAN establish...What it CANNOT establish...that the migration design is sound...that its findings are right...that nothing was omitted that the author did not think of
b_rows_sample.statement: A self-review (same producer as the artifact under review) explicitly states it can establish mechanical completeness and provenance (re-runnable by anyone) but cannot establish design soundness, correctness of findings, or omissions the author itself did not think of; states it must never be cited as independent verification.

b_rows_sample.anchor: INFO-1 — a defect this pass found in its own artifact... The plan should scope the claim as 'exactly one writer OF GOVERNANCE EVIDENCE' and cite the discriminating test.
b_rows_sample.statement: The plan's claim of 'exactly one writer' is correct but not reproducible from the obvious grep, which returns three files; the discriminating test (references runtime/workflow AND writes) is what makes the claim survive, and the plan should scope its own claim accordingly.

b_rows_sample.statement: INFO-2: a provenance discrepancy exists in the governance record itself (not the plan) — the plan discloses its own producer correctly, but the lane's registered executionContext names a different process as producer; reconciling this is left as a Governance act.

b_rows_sample.anchor: the §1 inventory is a point-in-time measurement of a LIVE corpus... §1's numbers are a dated observation, not the migration's inventory, and must not be substituted for the Phase-1 run.
b_rows_sample.statement: INFO-4: the plan's own current-state inventory numbers are only a dated snapshot of a corpus that continues to accept writes, and must never be substituted for the migration's own required Phase-1 inventory run.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Verified: the CONDITION was recorded two days earlier, in 2026-08-17-KOS-ATTR-ARCH-001-stage2-bounded-context-confirmation.md as coupling problem C-2
b_rows_sample.statement: Corrects the premise that a migration-plan finding is 'new evidence': the underlying condition (interpretation authority is environment-swappable via KOS_MECHANISM_PATH) was already recorded two days earlier as coupling problem C-2 with its own remedy route (R-37/ADR-C6); what the migration plan added was precision (a two-axis formulation and line-addressed evidence), not discovery.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The Single Authority Resolver invariant is explicitly extended from governance-evidence record location to also govern the mechanism that interprets those records...an EXPLICIT SCOPE EXTENSION, not as an application of the existing invariant.
b_rows_sample.statement: Decision: Option A (bring the interpreter-selection axis under the same resolver boundary as the record-location axis) is adopted, but recorded explicitly as a deliberate scope extension of the existing invariant rather than a silent application of it, so that the estate's rule against silent scope expansion is honoured.

b_rows_sample.anchor: the delivered plan already presumes A... The two delivered artifacts are not aligned: the plan implements an answer the review says is not yet given.
b_rows_sample.statement: Observes that the migration plan's Phase 5 already operationally assumes Option A (bringing the interpreter mechanism under the resolver) while the governance review states the question is not yet determined and that governance must not determine it — an internal misalignment between two delivered artifacts that the pending decision must resolve.

b_rows_sample.anchor: This review establishes: completeness · provenance · conformity to decided governance constraints. It CANNOT and does NOT establish: technical soundness · implementation correctness · migration safety · production readiness.
b_rows_sample.statement: An independent (different producer) governance review explicitly separates what it establishes (completeness, provenance, conformity to decided constraints, all re-executed rather than re-read) from what only a separate technical Architecture review may establish (soundness, correctness, safety, readiness).

b_rows_sample.anchor: INFO-1 — the inventory figures have drifted by one, and the drift is fully accounted for.
b_rows_sample.statement: Re-measures the corpus independently and finds a one-grant drift from the plan's cited figures, traces it exactly to a governance act registered after the plan's commit, and confirms the plan was accurate at its own commit — demonstrating the corpus's live-growth property with concrete numbers.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 23 / 30 ... trials that lost a transition ... exit status of the losing process 0 — accepted, reported {"ok":true,"seq":2} ... sequence set of every survivor DENSE and MONOTONIC
b_rows_sample.statement: A concurrency experiment run in a temp directory (never against the real corpus) launched two concurrent `append` calls against the workflow-state.php writer 30 times; 23 of 30 trials silently lost a transition, the losing process reported success (exit 0), and the surviving sequence remained dense and monotonic every time — the same loss reproduced on the `grant` write path.

b_rows_sample.anchor: session-resolve.php EXECUTES an arbitrary program named by the environment and HANDS IT the authority record directory as an argument. ⇒ This is not only an interpretation path. It is a WRITE path
b_rows_sample.statement: session-resolve.php is found to be stronger a hazard than the plan states: it executes a subprocess named by the KOS_MECHANISM_PATH environment variable and passes it the authority record directory as an argument, making it a write path through a component whose own bytes contain no write call — a hazard whose value rises once relocation makes the target the durable authoritative store.

b_rows_sample.anchor: the durable artifact is a git blob, and git — not the copy — decides the committed bytes... a clone on a CRLF platform materialises different bytes and the Phase-4 hashes no longer verify
b_rows_sample.statement: Byte-preservation of the migration copy is undermined by an unpinned .gitattributes (`* text=auto`, eol unspecified): checkout normalisation is a no-op today (no CR bytes exist), but a future clone on a CRLF platform would materialise different bytes and invalidate the Phase-4 hashes, and the plan's own scope fence names .gitignore but is silent about .gitattributes, the file that actually governs committed bytes.

b_rows_sample.anchor: PASS WITH DESIGN CLARIFICATIONS ... CL-1–CL-3 are GATES ON PHASE 3 — the migration must not begin until they are closed.
b_rows_sample.statement: Verdict: PASS WITH DESIGN CLARIFICATIONS, twelve items (CL-1..CL-12) ranked, of which CL-1 (concurrency/completeness claim must be bounded, not absolute), CL-2 (Phase 1 inventory must be re-executed and frozen at migration time, not pinned to a stale literal), and CL-3 (the plan names no act that produces the resolver it later switches to) are gate-class and block Phase 3 from beginning; none requires reopening B', R-CONFLICT, OPEN-M3, or placement governance.

b_rows_sample.anchor: the withdrawal is real ... NO SILENT REINTRODUCTION FOUND. The stronger claim does not survive anywhere in the artifact.
b_rows_sample.statement: CL-1 (concurrency/completeness) is verified CLOSED: AMD3's bounded restatement ('no record lost RELATIVE TO the frozen manifest and both inputs') is checked at every site in the artifact and the withdrawn absolute claim is not silently reintroduced anywhere.

b_rows_sample.anchor: RC-4 — NEW GAP the remedy does not cover ... A write landing after the Phase-5 re-hash but before the writer is switched goes to the RUNTIME copy ... and is destroyed by Phase 7.
b_rows_sample.statement: RC-4: the freeze/manifest/re-hash design verifies the runtime copy at exactly one instant (the Phase-5 re-hash), three phases before the destructive Phase-7 removal; a write landing in that gap is in neither the frozen manifest nor either reconciliation input and would be silently destroyed by Phase 7's removal, which relies on a byte-verification performed earlier and never rechecked.

b_rows_sample.anchor: RC-1 ... Phase 2b as written is CIRCULAR with Phase 3, and Phase 3's precondition is therefore unsatisfiable.
b_rows_sample.statement: RC-1: as amended, a phase that pins .gitattributes AND commits the Phase-1 manifest in the same commit as the Phase-3 copy cannot complete before Phase 3 (its commit must contain Phase 3's output), while Phase 3 cannot begin before that phase completes — the same defect class as CL-3 (a phase consuming an artifact its own predecessor has not produced) reappearing inside a remedy meant to close a different clarification.

b_rows_sample.anchor: RC-2 — but the OTHER half of INV-R1's row-1 cell was not split, and it collides with both contract suites... an implementer who applies the boundary check literally makes the entire pinned contract suite exit 65 with no report.
b_rows_sample.statement: RC-2: every test in both pinned contract suites drives the components through a --dir temp path outside the governed evidence boundary, so a literal reading of the resolver's boundary-validation rule would make the entire pinned suite refuse with no report; the fix requires stating that a governed override selects a non-authoritative output location rather than violating the boundary.

b_rows_sample.anchor: RC-10 — a mis-resolved path MATERIALIZES rather than failing ... The writer creates its parent directory.
b_rows_sample.statement: RC-10: saveRecord() calls mkdir on its target's parent directory, meaning a resolver that returns a wrong-but-well-formed path does not fail loudly but silently manufactures a new evidence location — recreating the exact misfiling defect B' exists to close, inside the component built to close it; the refusal must therefore be enforced before saveRecord is reached.

b_rows_sample.anchor: RC-9 — 'canonical re-encode' is not defined ... a false CASE B (escalation) rather than a false CASE A (silent merge) — the safe direction
b_rows_sample.statement: RC-9: the plan's 'common prefix byte-identical' comparison rule for CASE A does not define its canonicalization method (e.g. key-order sorting), and since JSON decode/encode preserves insertion order, two semantically equal but differently-ordered records would compare unequal, producing a false escalation to CASE B rather than a false silent merge (CASE A) — the safe failure direction, but ambiguous as written.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The ladder
a_rows_sample.statement: A three-status admission ladder governed by an explicit policy: Candidate -> Supported -> Accepted. Transitions form a covering relation -- each status reachable only from its immediate predecessor (I-12); skipping is formally excluded. The Supported -> Accepted transition is named Determination, governed by the AcceptancePolicy, which decides what may be admitted -- a different question from what the evidence supports.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The boundary
a_rows_sample.statement: Committed is not a fourth epistemic status; it is a decision-boundary status attached to an Accepted item by authority, under the model's sharpest rule A6: authority determines commitment, not evidential truth. Evidence can make a claim Accepted; only an authorized act can make anyone bound to it. The falsification pass caught the earlier formulation quietly treating Committed as a rung of the same ladder; the ratified repair re-typed it, and the lived governance record enacts exactly this discipline (adoption and authorization as separate human acts).

a_rows_sample.anchor: The policy governs itself — governedly
a_rows_sample.statement: The AcceptancePolicy is itself a governed, versioned object: policy-as-content (admissible like any claim, at rest inside K_t) is distinguished from policy-in-force (the approved version that actually governs admission), and no in-force policy changes without a governed decision (I-11); mentioned here because admission is where its absence would corrupt first.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The adjacent states — an inheritance
a_rows_sample.statement: The ladder answers how far admitted, never in what condition held. The ratified Final Architecture layers the constitutional state vocabulary beside it: REJECTED (failed reasoning preserved, never silently discarded), CONFLICTED (contradictory knowledge coexisting until governed resolution, the conflict record surviving resolution), and the evidence-layer triple UNKNOWN != ABSENT != FALSE. These are not extensions bolted on: the archaeology dated them to the programme's first weeks, before the ladder existed -- inherited from the constitutional side rather than invented to fill the gap.

b_rows_sample.statement: States that completing the partial order over authority (assigning the context-relative ordering relation for each context) is deliberately left as policy content (revisable knowledge at rest, per the policy-as-content/policy-in-force stratification) rather than a formally fixed structure, and that no governed open question is owned for this gap.

b_rows_sample.anchor: PF-9 ... The source algebra (025f) establishes... authority as a CONTEXT-INDEXED PARTIAL ORDER... a THREE-OUTCOME vocabulary Resolved/Unresolved/Invalid... the boxed ESCALATION LAW UnresolvedGovernanceConflict -> HumanGovernance... None of these has a distinct ratified object; I-10/I-11 + the R-1 loop carry the load-bearing minimum.
b_rows_sample.statement: PF-9: the governance algebra source material (025f, 042, 121) establishes authority as a context-indexed partial order, scope/temporal applicability as conflict preconditions, a resolution machinery (hierarchy, supersession, explicit exception), a three-outcome vocabulary (Resolved/Unresolved/Invalid), a boxed escalation law (UnresolvedGovernanceConflict -> HumanGovernance, with "knowing that something cannot be determined is itself a valid computed result"), an Instruction!=AuthorizedDecision distinction, an AI-non-override rule, a version-transition schema, and the recursive-governance claim that the Constitution is itself a member of AuthoritativeKnowledge -- none of which has a distinct ratified object; only I-10/I-11 plus the R-1 loop carry the load-bearing minimum in the ratified architecture.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Take the AcceptancePolicy -- the object whose mis-layering caused more recorded trouble than any other. As content, a policy draft is L2 material... As the governor of admission, the policy-in-force is an L2 object with an L1 shadow: Article 3 forbids it to self-authorize, and invariant I-11 forbids it to change without a governed, versioned decision
b_rows_sample.statement: Traces the AcceptancePolicy (the object whose mis-layering caused the most recorded trouble in the programme) through all five layers as a worked example: as content it is L2 material at rest in K_t; as the governor of admission it is an L2 object with an L1 shadow (Article 3 forbids self-authorization, I-11 forbids ungoverned change); any enforcement would be L4 code that must first consult the governance record; and the failure the layering prevents is the programme's most-sighted defect (the policy that governs while nothing governs it, sighted independently four times, per Chapter III.8).

b_rows_sample.anchor: FOUR interlocking guards make the modification governed rather than wild: 1. Mode separation... 2. The change is a Decision under contract... 3. Versioning with a transition schema... 4. Recursive self-subjection... The governor is inside the governed store, not above it.
b_rows_sample.statement: States the chapter's central answer to why self-modifying admission policy is not an uncontrolled system: four interlocking guards -- (1) mode separation (proposed policy is content only, force requires the approved in-force version; "a rule that is sort of in effect" is unrepresentable), (2) the change is a Decision under the full III.7 Decision-Contract machinery (no-averaging conjunction, Unknown->Block, Auth as an act, per A6), (3) versioning with a transition schema (change rationale, authority, effective date, superseded version, verification; forward-only supersession), and (4) recursive self-subjection (Constitution subset-of AuthoritativeKnowledge -- the governing documents obey their own provenance/authority/temporal-validity/traceability disciplines) -- making self-modification exist exactly once, as a narrow contract-guarded versioned human-authorized transition, with every other path a type error.

a_rows_sample.anchor: An aggregate is a consistency boundary, not a collection of related concepts. ... What must change atomically to preserve a domain invariant? Not: What concepts are intellectually related?
a_rows_sample.statement: Restates and sharpens the core DDD principle that an aggregate boundary is determined by what must change atomically for an invariant, never by conceptual relatedness alone; applied to reject folding evidence/reasoning/authority/predictions/models into one Claim aggregate.

a_rows_sample.anchor: KnowledgeClaim ... does not contain every evidence item, every reasoning path, every semantic representation, every authority, every prediction, every model. Those are related through references. ... one evidence item can support many claims.
a_rows_sample.statement: KnowledgeClaim aggregate holds only ClaimId/PropositionReference/Scope/CurrentStanding/CurrentRevision/Status/RevisionLineageReference; evidence, reasoning, semantics, authority, predictions and models are related by reference rather than embedded, since one evidence item can support many claims and one authority can govern many claims.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Evidence should normally be immutable in substance. Corrections create a new evidence version or invalidation event rather than silently rewriting history. ... EvidenceCaptured / EvidenceValidated / EvidenceInvalidated / EvidenceSuperseded.
a_rows_sample.statement: Evidence aggregate (EvidenceId, SourceReference, Observation, AcquisitionMetadata, Scope, Integrity, Validity, Provenance) is normally immutable in substance, with correction handled via new-version or invalidation events rather than silent history rewriting.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Do not model Claim/'confidence = 0.87' as though confidence were an intrinsic permanent property. Instead: Determination ... The Claim's current standing is derived/assigned according to governed rules from admissible determinations. ... ASSESSMENT != CLAIM ... CONFIDENCE != TRUTH.
a_rows_sample.statement: Determination-is-not-Claim-state ('one of the most important optimizations'): confidence must never be stored as an intrinsic Claim property; instead a separate Determination record (EvidenceSet, Assumptions, Method, Model, Result, Uncertainty, Scope, Assessor, Timestamp) feeds a governed derivation of the Claim's current standing.

a_rows_sample.anchor: They do not necessarily need to be transactionally co-owned. ... Cross-context coherence is maintained through: immutable references; domain events; deterministic policies; re-assessment; audit trails.
a_rows_sample.statement: Per-aggregate invariant list (Claim: identity+standing invariant; Evidence: integrity invariant; Determination: assessment integrity invariant; Authority: mandate invariant) with cross-context coherence maintained by immutable references, domain events, deterministic policies, re-assessment and audit trails rather than one transactional God aggregate -- called 'the correct DDD optimization.'

a_rows_sample.anchor: Candidate != Admitted Claim. ... Only admission creates authoritative domain state. ... Conflict is not rejection. CONFLICT != REJECTION. Two legitimate determinations can disagree without either being erased.
a_rows_sample.statement: Candidate->Admitted->Undetermined->{Validated/Rejected/Conflicted/Questionable/Unknown-Insufficient/Superseded/Withdrawn} lifecycle, with the constitutional gate performing only admissibility (not semantic reasoning), and the invariant that CONFLICT != REJECTION -- two legitimate determinations may disagree without erasure.

a_rows_sample.anchor: EvidenceInvalidated(E) -> Affected Claims -> Reassessment Required -> Assessment Mechanism -> New Determination -> KnowledgeClaim state transition. ... Do not synchronously rewrite every affected claim. ... This is scalable DDD.
a_rows_sample.statement: When evidence is invalidated, affected claims are event-driven-reassessed rather than synchronously rewritten -- an explicit example of 'what must be atomic' (Claim identity+standing transition, Evidence identity+integrity, Determination identity+assessment record, Authority grant+mandate validity are atomic; evidence-invalidation-plus-every-affected-claim-plus-every-projection is explicitly NOT atomic).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Measure: Risk = P(wrong | answered) ... four-way taxonomy: Unambiguous/Correct resolution, Ambiguous/False acceptance, Ambiguous/Correct abstention, Unambiguous/Blind abstention. The most dangerous failure is: False acceptance of an ambiguous case.
a_rows_sample.statement: Calibrated Abstention: AI mechanisms must expose Answer+Confidence+Coverage+Risk (Risk = P(wrong|answered)) and be evaluated against a four-way ground-truth-x-mechanism taxonomy, with 'false acceptance of an ambiguous case' identified as the most dangerous failure mode, fitting the constitutional UNKNOWN requirement.

a_rows_sample.anchor: English expression / German expression / JSON representation / Graph representation / LLM-generated paraphrase ... may refer to the same KnowledgeClaim. But: similarity != identity ... semantic equivalence != transactional ownership. ... Replace the interpreter. The constitutional boundary must still behave the same.
a_rows_sample.statement: Identity Architecture and Semantic Port: identity must be independent of representation/language/format, similarity != identity, and the core must remain invariant under mechanism (interpreter) replacement -- a stated 'major architectural test.'

a_rows_sample.anchor: The research was right about the invariants, but the earlier KnowledgeAggregate was too large as a literal DDD aggregate. ... The current research itself already warns that the large aggregate is only a hypothesis and that aggregate membership must be justified by atomic invariant protection.
a_rows_sample.statement: Explicit correction: the earlier KnowledgeAggregate hypothesis (Identity/Evidence/Justification/State/Confidence/History) was too large as a literal DDD aggregate; membership must be justified by atomic invariant protection, motivating the split into KnowledgeClaim/Evidence/Determination/Authority.

a_rows_sample.anchor: EXP-01 · The four evidence algebras (R4) — the corpus's first genuine experiment
a_rows_sample.statement: EXP-01 tested whether a simple scalar aggregation operator (A1=max, A2=weighted mean, A3=saturating 1-prod(1-si), A4=Bayesian updating) could serve as the epistemic foundation, using a formal design under triple role (mathematician/statistician/DDD) with an adversarial property test over 7 named properties on a shared normalized evidence universe. Result: MAX fails independent corroboration; Weighted Mean fails duplicates, corroboration, and dependency; Saturating and Bayesian-like both pass all 7. Verdict: 'No simple scalar operator is sufficient as the KnowledgeOS epistemic foundation,' with the strongest single result being that 'dependency must come first' (3 apparent evidences may be 1 observation plus 2 derived representations). This is COMPUTATIONALLY TESTED — the only R4 claim class with a recorded test artifact — but established only the negative result plus property/ordering requirements, not a validated aggregation architecture (candidate survival, not selection).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Evidence → supports Knowledge but: Evidence ≠ Knowledge. An observation may become evidence in a particular inquiry. The same observation can potentially support multiple claims. ... Evidence is therefore partly relational.
a_rows_sample.statement: Evidence supports Knowledge but Evidence != Knowledge; the same observation can become evidence for multiple different inquiries/claims (Observation -> Evidence for Inquiry A, Evidence for Inquiry B), making Evidence partly a relational concept rather than an intrinsic property of an observation -- with stated implications for the data model.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Knowledge ≠ Determination. Knowledge can exist without a specific decision being made. A determination is: an epistemically bounded conclusion reached under a specified context, evidence set and reasoning/verification method. D = f(K,E,C,M) ... Determination ≠ Decision. ... Decision ≠ Authorization. ... Authorization ≠ Execution.
a_rows_sample.statement: Chain of pipeline distinctions: Knowledge != Determination (a determination is 'an epistemically bounded conclusion reached under a specified context, evidence set and reasoning/verification method', formalized as D=f(K,E,C,M) over knowledge K, evidence E, context C, method M); Determination != Decision (a determination states a fact such as 'the implementation violates rule R', a decision states an action such as 'the implementation shall be corrected before release'); Decision != Authorization (a decision that something should happen is distinct from an authorization mechanism determining that a specific actor may execute a specific operation under specific conditions, giving the chain Decision -> Authorization -> Action rather than Decision -> Agent executes); Authorization != Execution (authorization does not entail the action has happened, enabling an 'authorized, not yet executed' state needed for auditability).

a_rows_sample.anchor: A governed representation of a claim or proposition whose source, context, validity and epistemic status are sufficiently known for the intended use. K = (claim, source, context, validity, status). ... Evidence supports Knowledge. but: Evidence ≢ Knowledge. ... Knowledge may have states such as: PROPOSED SUPPORTED CONFIRMED CONTESTED SUPERSEDED EXPIRED UNKNOWN ... K1 -- superseded by --> K2. Current truth ≠ Historical truth.
a_rows_sample.statement: Knowledge K = (claim, source, context, validity, status) is 'a governed representation of a claim or proposition whose source, context, validity and epistemic status are sufficiently known for the intended use'; Evidence supports Knowledge but Evidence is not identical to Knowledge. Candidate (non-final) knowledge-status enumeration: PROPOSED, SUPPORTED, CONFIRMED, CONTESTED, SUPERSEDED, EXPIRED, UNKNOWN. Superseded knowledge (K1 superseded-by K2) must not be erased, giving Current truth != Historical truth.

a_rows_sample.anchor: A Determination is a conclusion reached from specified knowledge/evidence under a defined context and method. D = f(K,E,C,M) ... A determination must be explainable. ... 'The AI said so' is not sufficient as a durable determination. ... VerificationResult → supports → Determination. But: VerificationResult ≠ Determination.
a_rows_sample.statement: Determination D=f(K,E,C,M) (knowledge, evidence, context, method) is a conclusion stronger than a casual opinion; invariant that a determination must be explainable via Determination -> Inputs+Method+Context, so 'the AI said so' cannot serve as a durable determination -- the system must be able to answer 'why did we reach this conclusion?' A deterministic VerificationResult (e.g. PASS) supports a Determination but is not identical to it (VerificationResult != Determination); a human/agent determination such as 'the implementation conforms to rule R' is a separate epistemic act built on top of the verification result.

b_rows_sample.anchor: An Observation is a recorded representation of something perceived, measured, detected, or otherwise encountered without automatically asserting its interpretation. O = (subject, method, value, time, context). Observation ≠ Interpretation. ... An observation must not silently contain an unmarked conclusion. ... An LLM frequently transforms: 'I found X' into: 'Therefore Y.' KnowledgeOS should preserve that boundary.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines Observation = (subject, method, value, time, context) as a recorded representation without automatic interpretation, distinguished from Interpretation and further from Claim (three epistemic levels illustrated by 'Nexus process is listening on port 8081' vs 'Nexus is reachable by application clients' vs 'Nexus architecture permits direct application access'). States the invariant that an observation must not silently contain an unmarked conclusion, warning this is especially important for AI-generated material, which frequently collapses 'I found X' into 'Therefore Y.'

b_rows_sample.anchor: An Inquiry is an intentional epistemic activity directed toward answering a question or resolving uncertainty. I = (question, subject, scope, context, objective). ... Task ≠ Inquiry ... although an Inquiry can generate Tasks. ... Inquiry ⇒ Question/Object. A generic 'Analyze this.' is insufficiently specified unless the intended question can be recovered.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines Inquiry = (question, subject, scope, context, objective) as an intentional epistemic activity ('determine something'), distinct from a Task ('do something'), though an Inquiry can generate Tasks (Task != Inquiry). Invariant: Inquiry implies Question/Object -- a generic instruction like 'Analyze this' is insufficiently specified unless its intended question can be recovered.

b_rows_sample.anchor: An observation becomes Evidence relative to an inquiry or claim. Evidence is contextual. E = (O, I, relevance, provenance, integrity). ... Evidence must preserve enough provenance to answer: Where did this come from? At minimum: Source(E) and Method(E). ... Evidence ≠ Proof unless the domain and method justify that terminology. We should use proof sparingly in the book.
b_rows_sample.statement: Evidence E = (Observation, Inquiry, relevance, provenance, integrity) is contextual -- an observation becomes evidence only relative to a specific inquiry/claim, and the same observation can be evidence for multiple inquiries. Minimum required provenance fields: Source(E), Method(E) (and for technical evidence, Time(E), Subject(E)). Distinguishes Evidence from mathematical Proof (Proof => Theorem under a formal system): engineering evidence is generally not equivalent to proof, and 'proof' should be used sparingly.

b_rows_sample.anchor: A governed representation of a claim or proposition whose source, context, validity and epistemic status are sufficiently known for the intended use. K = (claim, source, context, validity, status). ... Evidence supports Knowledge. but: Evidence ≢ Knowledge. ... Knowledge may have states such as: PROPOSED SUPPORTED CONFIRMED CONTESTED SUPERSEDED EXPIRED UNKNOWN ... K1 -- superseded by --> K2. Current truth ≠ Historical truth.
b_rows_sample.statement: Knowledge K = (claim, source, context, validity, status) is 'a governed representation of a claim or proposition whose source, context, validity and epistemic status are sufficiently known for the intended use'; Evidence supports Knowledge but Evidence is not identical to Knowledge. Candidate (non-final) knowledge-status enumeration: PROPOSED, SUPPORTED, CONFIRMED, CONTESTED, SUPERSEDED, EXPIRED, UNKNOWN. Superseded knowledge (K1 superseded-by K2) must not be erased, giving Current truth != Historical truth.

b_rows_sample.anchor: A Determination is a conclusion reached from specified knowledge/evidence under a defined context and method. D = f(K,E,C,M) ... A determination must be explainable. ... 'The AI said so' is not sufficient as a durable determination. ... VerificationResult → supports → Determination. But: VerificationResult ≠ Determination.
b_rows_sample.statement: Determination D=f(K,E,C,M) (knowledge, evidence, context, method) is a conclusion stronger than a casual opinion; invariant that a determination must be explainable via Determination -> Inputs+Method+Context, so 'the AI said so' cannot serve as a durable determination -- the system must be able to answer 'why did we reach this conclusion?' A deterministic VerificationResult (e.g. PASS) supports a Determination but is not identical to it (VerificationResult != Determination); a human/agent determination such as 'the implementation conforms to rule R' is a separate epistemic act built on top of the verification result.

b_rows_sample.anchor: A Decision is an authoritative selection among alternatives, made by an authorized decision-maker or mechanism within a defined governance context. Decision = (choice, authority, scope, context, time). ... Determination ≠ Decision ... Decision ⇒ Authority. ... Recommendation ≠ Decision. An AI may say: 'I recommend rejecting the architecture change.' That is a recommendation. It does not become an authoritative decision merely because the system generated it.
b_rows_sample.statement: Decision = (choice, authority, scope, context, time), an authoritative selection among alternatives made by an authorized decision-maker/mechanism within a governance context; a determination may inform but does not automatically become a decision (Determination != Decision); a decision requires identifiable authority (Decision => Authority, 'who or what had the right to decide?'); an AI recommendation is explicitly not a decision merely because the system generated it (Recommendation != Decision).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Authorization answers: Is this actor permitted to perform this operation under these conditions? Auth = f(actor, action, resource, policy, context, time). ... Decision ≠ Authorization. A governance body can decide that something should happen while an execution system separately authorizes a particular actor to perform it. ... Execute(a) ⇒ ValidAuthorization(a) unless an explicitly defined exception applies. ... Action ≠ Execution ... Execution(Action) produces observable effects.
b_rows_sample.statement: Authorization Auth=f(actor,action,resource,policy,context,time) answers whether a specific actor may perform a specific operation under specific conditions; Decision != Authorization (a governance decision that something should happen is separate from an execution system authorizing a particular actor). Invariant: Execute(a) => ValidAuthorization(a) unless an explicit exception applies. Action ('upgrade Nexus') != Execution ('podman pull ...', the mechanism); Execution(Action) produces observable effects, and Action->Execution->Observation closes the loop.

b_rows_sample.anchor: We started with nouns: Knowledge Evidence Decision Action and initially they looked like possible domain objects. But through the semantic analysis, we discovered that the more fundamental architecture is actually defined by relationships and invariants: supports derivedFrom determines authorizes executes supersedes contradicts observes. ... The domain is not merely: Objects. It is: Objects + Relationships + Invariants + Time + Authority.
b_rows_sample.statement: Major DDD observation: what began as candidate domain-object nouns (Knowledge, Evidence, Decision, Action) turned out, under semantic analysis, to be more fundamentally characterized by named relationships (supports, derivedFrom, determines, authorizes, executes, supersedes, contradicts, observes) and invariants; the domain is therefore relation-centric -- Objects + Relationships + Invariants + Time + Authority -- rather than a plain object model, judged 'much closer to the actual problem KnowledgeOS is trying to solve.'

b_rows_sample.anchor: I1: Observation ≠ Interpretation I2: Evidence ≠ Knowledge I3: Determination ≠ Decision I4: Decision ≠ Authorization I5: Authorization ≠ Execution I6: Unknown ≠ False I7: Provenance ≠ Lineage I8: Memory ≠ Historical Continuity I9: Recommendation ≠ Decision I10: Evidence must be traceable to its source. These should become candidates for the KnowledgeOS semantic constitution.
b_rows_sample.statement: Consolidates a candidate ten-invariant set (I1-I10: Observation!=Interpretation, Evidence!=Knowledge, Determination!=Decision, Decision!=Authorization, Authorization!=Execution, Unknown!=False, Provenance!=Lineage, Memory!=Historical Continuity, Recommendation!=Decision, Evidence must be traceable to its source), explicitly proposed as candidates for a future 'KnowledgeOS semantic constitution' -- not yet ratified.

b_rows_sample.anchor: We have not yet decided: exact bounded contexts; exact aggregates; database schema; event model; API structure; graph technology; microservices; class hierarchy; whether Wisdom deserves its own model; exact implementation of epistemic states. Those decisions belong later. ... Which invariants require a bounded context, which require an aggregate, which require a policy, and which are merely semantic relationships? ... Semantic Contract → Invariant → Consistency Boundary → DDD Boundary.
b_rows_sample.statement: Step 161 explicitly restrains scope: it has not decided exact bounded contexts, aggregates, database schema, event model, API structure, graph technology, microservices, class hierarchy, whether Wisdom deserves its own model, or the exact implementation of epistemic states -- deferred to later steps. Proposes Step 162 (Invariant and Boundary Derivation) to ask, per invariant, whether it requires a bounded context, an aggregate, a policy, or is merely a semantic relationship, via the pipeline Semantic Contract -> Invariant -> Consistency Boundary -> DDD Boundary.
