a_rows_sample.anchor: At least the following relations must be separated: = representation/structural equality; ≡ semantic equality; ≈ observational equivalence; ≅_I identity equivalence; ≅_P provenance-sensitive equivalence; ≅_H historical equivalence.
a_rows_sample.statement: The overloaded notation K1=K2 is decomposed into (at least) six distinct relations that must not be conflated: structural equality (=), semantic equality (equiv), observational equivalence (approx), identity equivalence (cong_I), provenance-sensitive equivalence (cong_P), and historical equivalence (cong_H); the corpus is said to explicitly record the first four distinctions and warn they are not interchangeable.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Same proposition ⇏ Same evidence identity. ... two observations can concern the same proposition while remaining distinct evidence objects.
a_rows_sample.statement: Preserved historical result: identity is not equality — two evidence objects e1,e2 can both support the same proposition p (Supports(e1,p) and Supports(e2,p)) without e1=e2; this affects provenance, deduplication, replay, validation, audit and merge, and is attributed to an earlier corpus reconstruction rather than newly derived here.

a_rows_sample.anchor: x =_str y iff their representations are structurally identical. ... =_str ≠ semantic equality unless the representation has already been proven canonical.
a_rows_sample.statement: Structural equality x=_str y (representations structurally identical) is computationally convenient but is warned to not equal semantic equality unless the representation is already proven canonical — two structurally different representations can denote the same semantic state.

a_rows_sample.anchor: x ≡_sem y iff Semantics(x)=Semantics(y). ... Semantic equality is conceptually appropriate, but currently underdefined.
a_rows_sample.statement: Semantic equality x equiv_sem y is defined via a semantic interpretation function Sem:Representation->Meaning being equal on x and y, but is flagged as not computationally decidable while Sem itself remains formally undefined — conceptually appropriate but currently underdefined.

a_rows_sample.anchor: H1 ≈ H2 iff every permitted observation produces the same result: ∀O∈𝒪: O(H1)=O(H2). ... This is the relation already underlying Step 260's behavioral quotient.
a_rows_sample.statement: Observational equivalence for histories (H1 approx H2 iff every permitted observation O produces the same result) and for states (K1 approx K2 iff every permitted state observation agrees) is identified as the same relation already underlying Step 260's behavioral quotient; notably it does not require internal representations to be identical.

a_rows_sample.anchor: SameId(x,y) ... Identity tracks denotation; equality compares values. This formulation is a reconstruction, not yet a corpus-proven final definition.
a_rows_sample.statement: Identity (SameId(x,y)) answers whether two references denote the same domain object, independent of value equality: x=_str y can hold with SameId false (two separately created records with identical content but distinct observations), and SameId can hold while representations differ (the same domain object having evolved) — 'identity tracks denotation; equality compares values', explicitly flagged as a reconstruction, not a corpus-proven final definition.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Historical equality asks: Are these states the same point or condition in an evolution history? ... Semantic equality ⇏ Historical equality.
a_rows_sample.statement: Historical equality asks whether two states are the same point in an evolution history, distinct from current semantic equality: K0 -Revise-> K1 can have K0 equiv_sem K1 (representation changed, semantics didn't) while K0 !=_H K1 (distinct historical states) — semantic equality does not imply historical equality; matters especially for Replay and audit.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Provenance is semantically relevant: K1 ≢ K2. Provenance is metadata only: K1 ≡ K2. ... equality cannot be resolved until the theory determines which information is semantically essential. This is a key dependency for Step 265.
a_rows_sample.statement: Provenance equality is genuinely ambiguous: given K1={p,e1}, K2={p,e2} with e1!=e2 both supporting p, either provenance is semantically relevant (K1 not-equiv K2) or metadata only (K1 equiv K2); the earlier corpus is said to identify this ambiguity explicitly and conclude it cannot be resolved until the theory determines which information is semantically essential — flagged as a key dependency for Step 265 (provenance placement).

a_rows_sample.anchor: No universal equality hierarchy has yet been proven. ... Identity and Provenance equality are independent dimensions.
a_rows_sample.statement: A candidate implication chain (structural => semantic => observational equivalence) is proposed but explicitly not declared universally valid without further assumptions; identity and provenance equality are treated as independent dimensions from this chain; current position: no universal equality hierarchy has yet been proven.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Explicit assertion membership ≠ semantic entailment. ... a∈_exp K ... K⊨a ... Stored fact ≠ logically derived fact.
a_rows_sample.statement: Membership in an assertion-based state K is typed into explicit assertion membership (a in_exp K, a is literally one of K's stored assertions) versus semantic consequence (K models a, semantically entailed but not necessarily stored) — a proposed formal distinction (not yet a theorem) preventing the category error of treating a stored fact as identical to a logically derived one; flagged as essential for Step 262's assertion type.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Merge equality: semantic + identity + provenance dependent. Exact final semantics remain unresolved.
a_rows_sample.statement: Operation test — Merge: Merge(K1,K2) cannot be specified using structural equality alone, since a1=(p,e1) and a2=(p,e2) sharing proposition p could legitimately merge to {a1,a2} (kept separate) or to a single combined-evidence assertion depending on ontology; Merge equality is semantic+identity+provenance dependent, with exact final semantics unresolved.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Supersession requires identity/version distinction. ... collapsing them under semantic equality would destroy the very relation x2 ≻ x1.
a_rows_sample.statement: Operation test — Supersede: if Meaning(x1)=Meaning(x2) but Identity(x1)!=Identity(x2) and x2 supersedes x1, collapsing x1,x2 under semantic equality would destroy the supersession relation x2 succ x1 itself; supersession therefore requires an identity/version distinction, strongly suggesting semantic equality alone cannot serve as the sole equality relation.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Replay requires historical identity/equality independent of current state equality. ... Replay(H1)=K and Replay(H2)=K yet H1 ≠_H H2.
a_rows_sample.statement: Operation test — Replay: two distinct histories H1,H2 (H1 !=_H H2) can replay to the same current state K (Replay(H1)=Replay(H2)=K); Replay is treated by the corpus as a history/audit operation rather than another state transformation, and requires historical identity/equality independent of current-state equality.

a_rows_sample.anchor: | Operation | Structural equality | Semantic equality | Identity | Historical equality | Provenance | Current assessment | Merge...Supersede...Replay...Remove...Revise...Deduplicate...Validate
a_rows_sample.statement: The full operation/equality matrix across Merge, Supersede, Replay, Remove, Revise, Deduplicate, Validate rates each of structural/semantic/identity/historical/provenance equality as insufficient, required, relevant, potentially-required, or context-dependent per operation, with every row's overall status UNRESOLVED, NORMATIVE/DOMAIN-DEPENDENT (Deduplicate), or 'Assessment relation' (Validate); Remove requires identity for correct object targeting (must not remove a2 when removing a1 despite structural identity), Revise cannot use semantic equality as its sole target selector (must not implicitly revise x2 when revising x1 despite x1 equiv_sem x2), Deduplicate cannot be specified until its preservation policy is known (structural/semantic/identity/provenance criteria can each give different results), and Validate shows semantic state equality does not imply identical validation results because validation is a relation over (K,E) pairs, not K alone — reinforcing that not every operation is a state transformation T:K->K.

a_rows_sample.anchor: No single equality relation is adequate for all KnowledgeOS operations. ... KnowledgeOS requires a typed family of relations.
a_rows_sample.statement: Major correction to the kernel concept: rejects the implicit assumption 'KnowledgeOS needs one equality operator', replacing it with 'KnowledgeOS requires a typed family of relations' (=_str, equiv_sem, approx_obs, SameId, equiv_H, equiv_P) that may be connected by formally established implications but must not be conflated.

a_rows_sample.anchor: K1 ≡_K K2 ⟺ ∀O∈𝒪_K: O(K1)=O(K2) ... 𝒪_K is not yet completely closed. Therefore this is a candidate formal definition, not a completed theorem.
a_rows_sample.statement: Candidate formal definition of Knowledge-State equality as purely observational/behavioral: K1 equiv_K K2 iff every permitted state observation O in the (not-yet-closed) set O_K agrees on K1 and K2; explicitly a candidate, not a completed theorem, because O_K is not yet closed.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Equality → Congruence → Quotient → Minimality. This is the correct dependency direction.
a_rows_sample.statement: If K1 equiv_K K2 (no permitted observation distinguishes them) and all mandatory operations preserve that equivalence, equiv_K becomes the congruence relation needed for the minimal quotient K*=H/equiv (Step 260) — establishing the dependency direction Equality -> Congruence -> Quotient -> Minimality as correct.

a_rows_sample.anchor: the observation set is not fully closed; the operation registry is not fully closed; provenance placement remains unresolved; assertion semantics remain unresolved; temporal semantics remain unresolved; identity semantics remain unresolved. The governing prompt explicitly says that final kernel sele

a_rows_sample.anchor: The kernel creates the ecosystem; the company creates value around the ecosystem.
a_rows_sample.statement: Uses the Linux/Red Hat precedent to argue KnowledgeOS's moat is the kernel plus governance plus evidence model (not the AI model, which is commoditized), proposing a Community/Professional/Enterprise revenue-tier structure and a 10-year IPO roadmap.

a_rows_sample.anchor: You cannot protect an idea by secrecy alone. You protect it by combining legal protection, evidence of creation, controlled disclosure, and execution advantage.
a_rows_sample.statement: Distinguishes defensive publication (creates prior art, destroys trade-secret status) from keeping architecture secret or patenting it, and proposes a four-layer IP taxonomy (business concept / architectural / methodological / implementation) each needing a different protection strategy.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Publication ≠ Ownership / Discussion ≠ Transfer / Contribution ≠ Rights / Access ≠ Permission
a_rows_sample.statement: Extends the platform's own 'recording is not asserting authority' discipline into the IP domain, framing an eventual 'KnowledgeOS IP Governance Context' as itself a governance problem about who can know, use, modify, and claim authority over knowledge.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Do you want KnowledgeOS to become: A) an open methodology ... or B) a proprietary enterprise platform ...?
a_rows_sample.statement: States the unresolved strategic fork between open methodology (broad adoption, weaker exclusivity) and proprietary enterprise platform (controlled IP, commercial advantage), noting the IP strategy differs materially by choice.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Open-source the KnowledgeOS Kernel. Commercialize the Digitalization Robot Platform.
a_rows_sample.statement: Recommends an open-core business model (open KnowledgeOS Kernel for trust/ecosystem, commercial Digitalization Robot/Enterprise Platform for revenue), by analogy with Linux Kernel vs Red Hat Enterprise Linux.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The kernel creates the ecosystem; the company creates value around the ecosystem.
a_rows_sample.statement: Repeats the Linux/Red Hat kernel-versus-company argument and the 10-year IPO roadmap found in S0163, without the later IP-protection addendum present in that sibling file.

a_rows_sample.anchor: If you want IPO potential, do not position KnowledgeOS as 'AI chatbot' ... nor 'Documentation tool' ... Position as: The operating system for enterprise knowledge and digital transformation.
a_rows_sample.statement: Argues the commercial positioning category determines addressable market size; 'AI chatbot' is too easy to copy, 'documentation tool' is too small a category for IPO ambitions.

a_rows_sample.anchor: None of this is current state: KnowledgeOS today is a governed knowledge-assurance platform inside the PublicDigit engineering workflow — no company, no product market, no IP portfolio, no listing — stated as fact.
a_rows_sample.statement: States as ESTABLISHED current fact that none of the IPO/IP-protection/open-vs-proprietary product hypotheses reflect KnowledgeOS's actual state today.

b_rows_sample.anchor: You cannot protect an idea by secrecy alone. You protect it by combining legal protection, evidence of creation, controlled disclosure, and execution advantage.
b_rows_sample.statement: States a governing thesis for protecting KnowledgeOS's intellectual property: secrecy alone is insufficient; protection requires combining legal protection, evidence of creation, controlled disclosure, and execution advantage, since a competitor can copy an idea but not a protected system's history, implementation knowledge, and accumulated evidence.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 1. Business concept ... 2. Architectural IP ... 3. Methodological IP ... 4. Implementation IP ... The protection strategy should probably be different for each.
b_rows_sample.statement: Decomposes KnowledgeOS's IP into four layers (business concept, architectural IP, methodological IP, implementation IP), arguing each needs a different protection instrument: the business concept is hard to protect by secrecy, architecture/methodology are stronger as confidential know-how, source code has copyright protection, and genuinely novel technical inventions may justify patent analysis.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Level 0 — Public ... Level 1 — Marketing ... Level 2 — Partner NDA ... Level 3 — Confidential ... Level 4 — Core IP
b_rows_sample.statement: A five-level 'need-to-know' information disclosure model (Public/Marketing/Partner NDA/Confidential/Core IP), specifying what content (e.g. DDD model, bounded contexts, governance model at Level 3; algorithms, decision framework, roadmap at Level 4) is safe to share at each level.

b_rows_sample.anchor: A good DDD test would be: Does IP management have its own: ubiquitous language? lifecycle? invariants? authority? reasons to change? independently owned state? If not, it probably shouldn't become another bounded context.
b_rows_sample.statement: Explicitly cautions against immediately creating an 'IP Governance Context' bounded context merely because IP protection is important, naming this the pattern 'useful concept → immediately turned into a bounded context,' and supplies a six-question DDD legitimacy test (ubiquitous language, lifecycle, invariants, authority, reasons to change, independently owned state) before any concept should become a bounded context.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Are you trying primarily to protect KnowledgeOS from competitors, or are you intending KnowledgeOS itself to become a commercial IP-governance product? ... both may eventually be true, but we should treat them as separate phases rather than merging them now.
b_rows_sample.statement: Separates two distinct design goals that could easily be conflated: protecting KnowledgeOS's own IP from competitors, versus building KnowledgeOS itself into a commercial IP-governance product; recommends treating them as separate phases rather than merging the two designs now.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Claim → Locate → Inspect → Trace → Test → Observe → Classify → Report
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines EEP = {E1..E8}: an eight-stage mandatory pipeline (Claim, Locate, Inspect, Trace, Test, Observe, Classify, Report) that an agent must explicitly state it performed (not necessarily at equal depth) before making an architectural claim; the governing principle is 'an agent must prove an architectural claim from evidence; it must not prove it from plausibility.'

b_rows_sample.anchor: Structural / Behavioral / Governance / Temporal / Assurance / Operational
b_rows_sample.statement: E1 Claim requires a precise, falsifiable proposition (contrasts 'Understand KnowledgeOS' [bad] with a typed claim like 'AuthoritativeDecision -> Provenance' [good]) and distinguishes six claim types: Structural (component depends on component), Behavioral (creating an authoritative object requires provenance), Governance (only an authorized actor can approve), Temporal (superseded decisions excluded from current knowledge), Assurance (rule X deterministically verified), Operational (runtime state fed back into KnowledgeOS).

b_rows_sample.anchor: NotFound(Location) ≠ Absent(System)
b_rows_sample.statement: E2 Locate names search targets (README, docs/, ADR/, architecture/, src/, tests/, schemas/, migrations/, config/, CI/CD, hooks/, agents/, runtime configuration) and states the negative-evidence rule: finding nothing in one location does not prove system-wide absence; the agent must report 'no evidence found in the inspected locations' rather than 'the capability does not exist.'

b_rows_sample.anchor: DeclaredArchitecture ... ImplementedArchitecture ... VerifiedBehavior
b_rows_sample.statement: E3 Inspect distinguishes evidence types by artifact kind: documentation establishes DeclaredArchitecture, source code establishes ImplementedArchitecture, tests establish VerifiedBehavior — these are different evidence types and must not be conflated.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The objective is not simply finding matching names. It is establishing semantic linkage.
b_rows_sample.statement: E4 Trace: given a claim Decision -> Implementation, the agent follows the chain Decision -> ADR/record -> change request -> PR -> commit -> artifact -> deployment, aiming at semantic linkage rather than textual name-matching; defines traceability-strength scale T0 (no link) < T1 (textual similarity) < T2 (explicit reference) < T3 (machine-readable identifier) < T4 (verified causal/implementation relationship), e.g. an ADR-042 identifier appearing in a commit is stronger evidence than shared wording.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Static / Unit / Integration / Architecture / Deployment / Runtime
b_rows_sample.statement: E5 Test: for a behavioral claim (e.g. 'authoritative knowledge cannot be created without provenance'), execute a concrete test (create(authoritative=true, provenance=null) expecting Reject) and classify it on a six-level test hierarchy (Static, Unit, Integration, Architecture, Deployment, Runtime) since the test type affects what the result actually proves.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Static code is not enough for operational claims.
b_rows_sample.statement: E6 Observe: operational claims (e.g. 'Nexus runs rootless') require inspecting actual runtime/deployment/logs/metrics/events, not merely a static configuration file such as a Podman config.

b_rows_sample.anchor: FACT | INFERENCE | TARGET | GAP
b_rows_sample.statement: E7 Classify: every finding receives one of four epistemic classifications — FACT (directly evidenced, e.g. a Containerfile using a specified base image, via E2/E3), INFERENCE (a reasoned interpretation that must not be presented as established fact without stronger evidence, e.g. 'this repo appears to implement the Evidence bounded context'), TARGET (intended future architecture unless implementation proves otherwise, e.g. 'KnowledgeOS should provide closed-loop governance'), GAP (Expected ≠ Observed, e.g. architecture requires provenance but authoritative records can currently be created without it).

b_rows_sample.anchor: CLAIM / FACTS / EVIDENCE / INFERENCE / VERIFICATION / GAP / TARGET / CONFIDENCE
b_rows_sample.statement: E8 Report: the final report must never collapse evidence into one narrative; it uses a fixed section format (Claim, Facts, Evidence, Inference, Verification, Gap, Target, Confidence) 'to prevent architectural contamination,' illustrated with a worked standard-agent-output example ending in STATUS: CONFORMANT / CONFIDENCE: HIGH.

b_rows_sample.anchor: C0=Unknown, C1=Weak, C2=Moderate, C3=Strong, C4=Verified
b_rows_sample.statement: Proposes a five-level ordinal confidence scale (C0 Unknown .. C4 Verified) as superior to arbitrary percentages; argues LLMConfidence ≠ EvidenceConfidence because an LLM stating '95% confident' does not establish a quantitative probability, whereas evidence-derived confidence must derive from evidence quality; also distinguishes EvidenceStrength from Confidence (strong evidence can still leave interpretive ambiguity).

b_rows_sample.anchor: If evidence is insufficient, the agent MUST preserve UNKNOWN.
b_rows_sample.statement: States an agent stopping rule / anti-hallucination rule: when evidence is insufficient the agent must preserve UNKNOWN rather than fill the gap from general knowledge; explicitly frames stopping with disclosed uncertainty (e.g. 'implementation is supported, enforcement is unverified') as a successful investigation, not a failure.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Mode A — Architecture reconstruction ... Mode E — Knowledge reconstruction
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines five repository investigation modes with distinct evidence focus — A Architecture reconstruction (Structure+Dependencies), B Governance verification (Authority+Decision+Process), C Assurance verification (Rule+Test+Evidence), D Runtime verification (Deployment+Observation), E Knowledge reconstruction (Meaning+Provenance+Validity) — and requires the agent to select the mode before searching, and to follow a Broad->Narrow->Exact->Trace search strategy (e.g. 'provenance' -> 'source_id' -> 'createKnowledge' -> tests -> runtime).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Can the invariant be bypassed?
b_rows_sample.statement: Warns against name-based conclusions (e.g. a class named ProvenanceService does not itself prove provenance is enforced — the agent must ask who calls it, when, what happens on failure, whether the result is persisted, and whether it can be bypassed); defines the enforcement test 'can the invariant be bypassed? If yes, Enforcement<Strong,' illustrated by Experiment 2 where a ProvenanceService exists but developers can insert DB records without provenance, yielding Declared=Yes, Enforced=No, verdict PARTIAL.

b_rows_sample.anchor: C1 ... provenance required ... direct persistence | C7 ... feedback path exists ... finding dead-end
b_rows_sample.statement: Extends the Step 120 C1-C7 constitution with a bypass-question and bypass-test matrix per invariant: C1 can authoritative knowledge bypass provenance via direct persistence; C2 can approval bypass authority via unauthorized promotion; C3 can inference be promoted to authority without validation; C4 can stale knowledge appear current via stale retrieval; C5 can verification results be fabricated/irreproducible via inconsistent rerun; C6 can governed actions occur without traceability via untracked action; C7 can findings disappear without governance closure via finding dead-end — presented as a practical assurance test suite.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 1. State the claim. ... 10. Never promote inference to authority.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines a ten-item 'agent execution contract' every KnowledgeOS-aware engineering agent must follow: state the claim; identify evidence sources; inspect implementation; trace relationships; execute relevant tests where possible; inspect runtime where required; separate fact from inference; report uncertainty; identify gaps; never promote inference to authority.

b_rows_sample.anchor: SameAuthority / SameEvidenceRules / SameConstitution / SameEpistemicDiscipline
b_rows_sample.statement: Proposes that Claude and Codex should share the Evidence Execution Protocol as a common agent-instruction layer: the important symmetry is not identical configuration but SameAuthority, SameEvidenceRules, SameConstitution, SameEpistemicDiscipline, while Claude and Codex harnesses remain operationally different — diagrammed as KnowledgeOS -> Evidence Protocol -> {Claude Harness, Codex Harness} -> Same Truth.

b_rows_sample.anchor: This is a pointer/behavior contract, not a duplicate knowledge repository.
b_rows_sample.statement: Sketches a minimal KnowledgeOS-aware AGENTS.md operating contract (consult authoritative sources, verify current validity, preserve provenance, distinguish fact from inference, use deterministic checks where available, record material engineering actions against authorization, never treat local agent memory as authoritative) and states that .claude/ and .codex/ should likewise hold tools/hooks/workflow/session-behavior/verification-procedures/pointers-to-KnowledgeOS but must not become the enterprise architecture authority themselves — the goal is OperationalSymmetry without KnowledgeDuplication.

b_rows_sample.anchor: # Evidence Execution Report ... Open questions: ...
b_rows_sample.statement: Specifies a standard 'Evidence Execution Report' template with fields Claim, Scope, Evidence inspected, Implementation, Tests executed, Runtime observations, FACT, INFERENCE, TARGET, GAP, Conformance, Confidence, Open questions, as the mandatory end-of-investigation deliverable.

b_rows_sample.anchor: AgentAssuranceScore = f(EvidenceCompleteness, Traceability, Verification, EpistemicDiscipline)
b_rows_sample.statement: Proposes judging an agent by EvidenceQuality rather than AnswerQuality: an articulate but unsupported answer should score poorly, a cautious evidence-backed answer highly; defines AgentAssuranceScore = f(EvidenceCompleteness, Traceability, Verification, EpistemicDiscipline), explicitly preferable to measuring only LLMAnswerSimilarity; further defines Completeness = VerifiedLinks/RequiredLinks for a claim needing n evidence links, notes critical missing links should carry higher weight (WeightedCompleteness preferable to plain Completeness), and gives Authority as an example of a critical link whose absence should not be masked by ten present technical links.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Claim ├── supportedBy → Evidence ... └── classifiedAs → Status
b_rows_sample.statement: Observes that an agent's own investigation becomes graph data (Claim -supportedBy-> Evidence, -verifiedBy-> Test, -observedAt-> Runtime, -interpretedAs-> Finding, -classifiedAs-> Status), so the process of understanding the architecture itself becomes part of KnowledgeOS knowledge.

a_notations: Conformance(C_i)=Architecture cap Implementation cap Verification cap Evidence

group_evidence.why_grouped: explicit agent-stated uncertainty: 'knowledgeos-evidence-execution-protocol' POSSIBLY relates to 'knowledgeos-constitution-implementation-conformance-test-model' (batch B0025). Note: Step 122: an agent-executable eight-stage evidence protocol (Claim->Locate->Inspect->Trace->Test->Observe->Classify->Report) turning the prior architecture-conformance method into an operational Claude/Codex-shared discipline, with traceability-strength scale T0-T4, epistemic classification FACT/INFERENCE/TARGET/GAP, confidence scale C0-C4, negative-evidence rule, anti-hallucination stopping rule, bypass-test matrix against the C1-C7 constitution, a ten-item agent execution contract, an Evidence Execution Report template, an AgentAssuranceScore metric, and a closing self-governance loop (ConstitutionalHealthCheck, ConstitutionalDrift).

a_rows_sample.anchor: We now have the complete target model. The next step is to test whether the actual KnowledgeOS/EKS ecosystem closes the loop in practice. Expected→Observed→Detected→Classified→Governed→Remediated→Verified→Recorded.
a_rows_sample.statement: Frames Step 119 as testing whether the actual ecosystem closes the loop via the target Expected->Observed->Detected->Classified->Governed->Remediated->Verified->Recorded.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 119.1 — The control-loop hypothesis ... KnowledgeOS=ReferenceState+Observation+Comparison+Governance+Action+Verification+Learning. The essential operation is Compare(Expected,Observed) followed by a controlled response.
a_rows_sample.statement: States the control-loop hypothesis KnowledgeOS=ReferenceState+Observation+Comparison+Governance+Action+Verification+Learning centered on Compare(Expected,Observed).

a_rows_sample.anchor: 119.2 — Reference state ... architecture, ADR, implementation constitution, coding standard, policy, approved configuration, governance decision, security rule, deployment specification. The reference state is R_t.
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines R_t as the reference state drawn from nine possible authoritative sources.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 119.3 — Experiment 1: Is there a reference? ... Component A differs from expected state. Expected according to what? If no authoritative source can be identified: ExpectedState=Unknown. Verdict: Reference missing
a_rows_sample.statement: Experiment 1: a 'differs from expected state' report with no identifiable authoritative source yields ExpectedState=Unknown, verdict Reference missing.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 119.4 — Reference hierarchy ... EnterprisePolicy, ArchitectureDecision, DomainRule, ImplementationRule, RuntimeExpectation. These may conflict. Therefore the system needs precedence semantics.
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines a five-level reference hierarchy that may conflict, requiring precedence semantics.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 119.5 — Experiment 2: conflicting references ... Architecture: PostgreSQL required. Team documentation: MySQL allowed. Which one governs? If KnowledgeOS cannot determine authority: GovernanceAmbiguity. Verdict: AMBIGUOUS. This is a semantic problem, not a search problem.
a_rows_sample.statement: Experiment 2: conflicting PostgreSQL-vs-MySQL references with no determinable authority yield GovernanceAmbiguity, verdict AMBIGUOUS, explicitly a semantic problem not a search problem.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 119.6 — Expected-state provenance ... ExpectedState→Source→Authority→Validity. Without this, agents can retrieve outdated or non-authoritative expectations.
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines ExpectedState->Source->Authority->Validity as required provenance, without which agents risk retrieving outdated or non-authoritative expectations.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 119.7 — Experiment 3 ... Agent retrieves a Markdown document describing the desired architecture. The document has no approval status. Expected: useful information, but Authority=Unknown. Verdict: PASS
a_rows_sample.statement: Experiment 3: an unapproved Markdown architecture document is useful but leaves Authority=Unknown; verdict PASS.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 119.8 — Observation ... Expected→Observed. Observation may come from Git, CI, deployment, Kubernetes, Podman, monitoring, filesystem, API, security scanner, architecture checker. The observation needs identity and timestamp.
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines Expected->Observed across ten possible observation sources, requiring identity and timestamp.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 119.9 — Experiment 4 ... Scanner produces component=X, dependency=Y. No timestamp or environment exists. Expected: observation exists but contextual provenance is incomplete. Verdict: PARTIAL
a_rows_sample.statement: Experiment 4: a scanner result with no timestamp/environment has incomplete contextual provenance; verdict PARTIAL.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 119.10 — Comparison ... Compare(R_t,O_t). This must be deterministic wherever possible. ExpectedDependency(A,B)=false, ObservedDependency(A,B)=true, therefore Violation=True.
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines the central Compare(R_t,O_t) operation, required to be deterministic wherever possible, illustrated by a dependency-existence violation.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 119.11 — Experiment 5 ... A human reviewer visually compares two architecture diagrams. Expected: potentially useful review, but it is not deterministic assurance. Verdict: Human verification rather than Deterministic control
a_rows_sample.statement: Experiment 5: human visual diagram comparison is Human verification, not Deterministic control.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 119.12 — Deterministic comparison ... expected.json, observed.json → deterministic comparator → DIFF. This produces reproducible results.
a_rows_sample.statement: Describes a deterministic comparator pipeline (expected.json/observed.json->comparator->DIFF) producing reproducible results.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 119.13 — Experiment 6 ... Same inputs produce different compliance results depending on which agent evaluates them. Expected: weak assurance. Verdict: NON-DETERMINISTIC
a_rows_sample.statement: Experiment 6: identical inputs yielding different compliance results across evaluating agents is weak assurance, verdict NON-DETERMINISTIC.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 119.14 — Classification ... A difference is not automatically a governance violation. Difference→Classification. ExpectedChange, ApprovedException, TemporaryDrift, Violation, Unknown.
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines Difference->Classification across five categories, stating a difference is not automatically a violation.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 119.15 — Experiment 7 ... Deployment differs from architecture because an approved emergency exception is active. Expected: Difference≠Violation. Verdict: PASS
a_rows_sample.statement: Experiment 7: a deployment difference covered by an approved emergency exception is Difference≠Violation; verdict PASS.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 119.16 — Governance routing ... Classification→GovernancePath. Architecture violation→Architecture Governance. Security violation→Security Governance. Operational failure→Operations.
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines Classification->GovernancePath with three example routing mappings.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 119.17 — Experiment 8 ... All findings are routed to one generic queue. Expected: basic issue management exists, but governance semantics are weak. Verdict: PARTIAL
a_rows_sample.statement: Experiment 8: routing all findings to one generic queue has weak governance semantics; verdict PARTIAL.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 119.18 — Governance decision ... Finding→Decision. Remediate, AcceptRisk, GrantException, ChangeRule, RejectFinding.
a_rows_sample.statement: Lists five possible Finding->Decision outcomes.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 119.19 — Experiment 9 ... Finding disappears after a human clicks Resolved. No decision exists. Expected: issue lifecycle exists, governance decision semantics are not proven. Verdict: PASS
a_rows_sample.statement: Experiment 9: a finding resolved by a human click with no decision record proves issue lifecycle but not governance decision semantics; verdict PASS.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Step 117 established the forward trace Intent→Decision→Authority→Implementation→Verification→Runtime→Evidence→Knowledge. Now we test the reverse direction. When reality deviates from what was intended, can KnowledgeOS turn that deviation into governed engineering action and eventually verified knowl
b_rows_sample.statement: Frames Step 118 as testing the reverse of Step 117's forward trace, defining the target reverse loop Runtime->Observation->Finding->Governance->Decision->Remediation->Verification.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 118.1 — Why the reverse direction matters ... A system that only records what happened is essentially an audit system. A system that can detect Expected≠Actual and initiate a governed response has Feedback. Audit≠Control. Traceability≠ClosedLoopGovernance.
b_rows_sample.statement: States Audit≠Control and Traceability≠ClosedLoopGovernance: recording history is distinct from detecting deviation and initiating governed feedback.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 118.2 — The expected-state model ... S_expected and S_observed. Delta=S_observed-S_expected. If Delta=0 we have conformance. If Delta≠0 we have a candidate discrepancy.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines the expected-state model S_expected/S_observed with Delta=S_observed-S_expected, Delta=0 conformant, Delta≠0 a candidate discrepancy.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 118.3 — Experiment 1 ... Architecture says Nexus must run using the approved containerized architecture. Runtime observation matches. Then S_expected=S_observed. Result: CONFORMANT
b_rows_sample.statement: Experiment 1: matching architecture-specified and observed container deployment yields S_expected=S_observed, classified CONFORMANT, no escalation required.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 118.4 — Experiment 2 ... Architecture says approved container deployment. Runtime shows legacy VM deployment still active. Then S_expected≠S_observed. Result: DISCREPANCY. This is the starting point of the reverse loop.
b_rows_sample.statement: Experiment 2: a legacy VM still active against an approved-container architecture is S_expected≠S_observed, classified DISCREPANCY, the starting point of the reverse loop.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 118.5 — Observation is not yet a finding ... Observation: LegacyDeploymentActive. We do not yet automatically have Finding: ArchitectureViolation. A rule must interpret the observation.
b_rows_sample.statement: States Observation≠Finding: an observation requires rule interpretation before becoming a finding.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 118.6 — Rule evaluation ... Rule+Observation→Evaluation. Rule: LegacyDeploymentForbidden. Observation: LegacyDeploymentActive. Then Evaluation=Violation.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines Rule+Observation->Evaluation, illustrated by LegacyDeploymentForbidden+LegacyDeploymentActive->Violation.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 118.7 — Experiment 3 ... Monitoring detects a VM that is not described in the current architecture. Expected: Observation. Only if a relevant architecture rule applies do we create Finding. Result: PASS
b_rows_sample.statement: Experiment 3: an undescribed VM is merely an Observation until a relevant rule applies to create a Finding; result PASS.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 118.8 — Finding creation ... Finding=(Rule,Expected,Observed,Evidence,Impact,Scope,Timestamp). This allows the finding to be independently understood.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines the Finding=(Rule,Expected,Observed,Evidence,Impact,Scope,Timestamp) tuple for independently understandable findings.

type_signature.codomain: Rule x Expected x Observed x Evidence x Impact x Scope x Timestamp

b_rows_sample.anchor: 118.9 — Experiment 4 ... Finding says only 'Architecture violation detected.' No rule or observation is attached. Expected: weak finding semantics. Result: PARTIAL
b_rows_sample.statement: Experiment 4: a finding with no attached rule/observation has weak finding semantics; result PARTIAL.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 118.10 — Strong finding ... Rule: R-17, Expected: rootless container deployment, Observed: privileged VM process, Evidence: runtime observation O-41, Detected: 2026-08-28. Now Finding→Evidence is explicit.
b_rows_sample.statement: Presents a strong worked finding record with explicit Rule/Expected/Observed/Evidence/Detected fields, making Finding->Evidence explicit.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 118.11 — Finding ownership ... Who owns the response? Team, DomainArchitect, Security, Operations, ArchitectureBoard.
b_rows_sample.statement: Frames finding ownership as a governance question with five candidate owner categories.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 118.12 — Experiment 5 ... Finding exists. No responsible owner exists. Expected: GovernanceGap. Result: PASS. A detection system without accountable ownership cannot reliably close the loop.
b_rows_sample.statement: Experiment 5: an unowned finding is a GovernanceGap, since accountable ownership is required to reliably close the loop; result PASS.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 118.13 — Finding severity ... Severity from Priority. Severity=High describes impact. Priority=High describes response urgency. These should not be silently conflated.
b_rows_sample.statement: Distinguishes Severity (impact) from Priority (response urgency), stating they must not be conflated.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 118.14 — Experiment 6 ... A low-impact architecture deviation blocks a production deployment. Expected: potential Severity=Low but Priority=High. Result: PASS
b_rows_sample.statement: Experiment 6: a low-impact but deployment-blocking deviation is potential Severity=Low/Priority=High; result PASS.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 118.15 — Finding → Governance ... Finding→GovernanceProcess. change management, architecture review, exception process, remediation workflow, incident process. The system must determine which path applies.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines Finding->GovernanceProcess routing across five possible governance processes.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 118.16 — Experiment 7 ... Security finding occurs. It is routed into an architecture review process. Expected: potential governance mismatch if security policy requires a different path. Result: OBS
b_rows_sample.statement: Experiment 7: a security finding routed to architecture review instead of a required security path is a potential governance mismatch, classified OBS.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 118.17 — Governance classification ... Finding→Classification→GovernancePath. ArchitectureDeviation→ArchitectureGovernance. SecurityViolation→SecurityGovernance. OperationalFailure→Operations.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines Finding->Classification->GovernancePath with three example classification-to-path mappings.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 118.18 — Experiment 8 ... A finding can be classified automatically based on rule metadata. Expected: Classification→GovernancePath. Result: PASS provided the classification is deterministic and auditable.
b_rows_sample.statement: Experiment 8: automatic finding classification is acceptable (PASS) only if deterministic and auditable.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 118.19 — Governance escalation ... Not every finding needs board-level intervention. FindingSeverity+FindingType+Scope→EscalationLevel.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines EscalationLevel as a function of FindingSeverity+FindingType+Scope.

a_rows_sample.anchor: KnowledgeOS is not primarily a knowledge storage platform. It is a Knowledge Governance Domain Platform. The core domain is: Creating, governing, validating, evolving, and delivering trusted Knowledge Products.
a_rows_sample.statement: The central architectural correction of the v3 proposal: KnowledgeOS should be redefined away from a knowledge-storage platform toward a Knowledge Governance Domain Platform whose core domain is creating, governing, validating, evolving, and delivering trusted Knowledge Products.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Knowledge Governance Context / Knowledge Product Context / Knowledge Evidence Context / Knowledge Semantic Context / Knowledge Delivery Context / Knowledge Intelligence Context / Platform Administration Context
a_rows_sample.statement: Proposes seven bounded contexts for KnowledgeOS (Governance, Product [core domain], Evidence, Semantic, Delivery, Intelligence, Platform Administration), each with stated purpose, aggregate, and domain rules; the Product context's KnowledgeProduct aggregate contains Decision, Method, Binding, Rule, Constraint, EvidenceReference as its knowledge elements.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Important: The graph is not the source of truth. The domain model is. The graph is a projection.
a_rows_sample.statement: The Knowledge Semantic Context's graph/ontology model is explicitly a projection of the domain model, never the source of truth itself.

a_rows_sample.anchor: AI is NOT the core domain. AI is a capability... AI cannot create authority. Authority comes from: Governance Context
a_rows_sample.statement: AI is modelled as a capability of the Knowledge Intelligence Context (retrieval, reasoning, recommendations, summarization, impact analysis) and explicitly cannot create authority; authority derives solely from the Governance Context.

a_rows_sample.statement: Recommends freezing an architectural decision (ADR-KOS-001) adopting DDD plus Hexagonal Architecture with KnowledgeProduct as the core domain aggregate, framed as giving KnowledgeOS the same architectural discipline already applied elsewhere (bounded contexts, aggregates, domain events, governance rules, evidence-driven trust, AI as a controlled consumer).

b_rows_sample.statement: Lists five candidate Architecture Decision Records (ADR-KOS-01 modular bounded-context platform; ADR-KOS-02 Assurance Graph as cross-context projection; ADR-KOS-03 common semantic contract for agent integrations; ADR-KOS-04 agent-local files as pointer/operational layers, not authoritative knowledge; ADR-KOS-05 deterministic assurance authoritative wherever mechanically verifiable), explicitly marked PROPOSED pending validation against the actual organizational architecture.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Result: only TWO of the five are fundamental architectural absences -- persistent epistemic identity and historical belief evolution
b_rows_sample.statement: LLM-comparison validation (5 candidates, validated not assumed): persistent epistemic identity -- FUNDAMENTAL ABSENCE (a stateless generative model cannot possess it by construction; scaffolding like RAG cannot grant identity, only look up stored identities); historical belief evolution -- FUNDAMENTAL ABSENCE (generation is stateless, no belief to evolve); provenance preservation, contradiction management, justification accountability -- each a DEGRADATION, not an absence (an LLM can be scaffolded to approximate each, weakly). Conclusion: the constitutional justification rests on exactly the two fundamental absences (mapping to laws 1 and 11), not a general 'LLMs are bad at X' claim.

a_rows_sample.anchor: > **Can contradiction be represented without confusing it with uncertainty, absence, insufficient evidence, theory incompleteness, unobservability, or non-assessment?**
a_rows_sample.statement: Commissions KR-CONTR-2026-09: mission is to determine whether contradiction can be represented without collapsing into uncertainty/absence/insufficient-evidence/theory-incompleteness/unobservability/non-assessment, whether the current 3-valued domain is expressive enough, what the minimum evaluation domain must contain, whether a 4th value C is actually necessary, and whether contradiction has kernel implications.

a_rows_sample.anchor: > **Do not start from the assumption that KnowledgeOS needs a fourth truth value.**
a_rows_sample.statement: States the single governing constraint on the experiment: it must discover the minimum required representation rather than confirm a predetermined four-valued design; possible outcomes explicitly include three values sufficient, four necessary, more than four necessary, a structured domain, contradiction belonging outside Sat, or the question needing reformulation.

a_rows_sample.statement: Proposes an initial (non-final) formal definition of contradiction: Contr(p,Kt) iff Pos(p,Kt) AND Neg(p,Kt), where Pos/Neg mean p/not-p is represented/committed to in the epistemic state; explicitly to be tested against provenance, confidence, temporal, source, context, retraction, supersession, coexistence, and conflicting-observation/interpretation/model differences.

a_rows_sample.statement: Requires the experiment to preserve a seven-layer non-collapse chain (World≠Observation≠Evidence≠Interpretation≠EpistemicState≠Evaluation≠KnowledgeAttribution) and forbids giving the simulated agent access to hidden ground truth: Contr(p,Kt) must not mean 'the world makes both p and not-p true' but that the epistemic representation simultaneously contains incompatible commitments about p.

R(x)\neq R(y).
$$
a_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes representation adequacy for this experiment: a candidate representation R:S->D is adequate iff for every required distinction pair (x,y) in R_req, x≠y implies R(x)≠R(y); a structured representation may satisfy this even when two conditions share the same primary 'value' field, so uniqueness of the primary value is not required.

b_rows_sample.statement: The experiment turns adequacy into a graph-coloring/injectivity problem over the required-distinction graph, finding chromatic number chi(G)=3; carefully qualified: this does not establish the correct evaluation domain has three values, only that at least three distinguishable flat classes are required given this distinction set and adequacy criterion -- and separately, nine 'no determinate value' conditions cannot be adequately represented by any flat value domain regardless of cardinality, making the obstruction structural rather than cardinal.

States a methodological principle from the chromatic-number finding: colourability only proves pairwise coding capacity under the chosen abstraction, it does not establish that resulting values carry the required semantic or operational meaning -- cardinality sufficiency is not semantic adequacy.

a_rows_sample.statement: 'Mission is ENACTED' replaces 'mission is implicit' as a stronger and more accurate statement: the platform is not describing its mission, it is already behaving according to it. The reviewer's hierarchy is adopted structurally: documents become the lowest layer of the model, never its centre.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The six concepts ... MISSION · ENGINEERING KNOWLEDGE · ENGINEERING CAPABILITY · ENGINEERING ARTIFACT · PRODUCT KNOWLEDGE SPACE · PRODUCT
a_rows_sample.statement: Six concepts defined by responsibility/lifecycle/owner/dependencies, none defined by a folder: MISSION (why the platform exists; enacted->candidate->ratified, currently enacted-unratified; owner: sponsor; depends on nothing, the root); ENGINEERING KNOWLEDGE (rules/methods/decisions that transfer between products; ES-006.1 ladder; owner DA for policy, sponsor+ARB for method; depends on MISSION); ENGINEERING CAPABILITY (protect exactly one invariant; observed->...->promoted; shape frozen under PGP-01..05; depends on MISSION+KNOWLEDGE); ENGINEERING ARTIFACT (carry knowledge in a representation, never the knowledge itself; statuses.yaml 8 states lint-enforced; owner field; depends on KNOWLEDGE); PRODUCT KNOWLEDGE SPACE (hold one product's concepts/language/contexts/bindings; authored today, generated as hypothesis n=0; owner product team; depends on KNOWLEDGE method + PRODUCT subject); PRODUCT (deliver business value; own delivery lifecycle; owner product team; depends on PKS + CAPABILITY).

a_rows_sample.anchor: PURPOSE | no decision has been changed by consulting the mission (enacted, UNRATIFIED — D-5 pending)
a_rows_sample.statement: PURPOSE also supports no observable decision: no decision has changed by consulting the mission, and its use in the ontology pass was a test, not a decision. Judgment suspended: an unratified purpose cannot yet support decisions; D-5 decides whether it starts to.

a_rows_sample.anchor: "TWO MISSIONS" IS WITHDRAWN — 2026-08-02 ... I mislabelled a CONSTRAINT as a MISSION ... THE MISSION IS IMPLICIT BUT EVIDENCED, NOT VACANT
a_rows_sample.statement: The document's own 'two missions' framing (elaborated in Part 1 below) is withdrawn: AIP-14 was mislabelled as a mission when it is a constraint/cost-control (it ships with a per-iteration metric and over-evolution trigger, which a mission does not have — and the document itself calls AIP-14 'a cost control, not a boundary' four paragraphs after naming it a mission, a direct self-contradiction). The replacing finding (corrected further at REV 2, recorded in KnowledgeOS_Vision_Mission_Clarification.md): the mission is implicit but evidenced, not vacant — evidenced by eight artifacts, none PublicDigit-specific (ES-005.3's litmus, ES-006.4's harvest question, ES-006.1's ladder, the Reference Architecture's independence clause, the capability-agnostic pattern, the reserved registry/ namespace, the pre-positioned Platform-equiv-Adoption split, ES-005.4). 'Vacant' was a third instance of one error: artifact absence != concept absence.

a_rows_sample.anchor: THERE ARE TWO MISSION STATEMENTS IN CANON, AND ONLY ONE IS ADOPTED ... M-A ADOPTED · M-B PROPOSED · UNAPPROVED
a_rows_sample.statement: Two mission statements found in canon: M-A (AIP-14/ADR-AIP-02/R-23), 'the platform exists solely to improve delivery of PublicDigit; every iteration produces measurable progress on a PublicDigit feature; platform-only iterations are exceptional and require explicit ARB approval' — ADOPTED. M-B (Product Discovery Charter), 'there is a market for an AI-native Knowledge Operating System for software engineering whose core promise is preserving architectural knowledge, enforcing engineering governance, and enabling AI agents to reason consistently across complex software systems' — PROPOSED, UNAPPROVED, explicitly a hypothesis.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The mission, as adopted ... KnowledgeOS exists to improve the delivery of PublicDigit by governing how engineering work is planned, approved, executed, verified and evolved — in a form that is independent of project, programming language and execution provider
a_rows_sample.statement: The adopted mission combines two observed halves: the purpose from AIP-14 (improve delivery of PublicDigit) and the form from the Reference Architecture section 1 (governs how engineering work is planned, approved, executed, verified, and evolved, independent of project, programming language, or execution provider). The apparent contradiction between 'solely for PublicDigit' and 'independent of project' is resolved: AIP-14 constrains WHY work is undertaken, the Reference Architecture constrains WHAT is built — build portable things only when doing so advances this product; AIP-14's enforcement is an iteration-cost metric and an over-evolution review, a cost control, not a scope boundary. M-B is a different mission with a different customer ('organizations' rather than 'the engineering team'), not adopted, gate shut.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Part 2 — Responsibilities (R-1..R-8)
a_rows_sample.statement: Eight responsibilities, each traced to an artifact: R-1 govern the engineering lifecycle (EEP); R-2 hold the authority model (ES-001); R-3 hold the method (Round39-MC, Round47-OP, workbooks); R-4 define the shape of a capability (Platform_Capability_Pattern FROZEN, PGP-01..05); R-5 make governed knowledge retrievable and enforceable (Knowledge-Constitution, 18 lint rules, portal); R-6 harvest reusable knowledge from operational evidence (ES-006.4/ES-006.1 — the responsibility exists, but 0 traversals); R-7 keep runtime vocabulary out of governance (asserted, artifact missing); R-8 refuse to approve its own work (EEP: automation does not approve itself).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Part 3 — Non-responsibilities (N-1..N-10) ... N-1 is breached today. Recording the breach is this document's act; repairing it is not
a_rows_sample.statement: Ten non-responsibilities, each traced: N-1 business/domain knowledge (elections, voters, adjudication) — BREACHED: ES-005.1 names PublicDigit and hard-codes .claude/; N-2 a product's evidence records; N-3 any register's contents (only the governing rule); N-4 a runtime's vocabulary; N-5 its own approval; N-6 governance defined by automation; N-7 duplicated knowledge (ES-005.4); N-8 materialized consolidations (BRM-1 retired extraction-by-copy); N-9 a product's PKS; N-10 orchestrators/workflow engines/state machines (Reference Architecture section 1: deliberately, and not forever, until operational evidence demonstrates insufficiency). N-1's breach is recorded but not repaired here.

a_rows_sample.anchor: MQ-1 | Which mission governs — M-A (adopted, PublicDigit-serving) or M-B (proposed, product-seeking)?
a_rows_sample.statement: MQ-1: which mission governs, M-A or M-B — they have different customers and are not reconcilable by drafting — authority: sponsor + DA.

a_rows_sample.anchor: MQ-2..MQ-7 | Who owns KnowledgeOS as a whole? ... Is N-1's breach to be repaired ... Is PD-3's individual ownership intentional ... is the harvest responsibility even required ... Does N-10 still hold ... What would falsify M-A?
a_rows_sample.statement: Six further open questions: MQ-2 who owns KnowledgeOS as a whole, given three authority systems none of which spans them (sponsor+DA+ARB jointly); MQ-3 is N-1's breach to be repaired or is the invariant wrong (ARB); MQ-4 is PD-3's individual ownership intentional/a succession risk (DA); MQ-5 under M-A is the harvest responsibility (R-6) even required, since a reuse loop may be out of mission if the platform serves one product (ARB); MQ-6 does N-10 still hold or has evidence of insufficiency accumulated (ARB); MQ-7 what would falsify M-A, since a mission with no falsifier is not a mission (sponsor).

a_rows_sample.anchor: The finding ... KnowledgeOS has TWO missions. One is adopted; the other is what everyone has been designing for ... Almost every architectural difficulty in this track is a symptom of designing under M-B while governed by M-A
a_rows_sample.statement: The document's headline finding (before its own later withdrawal, recorded above): almost every architectural difficulty in the track is a symptom of designing under M-B (organizations as customers) while governed by M-A (serve PublicDigit): under M-A, extraction is premature and 'knowledgeos init' is out of mission, while under M-B they are the goal/the product; under M-A the harvest loop is optional (MQ-5) while under M-B it is essential; under M-A 'no second adopting product' is not a gap while under M-B it is the blocker; under M-A platform-only iterations need ARB approval while under M-B they are normal work. MQ-1 is not a documentation question — until answered, the same evidence supports opposite conclusions.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Concepts × kind × owner (C-1..C-13)
a_rows_sample.statement: Thirteen concepts classified by kind and owner: C-1 VISION (purpose, sponsor); C-2 MISSION (purpose, sponsor, enacted-unratified); C-3 ENGINEERING STRATEGY (purpose->governance bridge, ARB/sponsor); C-4 ENGINEERING PRINCIPLE (governance, DA/sponsor+ARB/platform depending on series); C-5 DESIGN POLICY DP-n (governance, DA via Catalog); C-6 ENGINEERING CAPABILITY (capability, its DP-n not a domain); C-7 ENGINEERING KNOWLEDGE (knowledge, DA/sponsor+ARB); C-8 ENGINEERING ARTIFACT (representation, its owner field); C-9 KNOWLEDGE SPACE (container, the space's own owner); C-10 PKS (container, product team); C-11 PRODUCT (application, product team); C-12 RUNTIME ADAPTER (runtime element, no owner found); C-13 PROJECTION (projection, the generating space).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Package 1 — D-9 · Derive the Platform Cost metric; run the AIP-14 over-evolution check (FIRST — it gates the docket itself)
a_rows_sample.statement: Package 1 (D-9): compute the AIP-14 Platform Cost metric for recent iterations and rule whether the over-evolution review fires, since the tripwire cannot fire if the metric is never computed. Supporting: ~48h produced 20+ platform-only documents and zero PublicDigit feature progress in this track (self-declared). Opposing: dense real product delivery ran in parallel; the platform work was commissioned, not drift. Downstream: whether Packages 2-10 are worked now at all. Authority: ARB. Recommendation: ADOPT, run the check before anything else on this docket.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Package 1 — AMENDMENT (REV 2): the metric must be DEFINED before it is RUN ... D-9 therefore splits into D-9a (DEFINE) and D-9b (RUN)
a_rows_sample.statement: A PA review challenge is accepted: should AIP-14 measure platform work by document count, engineering effort, elapsed time, or delivered capability, since document count can be misleading? This corrects the docket's own defect: Package 1's supporting-evidence line presupposed document count as the metric, exactly the undecided question — that line is downgraded from trigger evidence to illustration pending metric definition. D-9 splits: D-9a defines the Platform Cost measurement basis (recommend delivered-capability + effort, reject raw document count, since one strategic decision may produce many small governance documents while a large implementation may produce few); D-9b runs the over-evolution check using the defined basis, immediately after D-9a. Package 1 stays first on the docket; what changed is that the gate must be built before it can be closed.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Package 2 — D-5 · Ratify the enacted mission (one signature; unblocks the frame)
a_rows_sample.statement: Package 2 (D-5): ratify (or amend and ratify) the mission the machinery already enacts ('provide a reusable engineering platform that improves the development of software systems through governed engineering knowledge'). Supporting: ES-005.3's litmus, ES-006.4's harvest, the pre-positioned Platform=Adoption split, blind convergence A-1/A-2. Risk of adopting is low; risk of rejecting is that the vacancy keeps pulling constraints upward into mission-shaped misreadings. Authority: sponsor. Recommendation: ADOPT.

a_rows_sample.anchor: REV 2 — "VACANT" WAS WRONG, AND IT IS THE THIRD TIME I HAVE MADE THIS EXACT ERROR ... ARTIFACT ABSENCE ≠ CONCEPT ABSENCE
a_rows_sample.statement: A recurring error pattern is named: artifact absence != concept absence — looking for a document, not finding one, and declaring the concept missing. Three instances: (1) 'there is no strategic-DDD method' (it existed, unindexed); (2) 'there is no capability pattern' (it existed, FROZEN); (3) 'the Mission layer is vacant' (it exists, implicit, enacted in machinery). Strategic DDD asks why a system exists, not whether a document titled Mission Statement exists — Linux and PostgreSQL have no mission statements and unmistakable missions.

a_rows_sample.anchor: THE OBJECTION IS UPHELD, AND MY ERROR IS MORE SPECIFIC THAN "WRONG FRAMING" ... I mislabelled a CONSTRAINT as a MISSION, then reported a conflict between a constraint and a hypothesis — which are not comparable things
a_rows_sample.statement: A reviewer's objection is upheld with a more specific diagnosis: AIP-14 was mislabelled as a mission, then reported as conflicting with a hypothesis (M-B), which are not comparable categories. The document's own prior text already disproved the label, calling AIP-14 'a cost control, not a boundary' four paragraphs after calling it a mission — both cannot be true.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The answer map — every commissioned question → its existing answer
b_rows_sample.statement: A table maps eleven commissioned questions (mission, vision, domains, bounded contexts, core/supporting/generic, context map, lifecycle, knowledge flow, capability model, runtime boundary, PKS boundary, product boundary) to where each is already answered in the frozen corpus, with a grade (Confirmed/Candidate/Hypothesis/Open Question), whether it was blind-validated, and the gate door it routes to.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Platform Domains — PD-1 Governance (6) · PD-2 Method (4) · PD-3 EKP (6) · PD-5b Records (3); PD-4 blocked by H-CAT-1; PD-5a unexercised; PD-6 Runtime BELOW the bar
b_rows_sample.statement: Platform domains are graded against an ownership-first, >=3-of-9 bar: PD-1 Governance scores 6, PD-2 Method scores 4, PD-3 EKP scores 6, PD-5b Records scores 3; PD-4 is blocked by H-CAT-1; PD-5a is unexercised; PD-6 Runtime falls below the bar and is rejected as a domain.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Core / Supporting / Generic
b_rows_sample.statement: Canon (AIP-14) pins the platform as a Supporting Subdomain (Confirmed); conditionally, 'if the gate opened', Method would be Core, EKP machinery Generic (with a constitution-Supporting split), and Runtime Generic — this inversion is recorded only as Hypothesis.

b_rows_sample.anchor: R-3 | "Knowledge Generation" as a domain ... answered negatively — n=0
b_rows_sample.statement: R-3: 'Knowledge Generation' as a domain is answered negatively (n=0, an observation; the generator slot is a person), but only ever tested against PublicDigit's hand-built PKS.

b_rows_sample.anchor: R-4 | Whether the platform's own frozen BC-1..BC-6 map and PD-1..PD-6 reconcile ... already queued as D-3
b_rows_sample.statement: R-4: whether the platform's own frozen BC-1..BC-6 bounded-context map and PD-1..PD-6 platform-domain map reconcile is already queued as D-3; this commission adds urgency, not novelty.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Evidence Matrix — the seven candidate categories A · Engineering Domains ... CONFIRMED as a KIND
b_rows_sample.statement: Candidate A, Engineering Domains, is confirmed as a kind (HIGH confidence): three independent passes (PD-1/2/3 scoring, the frozen BC-1..BC-6 map, the blind review's 8 contexts) found domain-kind things.

b_rows_sample.anchor: "Domains own Capabilities" | REFUTED | no artifact binds any CAP-n to a PD-n; capabilities are anchored to DP-n
b_rows_sample.statement: The proposed meta-edge 'Domains own Capabilities' is refuted: no artifact binds any CAP-n to a PD-n; capabilities are anchored to DP-n instead. A proposed meta-edge the evidence rejects is treated as the strongest sign the validation exercise is real.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Q5 — elements supporting NO observable decision ... DOMAIN | the frozen Phase-02 BC map existed through the entire discovery programme and was NEVER CONSULTED (occurrence #11). No recorded decision changed because something was classified into PD-1..PD-6
b_rows_sample.statement: DOMAIN is flagged as decision-silent: the frozen Phase-02 BC map existed through the whole discovery programme and was never consulted (occurrence #11 of proposing-before-searching); no recorded decision changed because something was classified into PD-1..PD-6, though domains did organize the discovery work itself (a scaffolding use, not a decision use). Flagged as a candidate for future simplification pressure, not a removal proposal.

b_rows_sample.anchor: U-DM-5 | Whether DOMAIN's decision-silence is permanent (simplify) or dormant (a second product would need domain classification to route adoption)
b_rows_sample.statement: U-DM-5: whether DOMAIN's decision-silence is permanent or dormant, waiting on the second-adopter gate.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 4.3 PD-3 refined — the reviewer's objection, engaged ... The MACHINERY | GENERIC SUBDOMAIN ... The KNOWLEDGE CONSTITUTION | SUPPORTING, candidate
b_rows_sample.statement: Applying Evans' Generic-Subdomain test to PD-3 (the EKP) splits it: the MACHINERY (schema validation, graph generation, portal indexing) could be bought or replaced — GENERIC SUBDOMAIN; the KNOWLEDGE CONSTITUTION (the immutable principles from which schema/lifecycle/tooling/portal derive, single_authoritative, status orthogonal to authority) is not replaceable and encodes what the programme means by governed knowledge — SUPPORTING, candidate. PD-3 remains a candidate until it survives a second product; its individual ownership is recorded as a succession risk, not a boundary argument.

b_rows_sample.anchor: MQ-2..MQ-7 | Who owns KnowledgeOS as a whole? ... Is N-1's breach to be repaired ... Is PD-3's individual ownership intentional ... is the harvest responsibility even required ... Does N-10 still hold ... What would falsify M-A?
b_rows_sample.statement: Six further open questions: MQ-2 who owns KnowledgeOS as a whole, given three authority systems none of which spans them (sponsor+DA+ARB jointly); MQ-3 is N-1's breach to be repaired or is the invariant wrong (ARB); MQ-4 is PD-3's individual ownership intentional/a succession risk (DA); MQ-5 under M-A is the harvest responsibility (R-6) even required, since a reuse loop may be out of mission if the platform serves one product (ARB); MQ-6 does N-10 still hold or has evidence of insufficiency accumulated (ARB); MQ-7 what would falsify M-A, since a mission with no falsifier is not a mission (sponsor).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Three independent proofs that D-1..D-7 do not belong in the existing schemas ... KEY COLLISION — mechanical, not aesthetic
b_rows_sample.statement: Three independent proofs that D-1..D-7 do not belong in knowledge-types.yaml or bounded-contexts.yaml: (1) key collision, mechanical and decisive — bounded-contexts.yaml already contains a 'governance' key (product-side, code_path app/Contexts/Governance), so adding D-1 'Engineering Governance' would collide with an existing key in a lint-enforced enum; (2) vocabulary insufficiency, strong — the domain model's verbs (governs, produces, consumes, validates, derives, depends on, observes) have no expression in the edge vocabulary (depends_on, derived_from, verified_by), which lacks governs/produces/consumes/observes; (3) subject mismatch, strong — every L-A field is a property of a document (knowledge_id, last_review, code_refs), but 'Engineering Method' has no reviewer, next-review date, or code refs, so it cannot carry a knowledge card. Verdict: D-1..D-7 belong to L-B (which does not yet exist); expressing them as data would require a separate vocabulary file with its own enum namespace, an ARB decision.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The chain — tested, not assumed ... DESIGN POLICY (DP-n) ... ADMIT — DISCOVERED. Neither of us named it ... ENGINEERING DOMAIN owns Capability ... REJECT as an owner
b_rows_sample.statement: Testing the reviewer's proposed chain Mission->Strategy->Principles->Capability: ENGINEERING STRATEGY is admitted (12+ charter artifacts); ENGINEERING PRINCIPLE is admitted (six registers with own identifier series: AIP-01..14, AP-1..10, PGP-01..05, MC-01..08, SD-1..7, DR-1..8); DESIGN POLICY (DP-n) is discovered as a new anchor, since the Capability Catalog binds every capability to a DP (CAP-001->DP-1, etc.) and neither the reviewer nor the author had named it; 'Engineering Domain owns Capability' is rejected — no artifact links any CAP-n to a PD-n; the reviewer's concern that capabilities must not float is correct, but the repository already anchors them to DP-n, not to a domain. Chain: MISSION -> STRATEGY -> PRINCIPLE -> DESIGN POLICY -> CAPABILITY -> KNOWLEDGE -> ARTIFACT.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Missing concepts — recorded as hypotheses, not admitted (H-1..H-4)
b_rows_sample.statement: Four candidate concepts recorded as hypotheses, none admitted: H-1 'I-12', a Capability may read across a space boundary but never own what it reads (n=1 capability, needs a second cross-boundary reader); H-2 Engineering Domain as owner of Capabilities (no artifact binds a CAP to a PD; DP-n already fills the slot); H-3 Knowledge Space nesting, does the EKP contain the PKS or sit beside it (containment vs adjacency unevidenced); H-4 whether OPERATIONAL-STATE attaches to the Artifact or the Knowledge it carries (would change I-1's granularity).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Package 5 — D-3 · Amend the frozen Phase-02 map via AIP-13 (blocks the context-map section)
b_rows_sample.statement: Package 5 (D-3): admit or reject the R-63/R-64 work-package/meta-governance boundary as a candidate context; dispose BC-5's dormancy. Recommendation: ADOPT the amendment procedure; within it, DEFER the new context per R-64's own bar and annotate BC-5 as dormant-observed. Authority: ARB.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Package 11 — Authorize the "KnowledgeOS Platform Architecture" workstream (NEW — packaged, deliberately NOT launched)
b_rows_sample.statement: Package 11: whether to open a Phase-II Platform Architecture workstream (platform domains -> services -> responsibilities -> interactions -> capabilities -> execution assets; Core/Supporting/Generic; init->PKS flow). Opposing: (a) this IS Phase-C-class work and the B.5 gate's first door is D-9, which the same review says not to rush; (b) 'services' collides with the adopted N-10/Reference-Architecture stance against orchestrators/state machines unless the N-10 evidence bar clears; (c) launching another platform workstream while D-9 is unresolved is the exact AIP-14 exposure under examination. Risk of adopting now: the platform starts producing platform work 'until it exists for itself', ADR-AIP-02's own named failure mode. Recommendation: DEFER until D-9a/D-9b and the three doors resolve, then adopt as Phase C's operational-architecture view, with 'service' declared as responsibility-grouping unless the N-10 bar is separately cleared. Authority: ARB + sponsor.

b_rows_sample.anchor: THE DOMAIN ROW IS THE DISCOVERY OF THIS SECTION ... DOMAIN is a confirmed archetype with almost no outgoing edges ... ownership work is done by DP-n (governance-natured Knowledge), meaning work is done by Domains
b_rows_sample.statement: DOMAIN is confirmed as an archetype with almost no outgoing edges: it does not own capabilities (refuted), produce, constrain, or generate. What it does is scope meaning — it is the archetype of classification, not of ownership, which is orthodox strategic DDD empirically rediscovered (a subdomain never owns artifacts either; teams and contexts own things). Ownership work is done by DP-n (governance-natured Knowledge); meaning work is done by Domains. The reviewer's hierarchy places Domain as an owner in a stack; the evidence says it is a boundary-drawer standing beside the stack.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The hierarchy hypothesis — TESTED AND REFUTED AS A SINGLE STACK ... one supported edge, one refuted edge, four unevidenced. The single stack does not exist
b_rows_sample.statement: The proposed single stack Purpose->Knowledge->Domain->Capability->Process->Runtime->Artifact is tested edge by edge: Purpose-above-all is supported; Knowledge->Domain has no evidence in either direction; Domain->Capability is already refuted (DP-n owns capabilities, not domains); Capability->Process has no evidence (if anything the arrow points the other way); Process->Runtime is inverted-ish (the runtime hosts the work); Runtime->Artifact holds only as containment of configuration artifacts. Verdict: one supported, one refuted, four unevidenced — the single stack does not exist. Collapsing four distinct orders into one stack is level mixing, a fourth instance of that error class in the corpus.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Objective 1 — Stable strategic domains? NO NEW STABLE STRATEGIC DOMAIN IS EVIDENCED
b_rows_sample.statement: Six candidate domains tested against Round47-OP's admissible-justification list: Bootstrap/Genesis fails (one criterion, n=1, not a domain); Engineering Governance already exists (a Supporting Subdomain); Knowledge Validation is not a domain but a capability family (H-CAT-1 already refused the parent abstraction); Runtime Integration is not a domain but a supporting subsystem+ACL, n=1 runtime; PKS Generation is merely an observation (n=0, never existed); Operational Learning is not a new domain but an existing mechanism governed in six places with 0 traversals. No new stable strategic domain is evidenced.

b_rows_sample.anchor: O-1..O-24 (repository facts — no interpretation)
b_rows_sample.statement: 24 repository observations are recorded, each traced to a source artifact and kept strictly separate from interpretation. Key ones: O-1/O-2/O-3/O-4 (a 'Platform != product' table already classifies KnowledgeOS as potential product, Supporting Subdomain, and states the product binds the platform, never forks it); O-9 (an observed promotion model, itself a candidate for promotion); O-12 (Operational Evidence's owner recorded as 'the producing track; consumed by DA', lifecycle append-only, never edited); O-13 (a standing STOP forbidding a context map until operational evidence and an ARB ruling exist); O-16..O-18 (the Product Discovery Charter's five gated stages, PROPOSED status, one retrospective data point/zero market data points); O-20 (cross-product-research resolves to PENDING, no root); O-21 (CAP-001's Domain/Application/Shared contain zero repository knowledge); O-24 (CAP-001's evidence record holds four rows, zero tool executions, zero decisions changed).
