a_rows_sample.anchor: Two of the three proposed repairs work, and they are the same intervention: stop calling it knowledge. ... it removes the blocker the review named ... Sat should therefore stay [PROP]
a_rows_sample.statement: Verdict: R1 and R2 are the genuine repairs and share one intervention (stop calling attribution knowledge); the experiment removes the factivity-based objection to defining Sat but Sat should remain [PROP] for other, independent reasons (Zero's three-way ambiguity, undefined status order, unproven class exhaustiveness).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Sat(K_t,r) in {top,bot,U} where top=established satisfied; bot=established violated; U=cannot currently be determined. That third value is important. Unknown must not silently become false.
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines the core three-valued satisfaction predicate Sat(K_t,r) and states the guiding principle that Unknown must never silently collapse into False.

a_rows_sample.anchor: R = R_content U R_evidence U R_provenance U R_epistemic U R_consistency U R_governance U R_temporal U R_operational ... Sat(K_t,r) = Sat_c(K_t,r) if r in R_c
a_rows_sample.statement: Partitions the requirement universe into eight classes (content, evidence, provenance, epistemic-status, consistency, governance, temporal, operational) and makes Sat class-indexed rather than one universal predicate.

a_rows_sample.anchor: p notin Content(K_t) does not necessarily mean not-p in Content(K_t). Absence is not negation. ... Evidence existence != evidence sufficiency ... Evidence != Truth.
a_rows_sample.statement: States two foundational non-collapse distinctions for the content and evidence classes: absence is not negation, and evidence existence is not evidence sufficiency, evidence is not truth.

a_rows_sample.anchor: the review says: Strong candidate [DEF] Sat: K x R -> {top,bot,U}. I would change that to: [PROP] Candidate common satisfaction interface ... because our latest simulation has already exposed a fundamental issue: factivity vs Gamma-determinacy.
a_rows_sample.statement: First self-review downgrades Sat from a proposed [DEF] to [PROP], citing the v1.1 factivity/Gamma-determinacy impossibility as the reason it cannot yet be mathematically closed.

a_rows_sample.anchor: We have not yet derived Sat; we have derived the need for a satisfaction mechanism. ... K_t, r, Gamma_t -[evaluation semantics]-> epistemic evaluation -> Delta_t ... investigating whether that evaluation can legitimately be represented by {top,bot,U}.
a_rows_sample.statement: Second self-review (a meta-review of the first) sharpens the distinction further: only the need for a satisfaction mechanism has been derived, not Sat itself; recommends investigating an evaluation-semantics object before assuming the three-valued codomain.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The eight definitions I gave previously are therefore still useful. But I would now label them: Sat_c Formal Candidate Specification v0.1 -- not implementation. ... we absolutely can define all eight Sat_c functions now without implementing them.
a_rows_sample.statement: Establishes the 'define != implement' discipline that governs the rest of the Sat_c research thread: specify the eight class functions as a v0.1 candidate without writing executable code for them.

a_rows_sample.anchor: I would change that to: [PROP] Candidate common satisfaction interface Sat: K x R -> {top,bot,U} ... So we cannot yet say that Sat has been mathematically closed.
a_rows_sample.statement: Downgrades the proposed Sat definition from a strong candidate [DEF] to [PROP] because the factivity-vs-Gamma-determinacy obstruction has not yet been repaired.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 3-valued semantics: candidate and 4-valued semantics: hypothesis/question rather than choosing either now.
a_rows_sample.statement: Declines to choose between three-valued and four-valued (contradiction-inclusive) satisfaction semantics, keeping both explicitly open pending further research.

a_rows_sample.anchor: M-3. value ∘ Eval_c is lossy, concentrated at U. T, F, C, UNDEFINED each receive one distinct evaluation situation; U receives nine, spanning [OPEN], [PROP] and [NEG] statuses.
a_rows_sample.statement: M-3: the value-composed-with-Eval_c projection is lossy and concentrated at U -- T/F/C/UNDEFINED each receive exactly one distinct evaluation situation while U receives nine, spanning [OPEN]/[PROP]/[NEG] statuses, destroying exactly the distinction the theory most needs (epistemic insufficiency vs theory incompleteness vs context absence vs world unobservability).

a_rows_sample.anchor: M-5. Blocked-class contagion. Under Kleene conjunction with five of eight evaluator classes undefined, every composite requirement of arity ≥ 4 is permanently U. ... The residual blockage is attributable to exactly two classes: status (⪰ undefined) and consistency (Contr undefined).
a_rows_sample.statement: M-5: under Kleene conjunction with five of eight Sat_c evaluator classes undefined, every composite requirement of arity>=4 is permanently U; supplying three candidate evaluators halved low-arity contagion but changed nothing at arity>=7; the residual blockage is attributable to exactly two classes, status (>= undefined) and consistency (Contr undefined).

a_rows_sample.anchor: ⪰ (the epistemic-status ordering) and Contr (the contradiction predicate) are the entire residual blockage of Sat. They are not independent ... Four open items are one decision.
a_rows_sample.statement: The status ordering (>=) and the contradiction predicate (Contr) are the entire residual blockage of Sat and are not independent: the only total, three-valued contradiction repair preserving absence!=negation routes Sat_content through Sat_consistency, with Contr carrying the fourth-value question -- so four apparently separate open items reduce to one decision.

a_rows_sample.anchor: N-2 -- define Contr, and the fourth value with it. ... any codomain extension must extend the Zero readings in the same step, or closure silently swallows the new value. Four open items, one decision.
a_rows_sample.statement: N-2: define the contradiction predicate Contr and the fourth truth value together -- this unblocks consistency and content, carries the codomain question, and per D-0 any codomain extension must extend the Zero readings in the same step or closure silently swallows the new value.

a_rows_sample.anchor: N-3 -- define ⪰. With Contr, it is the entire residual contagion. Both are currently used by the specification and defined nowhere.
a_rows_sample.statement: N-3: define the epistemic-status ordering (>=), which together with Contr is the entire residual contagion; both are currently used by the specification but defined nowhere.

a_rows_sample.anchor: any claim that an epistemic cycle is generative, healthy, progressive, spiral-like or improving must specify the ordering or criterion under which successive states are considered better. ... raw hits 2254, excluded as false positives 461, genuine epistemic-progress claims 1793, with an ordering nearby 302 (16.8%), without any ordering 1491 (83.2%).
a_rows_sample.statement: Runs a corpus-wide progress-claim audit under the rule that any generative/healthy/progressive/spiral/improving claim must specify its ordering criterion: of 2254 raw hits, 461 are excluded as false positives, leaving 1793 genuine epistemic-progress claims, of which only 302 (16.8%) have a nearby ordering and 1491 (83.2%) specify none.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Self-correction: my first run reported '84% of 2254'. 461 of those hits were the word 'convergence' in the name of the other research lane (three_model_convergence/), plus process improvement and source convergence -- none of them claims about K_t improving. Corrected before reporting. The headline figure barely moves (84% → 83%); the denominator was wrong by 20%.
a_rows_sample.statement: Explicit self-correction: the first audit run miscounted the denominator by including 461 false-positive hits (a folder name 'three_model_convergence/', process-improvement mentions, source-convergence mentions unrelated to K_t claims), a 20% denominator error corrected before reporting, though the headline percentage barely moved (84%->83%).

a_rows_sample.anchor: 83% of genuine progress claims in the corpus specify no ordering. Since ⪰ is undefined, all 1491 are unfalsifiable as stated -- not wrong, but not checkable either.
a_rows_sample.statement: [EXP]: because the epistemic-status ordering (>=) remains undefined, all 1491 unordered progress claims in the corpus are unfalsifiable as stated -- not wrong, but not checkable.

a_rows_sample.anchor: category check needs a declared lens register [OPEN]. progress audit needs ⪰ [OPEN] -- 83% of claims rest on it. stagnation predicate needs ⪰ (a count will not do) [OPEN]. ⪰ is not one open item among several. It is load-bearing for 1491 existing claims, for the stagnation predicate, and for any future statement that a cycle improves.
a_rows_sample.statement: [INF]: all three checks converge on the same blocker, the undefined epistemic-status ordering (>=): the category check needs a declared lens register, the progress audit needs >= for 83% of its claims, and the stagnation predicate needs >= (a count is insufficient) -- making >= not merely one open item among several but load-bearing for 1491 existing corpus claims plus the stagnation predicate plus any future progress claim.

a_rows_sample.anchor: value ∘ Eval_c maps nine situations to one value, while π_V(B) similarly destroys the distinctions carried by the richer boundary. ... The projection intentionally identifies states that the theory may need to distinguish. That is a much better diagnosis [than 'U is too vague'].
a_rows_sample.statement: Reframes the M-3 finding (value-composed-Eval_c collapsing nine situations to U) as an instance of the general induced-equivalence phenomenon: the projection intentionally identifies states the theory may need to keep distinct, a stronger diagnosis than merely 'U is too vague.'

a_rows_sample.anchor: Sat_c = π_value ∘ Eval_c is perfectly legitimate provided we explicitly accept what it loses. ... lossy projection ≠ bad projection but: lossy projection used beyond its semantic scope = defective model.
a_rows_sample.statement: Reframes Sat_c=pi_value o Eval_c as legitimate provided its information loss is explicit: lossy projection != bad projection, but a lossy projection used beyond its declared semantic scope = a defective model.

b_rows_sample.anchor: > **What evaluation structure is minimally required to preserve the distinctions the KnowledgeOS programme has already declared important?**
b_rows_sample.statement: W-KR-CONTR-2026-09 reframes the Contr question from 'three vs four values' to the deeper question of what evaluation structure is minimally required to preserve the programme's already-declared-important distinctions.

b_rows_sample.anchor: * Candidate A — fourth value: **7/12** * Candidate B — delegation: **7/12** * Candidate C — exclusive construction: **7/12** * Candidate D — structured evaluation: **12/12**
b_rows_sample.statement: Reports the core scoring result: A/B/C each pass only 7/12 required distinctions, failing on the identical seven; D (structured evaluation) passes all 12. The seven common failures collapse the unknown family (Unobservable≡InsufficientEvidence≡Underdetermined≡TheoryIncomplete≡...→U), meaning adding a contradiction value does not address distinctions lying outside the contradiction dimension.

b_rows_sample.anchor:
$$
\chi(G)=3.
$$... **Given this particular required-distinction set and this adequacy criterion, at least three distinguishable flat classes are required.**
b_rows_sample.statement: The experiment turns adequacy into a graph-coloring/injectivity problem over the required-distinction graph, finding chromatic number chi(G)=3; carefully qualified: this does not establish the correct evaluation domain has three values, only that at least three distinguishable flat classes are required given this distinction set and adequacy criterion -- and separately, nine 'no determinate value' conditions cannot be adequately represented by any flat value domain regardless of cardinality, making the obstruction structural rather than cardinal.

States a methodological principle from the chromatic-number finding: colourability only proves pairwise coding capacity under the chosen abstraction, it does not establish that resulting values carry the required semantic or operational meaning -- cardinality sufficiency is not semantic adequacy.

b_rows_sample.anchor:
$$
\min |\text{representation}|=2
$$

with the two minimum representations: $$
\{\text{value},\text{reason}\}
$$

and $$
\{\text{polarity},\text{reason}\}.
$$

And: **reason is indispensable.**
b_rows_sample.statement: The exhaustive minimum-representation search finds min|representation|=2, with two minimum representations {value,reason} and {polarity,reason}, establishing that reason is indispensable -- evaluation outcome is not value alone, EVal=(v,r) is the minimum representation found in the tested search space, kept explicitly [EXP]/[PROP] not a new KnowledgeOS primitive.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Candidate C maps contradiction to `T`. Yet it passes invariants I1–I5. Why? Because those invariants test contradiction against the **unknown family**, rather than against satisfaction itself.
b_rows_sample.statement: Candidate C (exclusive construction) maps Contradiction to T (Satisfied) yet passes invariants I1-I5, because those invariants only test Contr≠Unknown-family, not Contr≠Satisfied -- exposing a genuine coverage gap in the invariant suite itself, not merely a bad candidate; proposes I11: Contr≠Satisfied as a legitimate but not-yet-ratified [PROP] test-protocol addition, explicitly preserving the historical conflict (I1-I5 pass, capability guard fails) rather than retroactively declaring the suite complete.

b_rows_sample.anchor:
### R_A

The first implementation unfairly returned `T` for theory-incomplete/uninterpreted cases... ### E7

The literal `"C"` detector accidentally matched context identifiers such as `C1/C2`.
b_rows_sample.statement: Records two implementation self-corrections during the experiment: R_A, an initial implementation unfairly returned T for theory-incomplete/uninterpreted cases, corrected so all nine no-determinate-value conditions return U; E7, a literal 'C' contradiction detector accidentally matched context identifiers like C1/C2, corrected -- both classified as test-implementation defects, not candidate properties, caught by investigating rather than forcing expected results (E9).

b_rows_sample.anchor: > **The experiment does not support representing contradiction as a distinguished scalar evaluation value. The tested adequacy requirement is satisfied by a structured representation in which at least one reason-like dimension is indispensable. The precise evaluation semantics, including the role of contradiction, remains OPEN.**
b_rows_sample.statement: States the accepted formulation of the current Contr finding: the experiment does not support representing contradiction as a distinguished scalar value; a structured representation with an indispensable reason-like dimension satisfies the tested adequacy requirement; the precise evaluation semantics including contradiction's role remains OPEN -- explicitly weaker and safer than 'structured evaluation is the answer', since D is the surviving candidate, not yet the final theory.

b_rows_sample.statement: Commissions KR-COMP-2026-09 with the primary question of what composition semantics preserves the structured-evaluation result's required distinctions without introducing unsupported ones; specifies ten minimum test dimensions (composition over value, over reason, over (value,reason), M3/M4 isomorphism persistence, contradiction-without-becoming-a-truth-value, whether U stays unitary or becomes reason-parameterized, Zero interaction, contradiction+missing-evaluator, +insufficient-evidence, +theory-incompleteness) and warns against selecting the composition algebra before enumerating candidates and constructing separating witnesses.

b_rows_sample.statement: Restates the biggest theoretical improvement from the experiment as a dependency reframing: RequiredDistinctions -> Representation -> Composition -> Evaluation -> Zero, replacing the earlier naive Contradiction -> FourthValue framing.

Boundary\ dimensionality.

$$
b_rows_sample.statement: States the nine-way collapse (uninterpreted, not-applicable, unobservable, insufficient evidence, underdetermined, theory-incomplete, etc. all collapsing to U) as evidence that Contradiction dimensionality is not the same as Boundary dimensionality -- adding a contradiction value does nothing to solve this collapse, an important result for Zero Lens.

Softens 'reason is the sole indispensable field' (since 'reason' could trivially be defined as Reason(x)=x, a disguised complete state identifier) to the safer claim that within the tested representation language, an explicit reason/boundary component is indispensable -- reframing the next question as what the minimal structured semantics of Reason actually is, more interesting than merely adding a reason field.

b_rows_sample.anchor:
$$

Eval(x)=(Status(x),Reason(x))
}
$$

rather than: $$
Eval(x)=Status(x).
$$
b_rows_sample.statement: Proposes evaluation should be represented as Eval(x)=(Status(x),Reason(x)) rather than Status(x) alone, giving concrete examples (U,Unobservable) vs (U,Underdetermined) sharing top-level status but remaining distinguishable -- distinguishing Flat semantics Eval:X->V from Structured semantics Eval:X->V×R as a new research vocabulary distinction, and noting D is conceptually a product/structured evaluation space E=V×R, not simply a richer many-valued logic.

States a general methodological principle from the Candidate C failure: passing invariants does not imply semantic adequacy -- an invariant suite covering only one axis of separation (contradiction vs unknown) can miss another (contradiction vs satisfied) entirely, motivating I11 (Contr≠Satisfied) as a candidate, not yet canonical, invariant.

| Contradiction   | Unknown              |          YES |...Then the representation is tested against the matrix... $$
\chi(G)

b_rows_sample.statement: Proposes expressing evaluation requirements as an explicit pairwise-must-differ distinction matrix rather than a flat invariant list (making omissions visible, unlike I1, I2, I3...), with the chromatic-number calculation serving as a useful diagnostic on that matrix but not the adequacy criterion itself.

Connects the structured-evaluation result to the future ≡_sem work: two representations with identical final status (both Eval=U) need not be semantically equivalent if their Reason components differ and downstream operations can distinguish them -- Same Status does not imply Semantic Equivalence.

b_rows_sample.statement: Proposes a candidate FR-002 freeze covering thirteen items from W-KR-CONTR-2026-09: tested requirements do not force a fourth flat value [EXP]; A/B/C fail the same seven distinctions [EXP]; the common failure lies in the unknown/boundary family not contradiction [EXP]; D separates all tested distinctions [EXP]; a structured reason/boundary component is indispensable in the tested language [EXP]; candidate C can map contradiction to Satisfied while passing I1-I5 [EXP]; Contr≠Satisfied is a required candidate invariant [PROP]; minimum flat cardinality is requirement-set dependent [EXP]; 'KnowledgeOS requires four-valued logic' is not supported [NEG]; minimal structured evaluation semantics, composition, canonical Contr representation, and Zero semantics all remain [OPEN] -- explicitly withholding freeze of the whole experiment until the 'reason is sole indispensable field' wording is re-checked.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 25N (094210) -- Evidence Aggregation Algebra. FIRST PRINCIPLE (section25N.1): "evidence is not a scalar". SIX SEPARATE CONCEPTS: Support, Reliability, Authority, Probability, Confidence, Independence. ... IMPOSSIBILITY-STYLE RESULT ... Evidence has no intrinsic universal weight
a_rows_sample.statement: Step 25H (092308) formalizes a governed Sarathi decision operator S(K,G,D,M,C) -> DecisionResult in {Decision, HumanDecisionRequired, InsufficientKnowledge, GovernanceBlocked, ModelUnderspecified}, with probability treated as optional (decisions may rest on constraints/dominance alone) and three decision modes (deterministic/model-based/human-escalation). Step 25N (094210) states as a first principle that evidence is not a scalar, decomposing it into six separate concepts (Support, Reliability, Authority, Probability, Confidence, Independence), gives the likelihood-ratio combination law LR(E1..En)=product of LR(Ei) under conditional independence while flagging independence as an assumption never to be auto-applied, distinguishes a Statistical aggregation regime from a Qualitative one that must never be silently mixed, and derives by counter-scenario (high-authority/low-reliability versus low-authority/high-reliability evidence) an impossibility-style result that evidence aggregation is domain/model dependent, boxed as 'Evidence has no intrinsic universal weight' with effect instead modeled as a relation Effect(E,A|C,M).

a_rows_sample.anchor: 25K (093925) -- Knowledge State Algebra and Closure. K = 11 fields ... universal monotonicity FAIL, universal commutativity FAIL, universal associativity FAIL; section25K.49 reframes the three FAILs as "not failures".
a_rows_sample.statement: Step 25K defines an 11-field knowledge state K=(Assertions,Evidence,Provenance,Relations,Assessments,Validity,TemporalState,Conflicts,Versions,Contracts,Policies) with the event log kept conceptually separate, states six invariants (determinism, idempotence, provenance preservation, contradiction preservation, no-hallucinated-resolution, and monotonicity-only-carefully), and an eight-test closure result table that finds universal monotonicity, universal commutativity, and universal associativity all FAIL, immediately reframed as 'not failures' in the next section -- a reframing the trace later flags (as contradiction C-3) because these three negative results are never carried forward into Step 31's audit, Step 48's invariant set, or Step 51's invariant tests, quietly dropping out of the record while downstream summaries report uniform PASS.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Step 26 (101406) ... KEY DERIVATION (section26.5): epistemic Zero arises from observational equivalence -- Zero is given an information-theoretic ground ... section26.7 "identifiability is more important than confidence".
a_rows_sample.statement: Step 26 grounds epistemic Zero in observational equivalence (two world states that produce the same observation are indistinguishable in principle, not merely unmeasured), argues identifiability matters more than confidence, defines observational equivalence, identifiability, model validity region, domain of applicability, an abstraction function with leakage, an observability matrix, and an instrumentation gap; distinguishes safe sensing from world-changing action; and derives six boxed inequalities (Model!=Reality, Observation!=State, Computability!=Justifiability, Confidence!=Identifiability, Correlation!=Causation, and that Unknown does not mean the system should guess), giving the system a way to state 'I cannot know this from the currently available observations' as distinct from ordinary uncertainty.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Step 27 (101458) ... DEF (verbatim, section27.13): uncertainty is a vector U(H)=(U_measurement,U_epistemic,U_aleatoric,U_model,U_semantic,U_identity,U_temporal,U_causal) -- 8 components. ... TUPLE (section27.71): KnowledgeState = (Assertions,Evidence,Uncertainty,TemporalState,SemanticState,Provenance,Models,Rules) -- 8 fields
a_rows_sample.statement: Step 27 defines uncertainty as an 8-component vector U(H)=(measurement, epistemic, aleatoric, model, semantic, identity, temporal, causal), argues probability requires a reference class or model, treats Dempster-Shafer as bounded rather than adopted, and separately states an 8-field KnowledgeState tuple, a 6-field DecisionState, and a 5-field ActionState; replaces a naive 'Confidence: 87%' with a 12-field worked assertion record. States seven boxed non-equivalences including Unknown!=0.5 and EvidenceStrength!=Probability. The trace notes that step 31.24 later silently narrows this 8-component uncertainty vector to a 5-field descriptor under the same notation U(H), an unremarked change (a new contradiction instance).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Step 29 (101614) ... section29.24 the architectural discipline: "do we need an SMT solver everywhere? No" ... section29.31 "constraint confidence is unnecessary" ... section29.67 (the honest gap): "an internally consistent knowledge base can still be completely wrong"
a_rows_sample.statement: Step 29 formalizes satisfiability (SAT(K and C) -> SAT/UNSAT) and satisfiability-modulo-theories for constraints like Version bounds, states the architectural discipline that solvers should be used only where complexity justifies them (not universally), catalogues eight constraint classes (Structural, Temporal, Semantic, Cardinality, Authorization, Safety, Statistical, Causal), argues constraints are typed, not probabilistic ('constraint confidence is unnecessary'), introduces a consistency vector generalizing a single consistency score plus unit/dimensional-analysis consistency (judged genuinely novel in the corpus), and prefers a Generate->Verify->Accept pipeline over Generate->Trust. Ends with an honest, load-bearing admission (section 29.67) that an internally consistent knowledge base can still be completely wrong (InternallyConsistent and ExternallyIncorrect can co-occur), explicitly handed off to step 30.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Step 30 (102009) ... seven drift species -- model, data, concept, label, semantic, governance, reality drift ... section30.46 "drift detection can itself fail" -> section30.47 raised to fundamental epistemic invariant ... False != Unvalidated
a_rows_sample.statement: Step 30 builds a validation hierarchy with Brier score and log loss for calibration, distinguishes calibration from discrimination, catalogues seven distinct drift species (model, data, concept, label, semantic, governance, and reality drift), introduces freshness/epistemic-decay/time-to-obsolescence, validator independence, the principle that validation is itself evidence, that ground truth can be revised, a validation predicate requiring Inconclusive as an essential third outcome (False != Unvalidated), and elevates 'drift detection can itself fail' to a fundamental epistemic invariant; introduces validation debt and knowledge decay as technical debt, and explicitly declines to produce a single reality-alignment score. States five boxed non-equivalences (Consistency!=Correctness, Validation!=Truth, NotValidated!=Invalid, NoDetectedDrift!=NoDrift, single-PredictionError!=ModelFailure).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Step 31 (102251) ... section31.19: if Omega(W1)=Omega(W2) while W1!=W2, then "No algorithm can recover information that the observation function destroys." ... This is not a limitation of AI. It is an information-theoretic limitation. Classification: PROVEN-style
a_rows_sample.statement: Step 31 (76 sections, the largest single formal artifact in the batch) gives 45 one-line definitional sections (typed universe with Observations/Evidence/Assertions/Models/Constraints/Decisions/Actions/Validation/Conflicts as genuinely different types; a 7-field knowledge state K_t=(E_t,A_t,M_t,C_t,F_t,V_t,R_t); a partial transition delta:K x Event -> K; a provenance graph; EpistemicTypeSafety forbidding silent casts like Hypothesis->ValidatedAssertion), then states what the trace judges the strongest formal result in the whole batch: an information-theoretic impossibility result (section 31.19) -- if two distinct world states produce the same observation, no algorithm can recover the information the observation function destroyed, explicitly stated as not an AI limitation but an information-theoretic one -- immediately followed by a formal identifiability definition (31.20) and the derivation that a non-identifiable quantity must be reported as Underdetermined (31.21), both classified PROVEN-style (correct, if elementary, formal arguments) rather than merely asserted.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The 20 counterexamples ... CE11 hidden circularity A->M->V->A ... PASS conceptually. Formal implementation remains to be specified. ... CE20 all constraints satisfied but K not approx W -> InternalConsistency=True and ExternalValidity=False/Unknown -- PASS, annotated "perhaps the most important test".
a_rows_sample.statement: Step 31 runs 20 narrative counterexamples (CE1-CE20) against its own formal apparatus, covering conflicting versions, missing evidence yielding Underdetermined rather than a guess, model disagreement versus contradiction, hallucinated action denial, preserved history for defeated assertions, out-of-domain model applicability, hidden derivation circularity (the only counterexample with a qualified verdict, 'PASS conceptually, formal implementation remains to be specified'), statistical constraint violation, invalid inference from Unknown, provenance integrity, cross-context rule misapplication, semantic type violation, revalidation requirements, calibration failure, and CE20 (internal consistency co-occurring with external invalidity/unknownness, annotated as perhaps the most important test); all 20 pass, all classified CONCEPTUAL_ONLY since none was executed. A twelve-category audit (31.69) then finds most categories PASS or PASS-conceptually, but epistemic type safety only PROMISING, and formal uncertainty propagation, complete proof calculus, and computational complexity all left OPEN.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Step 32 (102341) ... section32.79 new atomic object: EpistemicClaim = (Subject,Predicate,Value,Context,Time,Evidence,Provenance,EpistemicStatus,Uncertainty,Validation,Dependencies) -- 11 fields, and it displaces Fact. ... three failure states False / Unknown / Undefined
a_rows_sample.statement: Step 32 constructs the core epistemic algebra K-fraktur=(K-calligraphic, preceq, compose, oplus, Revision, Validate, Infer, Conflict), sharpens the two-valued False/Unknown into three failure states False/Unknown/Undefined, distinguishes information ordering from truth ordering, states that evidence addition is monotonic under the information order while revision is non-monotonic, separates an accumulating evidence layer from a belief layer that may change interpretation, and introduces an 11-field EpistemicClaim=(Subject,Predicate,Value,Context,Time,Evidence,Provenance,EpistemicStatus,Uncertainty,Validation,Dependencies) that explicitly displaces the earlier concept of Fact as the atomic epistemic object.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Step 34 (102459) ... boxed formula I*=argmax_I[EVSI(I)-Cost(I)] subject to constraints. Classification DERIVED (standard decision-analytic result, correctly stated). This is the sharpest operational formula in the batch.
a_rows_sample.statement: Step 34 formalizes information acquisition using EVPI and EVSI, culminating in the boxed operational formula I* = argmax_I [EVSI(I) - Cost(I)] subject to constraints, selecting the next-best epistemic action; judged the sharpest operational (correctly-stated standard decision-analytic) formula in the batch and classified DERIVED rather than merely asserted.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Step 36 (102624) ... Object level vs meta level ... A knowledge system must be evaluated not only by the correctness of its outputs, but by the calibration of its epistemic processes. ... Step 37 (102747) ... the neutral-source assumption must be removed
a_rows_sample.statement: Step 36 introduces meta-epistemology as a distinct architectural layer, distinguishing calibration from accuracy and from confidence, and states the boxed meta-principle that a knowledge system must be evaluated not only by the correctness of its outputs but by the calibration of its own epistemic processes -- judged genuinely new relative to step 30's object-level calibration. Step 37 introduces the only adversary-with-incentives model in the batch, distinguishing random error, systematic bias, and strategic manipulation, and states that the neutral-source assumption must be removed, making EpistemicIntegrity first-class and extending the uncertainty taxonomy beyond aleatory sources; the largest file in the batch by size.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Step 41 ... formally separating Knowledge from DecisionSufficiency. Step 42 ... moves from "knows enough" to "can formally determine whether a decision is admissible". Step 44 ... boxed: A decision changes the future state space. Step 47 ... self-generated evidence; confirmation loop; policy-induced distribution shift.
a_rows_sample.statement: Step 41 formally separates Knowledge from DecisionSufficiency (necessary vs sufficient conditions for a decision), the precondition that makes step 42's decision-admissibility gate possible ('can formally determine whether a decision is admissible', later becoming invariant I7 Execute(d) implies Admissible(d)). Step 44 gives the only treatment in the batch of loop stability/oscillation, boxed as 'A decision changes the future state space.' Step 47 treats the self-referential learning/safety problem: self-generated evidence, confirmation loops, and policy-induced distribution shift, asking whether the system's own learning process remains trustworthy -- judged, alongside step 37, one of the batch's two genuine safety steps.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Step 48 (104102) ... The 20 global invariants ... The AND formula (section48.32): I={I1,...,I20} and the core correctness requirement for-all s in ReachableStates: AND_{i=1}^{20} I_i(s). ... Anti-inflation guards: section48.33 "20 invariants do not automatically prove correctness" -> Specification != Proof
a_rows_sample.statement: Step 48 states 20 named global invariants I1-I20 (evidence immutability, provenance traceability, no-hindsight temporal integrity, identity consistency, semantic-equivalence representation, temporal-order-does-not-imply-causal-claim, Execute-implies-Admissible, Execute-implies-Authorized, SafetyGate-False-implies-no-Execute, learning preserving historical evidence, decision reconstructability, revision traceability, scope non-generalization, uncertainty preservation, Unknown!=False!=True, AI proposals requiring evaluation before execution, independent validation for critical claims, model-version and policy-version tracking on predictions/decisions, and causal-claim-requires-model-plus-assumptions), formalized as I={I1..I20} with the correctness requirement that all 20 hold over every reachable state; immediately guards against overclaiming with the anti-inflation principle Specification != Proof, listing four unmet proof burdens (completeness, implementation preservation, boundary enforcement, no exceptional bypass) and leaving the completeness question (do desired properties follow from I?) explicitly OPEN, with the inductive base-case and preservation obligations stated but never discharged. States the correctness contract KOSCorrect iff I_global and Contracts and Safety and Liveness and Traceability and EpistemicIntegrity.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Step 49 (104146) ... THE 8-PRIMITIVE REDUCTION ... Entity + State + Event + Observation + Proposition + Relation + Policy + Action ... EXACT CLAIM STRENGTH -- this is the key deliverable. The reduction is ASSERTED, not proven.
a_rows_sample.statement: Step 49 proposes reducing the corpus's many prior concepts to a candidate 8-primitive kernel P = {Entity, State, Event, Observation, Proposition, Relation, Policy, Action}, kernel K=(E,S,T,O,P,R,Pi,A), with everything else expressed as Structure(P) (deriving Evidence as a qualified observation, Claim as Proposition, Provenance/Causality as typed relations, Learning as a knowledge-state transition, Decision as policy-constrained action selection). Critically, the trace precisely characterizes the exact claim strength: this reduction is ASSERTED, not proven -- the source itself hedges with 'many, not all' concepts being reducible and 'I would currently freeze... candidate mathematical kernel', offers no minimality proof (no demonstration that none of the 8 primitives is derivable from the other 7) and no completeness proof (that every KnowledgeOS concept is expressible in Structure(P)), supported only by 12 narrative falsification experiments, and is explicitly intended as a disciplinary governance test for future concepts rather than a theorem.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Step 50 (113416) ... exactly 50 numbered attacks ... Verdicts: 50/50 PASS. Not one unqualified failure. ... section50.56-59 the honest statistics ... FailureToFindCounterexample != ProofOfCorrectness ... declines to attach a number to P(ModelCorrect|Tests) for want of a justified prior
a_rows_sample.statement: Step 50 runs exactly 50 numbered adversarial attacks against a narrated reference state machine, spanning evidence hygiene, causal fallacies (including Simpson's paradox), AI boundary violations, governance, temporal/history, self-deception/feedback, drift, dynamics, computation, liveness, DDD boundary, event/messaging, registry/graph integrity, statistics, and runtime governance/concurrency; all 50 pass, 13 with explicit conditions attached (e.g. 'provided policy precedence is explicitly modeled'). Delivers what the trace calls the batch's best anti-inflation passage: explicitly stating Counterexample(model)=empty-set-within-the-tested-attack-set is not a proof, the scientifically correct statement is 'no counterexample was found in the tested scenarios' not 'none exists', and declining to attach a numeric value to P(ModelCorrect|Tests) for want of a justified prior, judging that qualitative confidence increase is defensible but a number currently is not.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Step 55 ... STEP 55 -- PASS... But unlike earlier steps, we should not yet claim that the reference implementation has passed. Why? Because we have specified it. We have not yet executed it. That distinction is scientifically essential. ... Step 56 ... 62 PASS tokens, zero code fences ... exercised. Nothing was exercised. The Step-55 guard is honoured in section56.43 and violated by section56.42 in the same file.
a_rows_sample.statement: Step 55 (Reference Implementation Specification) states, judged the single most explicit specified-vs-executed guard in the batch: 'we should not yet claim that the reference implementation has passed... we have specified it, we have not yet executed it -- that distinction is scientifically essential.' Step 56, titled 'Build and Execute the KnowledgeOS Reference Machine' and containing zero code fences of any language, then runs 30 narrative experiments, renders them as an all-PASS 30-row matrix (section 56.42), but its own section 56.43 immediately re-states the Step-55 guard, naming three levels (mathematical consistency tested; reference-machine consistency 'specified and exercised'; production correctness not yet demonstrated) -- the trace flags that the word 'exercised' does unlicensed work here since nothing was actually exercised, meaning the Step-55 guard is honoured in one section of Step 56 and effectively violated by an adjacent section of the very same file (registered as contradiction N-3).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Step 57 (113901) ... NEW INVARIANT (section57.61), verbatim: I_Liveness: Every reachable nonterminal workflow state has a governed termination/resolution path. -- this is invariant #21, added after Step 48 froze I at 20 ... Step 58 ... Hazard 1 MutableKnowledgeReference ... Hazard 2 AuthorizationCheck(t1) ... TOCTOU on governance.
a_rows_sample.statement: Step 57 adds a new liveness invariant, I_Liveness ('every reachable nonterminal workflow state has a governed termination/resolution path'), functioning as a 21st global invariant added after step 48 had already frozen the set at exactly 20 -- without renumbering, without amending the AND-formula, and without re-running step 51's invariant test suite, flagged as contradiction N-1 since the step-48 correctness contract already names Liveness separately, giving the system an invariant that is simultaneously inside and outside I_global. Step 58 (Compositional Correctness) is judged the only step in the 52-60 block where the falsification exercise actually changed the design rather than confirming it, discovering two real hazards: Hazard 1, a MutableKnowledgeReference that could cause historical contamination, and Hazard 2, an AuthorizationCheck performed at one time but acted on at a different time -- a time-of-check-to-time-of-use vulnerability on governance decisions.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Step 60 (114040) ... boxed KnowledgeState != BooleanState ... two support dimensions (support-for and support-against, kept separate) ... boxed: "Lattice structure remains an open hypothesis. That is exactly where we should leave it." ... downgrades it from a proposed structure to an open hypothesis.
a_rows_sample.statement: Step 60 argues KnowledgeState is not a Boolean state (requiring at minimum True/False/Unknown/Uncertain/Contradictory), distinguishes ignorance, uncertainty, and contradiction as three separate concepts, keeps support-for and support-against as two separate dimensions rather than one signed scalar, and treats a Bayesian interpretation as optional rather than default. Its key move is a status reversal (flagged as contradiction N-2): step 32 had introduced an information lattice and folded the preceq ordering into its core algebra as an established component, but step 60 explicitly boxes 'Lattice structure remains an open hypothesis. That is exactly where we should leave it,' downgrading step 32's structure without any intervening file recording a retraction -- so the corpus does not say whether step 32 overstated the lattice or step 60 under-credits it.

a_rows_sample.anchor: C-4 (PASS-INFLATION) -- the dominant defect of this batch. Evidence: ~880 PASS tokens, 0 executions, 0 FAILs across 60 steps. ... Mitigating and worth recording: this batch also contains the corpus's strongest anti-inflation language
a_rows_sample.statement: Names PASS-inflation the dominant defect of the entire batch: approximately 880 occurrences of the string PASS, zero executions, and zero FAILs across 60 substantive steps. Identifies four specific mechanisms: titular overclaim (a step titled 'Build and Execute' contains neither); terminology creep (a list of thirteen unproven capabilities labeled 'Proven/computable' in step 25N); qualified PASS silently aggregated as unqualified PASS (13 of step 50's 50 attacks pass only conditionally, yet the aggregate reads Counterexample=empty-set); and conditional PASS treated as a final verdict across six later steps. Notes as a mitigating, worth-recording fact that this same batch also contains the corpus's strongest anti-inflation language (Specification!=Proof, the refusal to numericize P(ModelCorrect|Tests), the step-55 specified-vs-executed guard, step-56's three-level ladder) -- concluding the authors were not unaware of the problem, but that awareness lived in prose while the indexed verdict tokens remained uniformly PASS regardless.

b_rows_sample.statement: Global execution-evidence sweep across all 17 audited files: exactly 62 code fences, all bare/```text, zero language-tagged; zero hits for reproducibility/execution-log keywords; no file contains an executed computation, command output, solver invocation, dataset, or sample size; every one of ~190 'PASS' tokens is an author-written label, not a test result.

b_rows_sample.statement: Step-031 (the corpus's designated formal audit) is found ILL-TYPED at its own type universe (undeclared P, colliding V symbol, untyped sigma, colliding G=(V,E)); its status upgrade to 'Structurally Sound + Mathematically Coherent at the Core' (§31.70) is ruled unearned on four independent grounds (coherence undefined while the proof calculus is OPEN; no new evidence beyond a mostly oracle-gated/circular counterexample set; the upgrade's own §31.75 'no contradiction' line is refuted by two in-file contradictions VC-1/VC-2; and it reverses the commissioning meta-file's calibrated verdict on no new evidence) -- called a relabelling, not a finding.

a_rows_sample.anchor: EL_i=(Step,Artifact,Observation,Fact,Derivation,Decision,Architecture,Invariant,Evidence,Status) ... EL=∪_i EL_i
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines the Evidence Ledger as a per-step 10-field record EL_i=(Step,Artifact,Observation,Fact,Derivation,Decision,Architecture,Invariant,Evidence,Status), with the overall ledger EL as the union across all steps, turning step 213's F/D/P/U discipline into a working data structure.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Observation -> Fact -> Derivation -> Architectural Principle -> Invariant ... Invariant -> Implementation -> Test -> Evidence
a_rows_sample.statement: States the ledger's two-directional fundamental chain (forward: Observation->Fact->Derivation->Architectural Principle->Invariant; feedback: Invariant->Implementation->Test->Evidence->New Knowledge), diagrammed as the architecture's epistemic feedback loop.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Knowledge_t != Knowledge_{t+1} ... The fact that H_2 is better does not mean H_1 never existed
a_rows_sample.statement: States that the ledger must preserve chronology (when a belief was held), not only its content, since a later, better hypothesis H2 does not erase the historical fact that an earlier hypothesis H1 was held -- essential to reconstructing the real engineering journey rather than a retrospectively idealized one.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Calendar chronology ... Engineering chronology ... Epistemic chronology ... The code may exist before the architectural concept has been named
a_rows_sample.statement: Distinguishes three non-identical chronologies (calendar: when it happened; engineering: what was built before what; epistemic: when it was understood), illustrated by Implementation->Observation->Understanding, where code can precede the naming of its own underlying architectural concept.

a_rows_sample.anchor: implementation -> repeated problem -> experiment -> pattern recognized -> concept named ... The later name should not be projected backward as though it had been consciously designed from the beginning
a_rows_sample.statement: Names the 'late naming' phenomenon: a pattern can exist implicitly in the implementation before it is given a formal concept name, and warns against projecting the later name backward as if it had been consciously designed from the start, since that would distort the history.

a_rows_sample.anchor: | Field | Purpose | ... Rejected alternative | What was not chosen |
a_rows_sample.statement: Gives a practical 15-field Evidence Ledger schema (Step ID, Artifact, Date/sequence, Observation, Fact, Interpretation, Derived principle, Decision, Rejected alternative, Architectural consequence, Invariant, Verification, Evidence status F/D/P/U, Confidence, Open question).

a_rows_sample.anchor: What we rejected ... as by: What we selected ... That rejection itself is architectural knowledge
a_rows_sample.statement: Argues architecture is defined as much by what was rejected as by what was selected (e.g. Alternative A rejected because SemanticLoss(A)>0), justifying a dedicated 'Rejected alternative' ledger field as architectural knowledge in its own right.

a_rows_sample.anchor: NegativeKnowledge ... knowledge about approaches, assumptions, transitions or interpretations that have been demonstrated to be unsuitable under specified conditions ... different from failure
a_rows_sample.statement: Introduces NegativeKnowledge as knowledge about approaches/assumptions/transitions/interpretations demonstrated unsuitable under specified conditions, distinguished from mere failure -- a failure becomes useful (negative) knowledge only once its cause ('why it failed') is understood.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Experiment=(Hypothesis,Setup,Observation,Result,Interpretation,Consequence) ... Result -> Knowledge
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines a six-field experimental-lineage record (Hypothesis, Setup, Observation, Result, Interpretation, Consequence) intended to let the eventual book demonstrate the scientific/engineering nature of the work.

a_rows_sample.anchor: A hypothesis says: X may be true ... An invariant says: X must remain true ... Hypothesis -[evidence]-> Pattern -[validation]-> Invariant. Not every hypothesis becomes an invariant
a_rows_sample.statement: Distinguishes hypothesis (X may be true) from invariant (X must remain true) and defines the promotion pipeline Hypothesis->(evidence)->Pattern->(validation)->Invariant, explicitly noting not every hypothesis is promoted.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Observed(H) does not imply Universal(H) ... AllAI -> InconsistentCode [is unwarranted from one tested workflow]
a_rows_sample.statement: States a statistical-discipline guardrail: evidence for H under tested conditions (Observed(H)) must not be generalized to Universal(H), illustrated by a prompt-strategy-specific inconsistency finding that must not be generalized to all AI.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Claim=(Proposition,Context,Conditions) ... Valid(C) should really mean: Valid(C | Context,Conditions)
a_rows_sample.statement: Proposes representing every conclusion as Claim=(Proposition,Context,Conditions) so that validity is always conditioned (Valid(C|Context,Conditions) rather than bare Valid(C)), framed as a connection between DDD and statistical reasoning; extends this to bounded knowledge (Knowledge_A != Knowledge_B across DDD bounded contexts, requiring an explicit ubiquitous-language-guarded translation when a concept crosses a context boundary).

a_rows_sample.anchor: p(C_A) => p'(C_B) ... where p' is the explicitly defined interpretation in the target context. If that implication does not hold, the contract may introduce semantic loss
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines a semantic-preservation condition for cross-context evidence transfer: a property p holding in context C_A after transformation T to C_B must imply the target-context-defined interpretation p' holds in C_B, or the contract introduces semantic loss; states evidence for a claim in one context does not automatically establish it in another without an explicit Mapping and evidence the property survives translation.

a_rows_sample.anchor: ELG=(V,E) ... V=Artifacts∪Facts∪Observations∪Hypotheses∪Decisions∪Principles∪Invariants ... substantially richer than a conventional requirements traceability matrix
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines the Evidence Ledger as a graph ELG=(V,E) with seven node types (artifacts, facts, observations, hypotheses, decisions, principles, invariants) and seven edge types (supports, contradicts, derives, motivates, rejects, implements, verifies), explicitly positioned as richer than a conventional requirements traceability matrix.

a_rows_sample.anchor: C_1 <-[contradicts]-> C_2 ... We should not immediately delete one. Instead record: Contradiction(C_1,C_2) ... Sometimes the contradiction disappears once context is made explicit
a_rows_sample.statement: Treats contradiction as a first-class graph edge to be recorded rather than resolved by deletion; investigating Context(C_1) vs Context(C_2) can dissolve an apparent contradiction, and more generally an apparent contradiction (ModelA accurate vs inaccurate) can resolve into conditional coherence once Context/Population/Time/Purpose dimensions are introduced -- framed as contradiction potentially revealing a missing dimension.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Generation != Adjudication ... Candidates -> Evidence -> Adjudication -> AcceptedKnowledge
a_rows_sample.statement: Applies the contradiction-as-evidence principle to AI-generated competing interpretations: rather than declaring one AI output true and another false, treats {AI_1,AI_2} as an explicit candidate knowledge set requiring adjudication, architecturally separating Generation from Adjudication via Candidates->Evidence->Adjudication->AcceptedKnowledge.

a_rows_sample.anchor: KState in {Observed,Hypothesized,Derived,Corroborated,Contested,Rejected,Accepted,Deprecated} ... should not automatically be treated as a single linear lifecycle ... Accepted + Contested
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines an eight-value knowledge-item epistemic state (Observed/Hypothesized/Derived/Corroborated/Contested/Rejected/Accepted/Deprecated), explicitly not a single linear lifecycle -- states may coexist, e.g. Accepted+Contested when knowledge is operationally accepted but still scientifically disputed; reiterates the anti-Boolean discipline (verified=true is insufficient; use KnowledgeState+Evidence+Context+Time).

a_rows_sample.anchor: UnderlyingPrinciple != CurrentManifestation ... The analogy helps us ask better architecture questions. It does not prove them
a_rows_sample.statement: Applies a Gita chapter-4 analogy (enduring knowledge vs changing manifestation) to DomainInvariant!=CurrentRuntimeState and HistoricalKnowledge!=CurrentRepresentation, explicitly bounding the analogy as interpretive/heuristic ('helps us ask better questions, does not prove them').

a_rows_sample.anchor: S_{t+1} does not contain all information about S_t ... S_{t+1} ⊉ S_t ... CurrentState + HistoricalRecord -> HistoricalUnderstanding
a_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes the 'new state does not know old state' principle as S_{t+1} not-superset-of S_t in general, requiring an additional historical mechanism H_t; concludes CurrentState alone is insufficient and CurrentState+HistoricalRecord is needed for HistoricalUnderstanding, distinguishing CurrentState, HistoricalRecord, and HistoricalInterpretation as three different things.

a_rows_sample.anchor: K_t=(CurrentKnowledge_t,HistoricalKnowledge,Uncertainty_t) ... Update does not necessarily erase prior knowledge ... KnowledgeVersion [distinct from] KnowledgeState ... Git commit != current working tree
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines a knowledge-continuity model K_t=(CurrentKnowledge_t,HistoricalKnowledge,Uncertainty_t) with K_{t+1}=Update(K_t,E_{t+1}), where Update may supersede/qualify/contradict/preserve/deprecate rather than erase prior knowledge; proposes distinguishing KnowledgeVersion from KnowledgeState by analogy to a git commit vs the current working tree, again explicitly flagged as analogy not proof.

a_rows_sample.anchor: ## §3.1 The corpus has NINE registers, not one ... `261.1` is the widest state-level register: six. `012 §36` is the widest *relation* codomain: six. **No corpus artifact reconciles them.**
a_rows_sample.statement: Enumerates nine distinct corpus equality/equivalence registers by locus, date, symbols, and carrier: R1 (25I.11, three assertion-level relations), R2 (25J.5, an implication chain with an open question mark), R3 (25J.26, seven typed assertion edges), R4 (25S.36/43, three identity kinds), R5 (Step 246, four state relations =,≡,≈,≅_λ), R6 (258.1, three relations by carrier), R7 (258.4, four object-level relations), R8 (Step 260, candidate vs proven behavioural equivalence), R9 (261.1, SIX state-level relations =,≡,≈,≅_I,≅_P,≅_H -- the widest state-level register), plus three unnumbered additions (264.15's value-level ≡_D, 195.21/52's Identity/Continuity/Similarity triad, and 012 §36/46's six-member relation codomain, the widest relation codomain). States explicitly that no corpus artifact reconciles these nine registers with each other.

a_rows_sample.anchor: | Verdict | Members | ... 🔴 **INCOMPATIBLE definitions** | **`≡` and `≈` — see §3.3** | ... **NOT an equality at all** | `Similarity` ... `⪯` refinement ... `Validate`
a_rows_sample.statement: Sorts the nine registers' members into six buckets answering the mandate's question (different relations, or overloaded notation?): genuinely-different relations (=, ≡, ≅_I, ≅_P, ≅_H/∼_H, Continuity -- differ by carrier or admitted information); different names for ONE structural relation (≡_struct, =_S, E_struct, and both 246's and 261's '=' -- four names, one relation); relations at different LEVELS (≡_D vs ≡; =_I vs ≅_I; ∼_H vs ≡); INCOMPATIBLE definitions (≡ and ≈, flagged as the critical case); overloaded notation (the ≅ glyph covers four different relations; the ≡ glyph covers six); and constructs that are NOT equalities at all (Similarity is evidence-for, not identity itself; refinement ⪯ is an order; Validate is an assessment relation).

a_rows_sample.anchor: `258.8` | `K_1 ≡_K K_2 ⟺ ∀O ∈ 𝒪: O(K_1)=O(K_2)` ... `261.5` | `K_1 ≈ K_2 ⟺ ∀O ∈ 𝒪_K: O(K_1)=O(K_2)` — **the identical formula** ... $$\boxed{\equiv_K \text{ and } \approx \text{ share one formula while being listed as distinct.}}$$
a_rows_sample.statement: Discovers a critical corpus self-contradiction (later catalogued as gap G-67): loci 261.1 and 246 declare semantic equality (≡) and observational equality (≈) to be distinct and non-interchangeable, yet loci 258.8 and 261.21 define K1≡_K K2 as 'for all O in the observation set, O(K1)=O(K2)' -- and locus 261.5 gives the identical formula, 'for all O in O_K, O(K1)=O(K2),' as the definition of K1≈K2. Conclusion: either ≈ collapses into ≡ (violating the corpus's own non-interchangeability warning) or ≡ has no definition of its own at all, since the observational formula is the only one on offer. Classified NORMATIVE and left unresolved, with no branch preferred.

a_rows_sample.anchor: ## §3.4 The reconciled matrix (mandate §3 columns) ... $$\boxed{\text{ZERO unconditional Level-5 state-level relations...}}$$
a_rows_sample.statement: Produces a full reconciliation matrix across all mandate-required columns (level, corpus definition, source, decision procedure, computability, equivalence properties, congruence, provenance/governance inclusion, identity involvement, dependencies, contradictions, normative decisions) for eight named relations (=, ≡, ≈, ≅_λ/≅_P, ≅_I, ≅_H/∼_H/≡_𝒯, Continuity, ≡_D). Key entries: '=' is computable only relative to canonicalization and is NOT a congruence (executed); '≡' is not fully decidable and has transitivity unestablished; '≈' has no decision procedure since its observation set 𝒪_K is not closed; ≅_I is an equivalence relation only within a context (I_48); ≡_D is the only relation fully specified but sits at the wrong (value) level for K.

a_rows_sample.anchor: `25J.5` writes `E_exact ⇒ E_struct ⇒`**`?`**`E_sem` — the question mark is the corpus's. `261.9`: $\boxed{\text{No universal equality hierarchy has yet been proven}}$ ... `D285-5`'s `history ⊊ structural ⊊ semantic` chain is therefore not merely unmeasured — it is **forbidden**.
a_rows_sample.statement: Establishes that no implication hierarchy among the equality relations is proven or licensed: 25J.5 itself leaves the exact-implies-structural-implies-semantic chain with an open question mark on the second arrow; 261.9 boxes 'no universal equality hierarchy has yet been proven'; and 258.19 explicitly states the relations should NOT be interpreted as a strict mathematical hierarchy but as separate semantic constructs connected by explicit rules. Consequence: D285-5's previously-used chain 'history ⊊ structural ⊊ semantic' is not merely unmeasured but positively forbidden by the corpus's own stated position, with the correction already propagated to D285-5's source and REFINED-STEP-287 §2.

a_rows_sample.anchor: ### 🆕 NEW | **G-67** | 🔴 **`≡` and `≈` share one definition while listed as distinct** ... ① **corpus contradiction — CRITICAL** ... | **G-72** | `G_I` is a separate graph ... but the kernel has one 3-field `ℛ` | ③ architectural
a_rows_sample.statement: Catalogues nine newly-opened gaps: G-67 (critical corpus contradiction -- equiv and approx share one defining formula while listed as distinct); G-68 ('=' and ≡_exact decidable only relative to a canonicalization the corpus forbids fixing a priori); G-69 (Continuity is in no register; identity is orthogonal to lineage); G-70 (four rival decision codomains; the Relation-vs-Status principle unapplied); G-71 (6 of 11 mandate operations have no equality analysis); G-72 (G_I is architecturally a separate graph but the kernel has one three-field R); G-73 (equality's decision-theoretic layer is entirely unparameterized and inherits the no-probability-space gap G-22); G-74 (Closure(Identity)/AffectedKnowledge(x) absent from the operation discussion); G-75 (equiv is a (context,time)-indexed family, treated everywhere as one relation).

a_rows_sample.anchor: | **N-1** | 🔴 **Are `≡` and `≈` one relation or two?** ... the corpus **contradicts itself** ... | 🔴 **OPEN — CRITICAL, newly found** | ARB | ... **20 open normative decisions. N-4 gates N-3, N-5, N-11 and the technical half of N-2.**
a_rows_sample.statement: Catalogues twenty distinct open normative decisions (N-1 through N-20), each with formally consistent options, technical/governance consequences, status, and an assigned authority: N-1 (are equiv and approx one relation or two -- CRITICAL, newly found, ARB); N-2 (Decision 3, Pi in equiv, ARB+PO); N-3 (which 𝒪_K, ARB); N-4 (which 𝒪/𝒯, unenumerable here, ARB -- 'the single upstream gate', blocking everything); N-5 (is approx indexed by axis-subset, policy, or 𝒪, ARB); N-6 (which relevance predicate lambda, ARB); N-7 (is equiv required transitive, ARB); N-8 (define 'identity context', ARB); N-9 (ratify I_48-I_51, ARB); N-10 (decision codomain Relation x Status or a flattening, ARB); N-11 (per-operation equality bindings, blocked by N-4, ARB); N-12 (Deduplicate's criterion, PO+domain); N-13 (which canonicalization, newly raised, ARB); N-14 (id=H(...) with mutable state, governance not engineering, ARB); N-15 (ratify EntityID/KAID/RecordID, ARB); N-16 (is Continuity a kernel relation, newly raised, ARB); N-17 (is G_I a kernel component or part of R, newly raised, ARB); N-18 (Merge commutative/associative, ARB); N-19 (false-merge/false-split loss asymmetry and operating point, also blocked by the no-probability-space gap G-22, PO+domain); N-20 (the '287' identifier collision -- equality-287 vs invariants-287 vs renumber, registry). Notes N-4 as the pivotal blocking decision, gating N-3, N-5, N-11, and the technical half of N-2.

a_rows_sample.anchor: **Step 288 did exactly what it was supposed to do: it did not solve equality; it converted a vague blocker into a much more precise dependency/closure problem.**
a_rows_sample.statement: Reviewer's overall assessment of Step 288: its main conclusion ('equality remains OPEN, precisely bounded', with 2 of 12 closure criteria partial and 10 failing) is judged sound and not a weakness, since it shows the programme has not confused having mathematical candidates with having an implementable equality contract; the finding that Step 261 §261.23 remains active with 0 of 6 conditions resolved is highlighted as extremely important, confirming Step 288 provides evidence for (not supersession of) the Step-261 stop-gate.

a_rows_sample.anchor: This finding deserves particular attention: `258.8/261.21 define ≡_K by the same formula ... list them as distinct` ... **Either ≈ collapses into ≡, or ≡ has no definition at all.** ... The decision: **N-1, adjudicate first, no branch preferred** is therefore very good.
a_rows_sample.statement: Endorses the nine-register conflict (the equiv_K/approx formula collision, G-67) as potentially more important than the equality formulas themselves, listing six sub-questions the programme must resolve before designing any equality algorithm (which registers are authoritative, which are duplicates, which conflict, whether they are genuinely different or merely differently named, whether equiv/equiv_K/approx are meant to be distinct, whether the duplication is historical or normative), and explicitly endorses treating this as decision N-1, to be adjudicated first with no branch preferred, and instructs the next step not to quietly choose an interpretation.

a_rows_sample.anchor: | Reading | Consequence | | **(a)** `≈` collapses into `≡` | register drops to **5**; violates the corpus's own *"not interchangeable"* | | **(b)** `≡` needs a new, non-observational definition | then **`≡` currently has NO definition** | | **(c)** notation clash only; rename one | ⚠️ **cheapest, and it must be *established*, not assumed**
a_rows_sample.statement: Tests three specific readings of the equiv/approx formula-collision conflict: (a) approx collapses into equiv, dropping the register to five relations and violating the corpus's own non-interchangeability declaration; (b) equiv needs an entirely new, non-observational definition, meaning equiv currently has NO definition at all (the observational formula being the only one offered); (c) it is merely a notation clash to be resolved by renaming one relation -- flagged as the cheapest fix but one that must be established from evidence, not assumed, since 261.1 and 261.21 (which state the distinction and the shared definition respectively) sit in one document, making an author-level slip plausible but not demonstrable from the text.

a_rows_sample.anchor: ### Is the duplication **documentary** or **normative**? $$\boxed{\textbf{NOT DETERMINABLE from the corpus.}}$$ `261` states both the distinction (§261.1) and the shared definition (§261.5, §261.21) **without noting any tension** ... **No reading is chosen here.** → **`N-1`**
a_rows_sample.statement: Concludes explicitly that whether the equiv/approx duplication is a documentary artifact or a deliberate normative identification is NOT DETERMINABLE from the corpus text: Step 261 states both the distinction (261.1) and the identical shared definition (261.5/261.21) without noting any internal tension between them, so the text supports neither a 'deliberate identification' nor an 'editorial slip' reading -- this genuine textual underdetermination is precisely why the question needs an assigned decision-owner rather than an inferred resolution, formally routed to decision N-1 with no reading chosen here.

a_rows_sample.anchor: ## Which registers are authoritative? $$\boxed{\textbf{NONE. No register carries a ratification record.}}$$ ... **`261.1` is the widest and latest, which is not the same as authoritative** — and treating recency as authority would be exactly the promotion this programme forbids.
a_rows_sample.statement: Determines that none of the nine equality registers carries any ratification record -- all nine are research-lane and self-verdicted, with R4 (25S.36/43) explicitly marking itself 'provisional'. Explicitly warns that Step 261's register (261.1), while the widest (six relations) and the most recent (2026-08-30), is not thereby authoritative, and that treating recency or breadth as a proxy for authority would itself constitute exactly the kind of unwarranted promotion this whole research programme is designed to forbid; register ownership/authority is itself recorded as an open governance item.

a_rows_sample.anchor: | **N-1** | Are `≡` and `≈` one relation or two? | ... **The text supports no reading over another.** Choosing one would *repair the corpus by inference* — which §14 and Step 288's mandate both forbid | **corpus owner / ARB** ... | **N-21** | The `287` identifier collision | equality-`287` · invariants-`287` · renumber | two artifacts share a number | ...
a_rows_sample.statement: Presents the full 21-entry normative decision register (N-1 through N-21), matching Step 288's N-1..N-20 in substance but adding N-21 (the Step-287 identifier collision between the equality track and the invariants track) and sharpening several justifications, notably N-1's 'why research cannot decide it': choosing a reading of the equiv/approx conflict would mean repairing the corpus by inference, which the governing mandate's section 14 explicitly forbids. Each record carries decision question, alternatives, consequences, evidence available, evidence unavailable, why research cannot decide it, and an assigned authority (predominantly ARB, with PO+domain for N-12/N-19 and 'registry' for N-21).

a_rows_sample.anchor: ## ⭐ Step 261 carries ONE register in TWO notations $$\mathfrak K = (K,\ =_{str},\ \equiv_{sem},\ \approx_{obs},\ SameId,\ \equiv_H,\ \equiv_P) \qquad (\texttt{261.25})$$ **Six-for-six against `261.1`.** ... **Notation drift inside one document — not a second register.**
a_rows_sample.statement: Discovers that Step 261 itself carries one six-relation register under two distinct notations: 261.1's named relations (=, equiv, approx, cong_I, cong_P, cong_H) map six-for-six onto 261.25's tuple form K=(K, =_str, equiv_sem, approx_obs, SameId, equiv_H, equiv_P) (cong_I<->SameId, cong_P<->equiv_P, cong_H<->equiv_H). This is characterized as notation drift within one document, not a second independent register -- the nine-register count from Step 288 stands unchanged -- but the drift means the equiv glyph is reused in the second notation for both semantic equality and (via equiv_H, equiv_P) historical and provenance relations that the first notation gives distinct symbols (cong_H, cong_P); a reader tracking the glyph rather than the section would see equiv apparently doing four jobs, a plausible contributing cause of the confusion the whole equiv/approx investigation exists to resolve.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 1. ⭐⭐⭐ G-67 is a homonym, and the InvariantReg reading is misclassified ... two lanes assigned the same gap ID to two different objects ... The InvariantReg premise does not survive ... ℐ is enumerated three times, in three incompatible ways, by three lanes that do not cite each other
a_rows_sample.statement: Finds G-67 is a homonym used by two unrelated corpus lanes: in phase_measure_theory/knowledgeos_kernel/ steps 288-291, G-67 means the equiv_K/approx formula-collision, WITHDRAWN by Step 290 and replaced by N-1'; in readiness/07, a Gita document, and a forward plan, G-67 means 'InvariantReg (I), the mandatory invariant register, never enumerated' -- described in the investigator's own forward plan as 'the single most evidenced blocker in the estate.' Finds the InvariantReg reading does NOT survive: I is independently enumerated three times, in three mutually incompatible shapes, by three lanes that never cite each other: (1) Step 048 SS48.60's InvariantRegistry, a 10-field schema with 0 rows populated (2026-08-28); (2) Step 120's K1-K7, seven named invariants (Provenance, Authority, Epistemic status, Temporal validity, Deterministic verification, Traceability, Feedback) each with an experiment and verdict, plus a systematic absorption/necessity argument (2026-08-28T12:45:10); (3) Theory v1.0 SS75's I1-I9, nine boxed invariants explicitly titled 'Kernel invariants' and closing with 'these are now the beginning of the KnowledgeOS Constitution' (2026-09-02T00:46:31). Verifies enumeration 3 sits inside one unbroken internal section run (SS70 Kernel -> SS71 Kernel shape -> SS74 Invariant custody -> SS75 Kernel invariants I1-I9) requiring no inference to bridge.

b_rows_sample.anchor: after Repair B: system state = (K,\ Q_t,\ H) \qquad\text{not}\qquad K ... the sufficiency question re-opens **one level up**
b_rows_sample.statement: Mathematician's-lens argument that Repair B, though invariant-preserving over K, silently changes what 'the state' means to (K,Q_t,H); K alone can no longer distinguish M1 from M2, so the sufficiency question reopens one level up: is (K,Q_t) sufficient and minimal? Names G-56 (Sufficient(K,O,I)) as exactly the needed instrument, noting it remains unadopted as of this document.

b_rows_sample.anchor:
def expressive(F, predicates, space=SPACE):
    """Expressive(F, I): no two F-identified states disagree on any predicate."""
b_rows_sample.statement: Ground-truth executable definition of Expressive(F,I): for a given finite enumerated space of states, bucket states by their F-image, then check that no two states sharing an F-image disagree on any predicate in I; returns (bool, list of witnessing disagreements). This is the operational form of the Expressive conjunct used throughout the Sufficient(F,O,I) adoption argument.

b_rows_sample.anchor: \mathrm{Sufficient}(F,\mathcal O,\mathcal I)\;&:\Longleftrightarrow\; \mathrm{Congruent}(F,\mathcal O)\ \wedge\ \mathrm{Expressive}(F,\mathcal I)
b_rows_sample.statement: Formal definition proposed for adoption: for a state abstraction F with s1~F s2 iff F(s1)=F(s2), Congruent(F,O) requires every state-transforming operation in O to respect F-indistinguishability, Expressive(F,I) requires every mandated predicate/invariant in I to respect F-indistinguishability (i.e. Expressive is Congruence for the 0-ary/predicate case), and Sufficient(F,O,I) is their conjunction. Closes G-56 (previously open since the second-order pass, at 0 adoption).

type_signature.domain: state abstraction F, operation set O, predicate set I

b_rows_sample.anchor: Congruent ∧ ¬Expressive | `F₄ = K=(𝒜,ℛ)` ... Expressive ∧ ¬Congruent | `F₂ = content+status`
b_rows_sample.statement: Executed independence proof that Congruent and Expressive are neither redundant: witness (a) F4=K=(A,R) is Congruent=True but Expressive(I_merge_prov)=False against the section-265.11 merge-provenance invariant; witness (b) F2=content+status is Congruent=False (fails on Remove/Revise/Transform) but Expressive(I_any_accepted)=True. Both directions realized, so the conjunction Sufficient=Congruent AND Expressive is a proper (non-redundant) conjunction.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Sufficient(K,\mathcal O,\mathcal I)\ \text{FAILS on the EXPRESSIBILITY conjunct the moment } \textit{“was }p\textit{ asked?”}\ \in \mathcal I
b_rows_sample.statement: The decisive adoption argument: modeling the Step 280 defect (proposition p, inquiry recorded or not) shows K alone is CONGRUENT (the only operations are Assert and Ask; Ask changes only the inquiry register, which K does not project, so K-indistinguishability is preserved by every K-transformation) but NOT EXPRESSIVE the moment 'was p asked?' is admitted as a mandated predicate -- so Sufficient(K,O,I) would have located the exact Step 280 defect, and named the repair site (the smallest carrier making I_was_asked expressible), BEFORE the empirical test ran, i.e. a priori rather than by post-failure comparison.

b_rows_sample.anchor: `ℐ` now carries the weight `𝒪` used to. ... **There is no invariant register.**
b_rows_sample.statement: Adoption obligation stated: while the mandatory-operation set O is usable now (15 named, 5-class partition, 14-element lower bound forced, 4 operations' mandatory status open as D-1), the invariant/predicate set I has NEVER been enumerated -- opened as new gap G-67, a class-(1) actual theoretical hole inheriting the load-bearing role O held before Step 272A; recommends I become a maintained register with the same citation discipline O received, seeded with the seven known members (one of which, section 265.11's merge-provenance invariant, is currently inexpressible in K=(A,R)).

b_rows_sample.anchor: `Sufficient` is *demonstrated* on a bounded model and *derived* from the corpus's own two criteria. It is **`DERIVED`, not proven**, and it should not be described as a theorem until `ℐ` is closed.
b_rows_sample.statement: Explicit epistemic-status caveat on the adoption document's own claim: Sufficient(F,O,I) is demonstrated on a bounded 3-state model and derived from two pre-existing corpus criteria (congruence, and the corpus's own restriction noted at 259.8), not proven as a general theorem, and must not be described as a theorem until the invariant set I is fully enumerated (G-67).

a_rows_sample.anchor: ValidTime ... TransactionTime ... KnowledgeTime ... not necessarily identical

a_rows_sample.statement: Extends bitemporal data with a third dimension, EpistemicStateTime, needed because an assertion can exist before being accepted as knowledge, worked with an observation-arrives/evidence-assessed/assertion-accepted timeline.

a_rows_sample.anchor: WorldState(t) ... KnowledgeState(t) ... these can produce different answers
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines two distinct query types, WorldState(t) and KnowledgeState(t), which can produce different answers.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Why did the system approve this change on 10 August? ... KnowledgeState(10Aug), not today's knowledge ... HistoricalDecision must use HistoricalKnowledge
a_rows_sample.statement: States HistoricalDecision must use HistoricalKnowledge (KnowledgeState at the historical time), not today's corrected knowledge — crucial for auditability.
