a_rows_sample.statement: Defines epistemic versioning K1->K2, requiring the system to answer queries at either historical point.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Snapshot(t) ... the complete set of epistemically valid knowledge available under a specified temporal and contextual boundary ... more precise than database state at time t
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines Snapshot(t) as the complete epistemically valid knowledge under a specified temporal/contextual boundary, more precise than 'database state at time t.'

a_rows_sample.anchor: S=(t,Context,IdentityVersion,SemanticVersion,RuleVersion,ModelVersion,PolicyVersion) ... UpgradeAllowed is not meaningful without knowing which versions were used ... Conclusion=f(Knowledge,Context,Semantics,Rules,Models,Policies)
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines a seven-field multidimensional Snapshot, worked with a fully-versioned UpgradeAllowed example, giving Conclusion=f(Knowledge,Context,Semantics,Rules,Models,Policies) at a defined temporal point.

a_rows_sample.anchor: VersionAlignment ... Evidence_{2026} cannot necessarily be evaluated under Rule_{2024} ... Meaning_{v2} should not be silently interpreted using Meaning_{v1}
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines VersionAlignment: all derivation components must be temporally compatible, worked with cross-year evidence/rule and cross-version meaning mismatches.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Valid(D)\Rightarrow Compatible(Evidence,Rules,Semantics,Models,Identity,Context) ... a powerful invariant
a_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes the temporal consistency condition: a derivation is valid only if all its dependencies are temporally compatible.

a_rows_sample.anchor: January decision under Rule_{v1} ... rule changed in June ... evaluating using Rule_{v2} we might conclude the January decision was invalid. But perhaps it was perfectly valid ... CurrentRule\neq HistoricalRule
a_rows_sample.statement: Worked temporal-paradox example: judging a historical decision by a later rule version can wrongly invalidate a decision that was correct under the rule in force at the time — CurrentRule ≠ HistoricalRule.

a_rows_sample.anchor: ObservationRecorded, EvidenceAssessed, AssertionAccepted, RuleActivated, RuleRetired, ModelPublished, ModelRevised, DecisionMade, DecisionAuthorized, ActionExecuted, ObservationCorrected ... State_t=Fold(Events_{\le t})
a_rows_sample.statement: Lists an eleven-event vocabulary and restates State_t=Fold(Events_<=t) as 'mathematically elegant' event-sourced state derivation.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Events tell us what the system recorded. They do not automatically tell us what was true ... EventHistory\neq WorldHistory ... explicit valid-time semantics where appropriate
a_rows_sample.statement: States event sourcing alone is insufficient: events record what the system recorded, not necessarily what was true in the world — EventHistory ≠ WorldHistory, requiring explicit valid-time semantics.

a_rows_sample.anchor: E_1:t=10:00 arrives after E_2:t=10:05 ... Arrival order E_2,E_1. World order E_1,E_2 ... ArrivalOrder\neq EventOrder. This matters enormously in distributed systems
a_rows_sample.statement: Worked out-of-order-arrival example giving ArrivalOrder ≠ EventOrder, foreshadowing distributed-systems relevance.

a_rows_sample.anchor: LateEvidence ... deployment at 10:00 received at 12:00 ... attach to ValidTime=10:00 while preserving RecordedTime=12:00
a_rows_sample.statement: Requires late-arriving evidence to attach to its correct ValidTime while preserving its separate, later RecordedTime.

a_rows_sample.anchor: t\in[10:00,10:15] ... should preserve an interval. Not t=10:07 simply because that is convenient ... TemporalPrecision must not exceed EvidencePrecision
a_rows_sample.statement: States the invariant that temporal precision must not exceed evidence precision — an uncertain interval must be preserved, not collapsed to a convenient point.

b_rows_sample.statement: Refines the assertion structure to A=(P,E,Σ,Π,T_v,T_o,T_k,Context,ID), noting decision time belongs to a separate Decision event, not the assertion.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Event time ... Nexus was upgraded ... e=Upgrade(Nexus,3.69,3.70) ... occurrence time T_e(e). The resulting state Version(Nexus)=3.70 has a validity interval. Event\neq State. ... State transition ... X_{t+1} = \delta_X(X_t,e_t). This is different from the Knowledge State K_{t+1}=\delta_K(K_t,o_t). W
b_rows_sample.statement: Distinguishes an Event (with occurrence time T_e) from the resulting State (with a validity interval) — Event ≠ State — and defines a domain-state transition X_{t+1}=δ_X(X_t,e_t) distinct from the Knowledge State transition K_{t+1}=δ_K(K_t,o_t).

b_rows_sample.anchor: World state versus Knowledge State ... World/domain state X_t represents the state of the domain/reality being modeled. Knowledge state K_t represents what KnowledgeOS knows/believes/accepts about that domain. X_t\neq K_t. KnowledgeOS can be wrong about the world.
b_rows_sample.statement: States the central Step 16 result X_t ≠ K_t: the world/domain state and KnowledgeOS's knowledge of it are distinct, so KnowledgeOS can be wrong about the world.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The epistemic gap ... X_t: Version(Nexus)=3.72 but K_t: Version(Nexus)=3.69. K_t\neq X_t. KnowledgeOS may not know the discrepancy exists. A knowledge system cannot detect an unknown discrepancy without some new evidence or observation. That should be explicitly accepted in our theory.
b_rows_sample.statement: States a fundamental limitation: a knowledge system cannot detect an unknown discrepancy without new evidence, illustrated by a world/knowledge version mismatch KnowledgeOS is unaware of.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Event sourcing perspective ... NexusProvisioned, NexusConfigured, NexusUpgraded, FirewallChanged, CertificateRenewed, BackupTested ... X_t=Fold(X_0,e_1,\ldots,e_n). b_rows_sample.anchor: Two histories ... H_X = domain/world event history and H_K = KnowledgeOS epistemic history. They are related but not identical. b_rows_sample.statement: Distinguishes domain history H_X from knowledge history H_K (an event enters H_X before knowledge of it enters H_K), allowing EventOccurred to be represented without KnowledgeOfEvent — reality does not wait for observation.

b_rows_sample.statement: States Event ≠ Snapshot (both must be preserved), defines an Event structure e=(EventID,Type,AggregateID,Payload,Actor,OccurredAt,RecordedAt,Provenance,CorrelationID), and reaffirms OccurredAt ≠ RecordedAt with a firewall-change example.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Retraction ... Retract(A) creates a new epistemic event. The historical fact that KnowledgeOS once held A remains. This is essential for auditability. ... Revision ... Supersedes(A_2,A_1). The old assertion remains historically visible. Revision preserves history.
b_rows_sample.statement: Reaffirms Retract(A) creates a new event without erasing the historical fact of holding A, and Revision via Supersedes(A2,A1) preserves the superseded assertion's historical visibility.
